source_fields.faq: How is component aggregation used as a design methodology in parametric architecture? :: Component aggregation is a bottom-up design strategy where a single geometric unit, defined by specific spatial and dimensional parameters, is studied, varied, and then assembled into increasingly complex configurations. The relationship between components, including how they connect, overlap, pack, and grow, becomes the formal and organizational logic of the design. In parametric practice, this is developed in Grasshopper through controlled growth systems that define how components relate to each other structurally and spatially, allowing designers to scale from a single unit to an urban-scale cluster with consistent internal logic. || What does the Hyper Patterns studio at PAACADEMY cover? :: The studio follows four interconnected phases. Component Study involves selecting pre-rationalized components, manipulating geometric parameters through experiments, and documenting findings in a matrix-based catalog. The Growth System phase examines relationships between components within a controlled aggregation system, investigating compact and efficient assembly strategies. Participants then develop a pattern cluster language addressing formal and organizational possibilities across scales, ultimately applying the methodology to tower typology research as the final project. Work is conducted in groups using Grasshopper, Rhinoceros, Adobe Illustrator, and InDesign for modeling, documentation, and presentation. || What background do I need to participate in the Hyper Patterns studio? :: The studio is research and design-intensive and is suited to participants with prior experience in parametric design and a working knowledge of Grasshopper and Rhinoceros. The methodology involves advanced geometric logic, component rationalization, and multi-scenario design development, so participants should be comfortable with computational design workflows. The studio is led at a level consistent with Arian Hakimi's work at ZHA and IaaC, and is oriented toward designers seeking to move beyond individual form-making toward systemic, data-driven design thinking. || What will I produce through the Hyper Patterns studio? :: Working in groups, participants will produce a series of matrix-based digital catalogs documenting component studies and geometric variations, a developed pattern cluster system with growth logic built in Grasshopper and Rhinoceros, and a final tower typology research project applying the aggregation methodology to a multi-scenario hyper-building cluster. The work is presented and documented using Adobe Illustrator and InDesign as part of the studio's design production requirements.

source_fields.introduction: A new design revolution is here! The advent of AI (Artificial intelligence) technology and tools like Midjourney and DALL-E 2 is finally maturing out of infancy and into the field of art, architecture, and design. Creators from every industry across the globe are scrambling to learn and harness this new technology to inform design decisions. AI (Artificial intelligence) image-prompting is said to be an art form, one that is easy to learn and hard to master. Learn to work through the chaos of the image outputs, find patterns between language and image, and control the iterative process towards intentional and feasible results. This interactive course uses discord chat and polls to streamline each participant’s involvement.

source_fields.name: AI Conceptual Architecture
source_fields.introduction: Artificial intelligence is not a novel thing in our lives; its existence has surrounded us for a while. And now that it’s knocking on the doors of the creative process, it’s of the utmost importance to understand the true powers (and limitations) of these tools as soon they will become to shape our careers as architects and designers. And while the current diffusion models cannot break the wall of physical reality just yet, It is surely shaking the grounds below everything we know about creativity and inspiration.
source_fields.description: The AI Conceptual Architecture will cover the basics of prompt techniques in Midjourney and Dalle-2, and explore architecture concepts.
source_fields.objectives: Understand the fundamentals of prompt crafting techniques in Midjourney and DALL·E 2. Explore and create conceptual works using architectural elements through AI tools. Differentiate between various AI models and their applications in architectural design. Gain insights into the creative potential and limitations of AI in architecture. Participate in discussions to refine and develop selected works for further exploration.
source_fields.methodology: In “AI Conceptual Architecture,” participants can expect to learn the basics of working with different Ai text-to-image tools in creating conceptual works using architectural elements with an emphasis on Midjourney and briefly touching on other platforms like Dall-E2 and DreamStudioAI. Participants are expected to learn the basic prompt crafting techniques in different models of Midjourney and understand the differences between each one through exploring various concepts about architectural elements. To conclude the workshop, a few participants’ works will be selected for further discussion/development.
source_fields.notes: No previous knowledge of any software is required. You will learn everything in the workshop.

courses.name: Architectural Follies

source_fields.name: Architectural Follies
source_fields.introduction: In this course of Architectural Follies, you will be designing a pavilion using the various computational design methods, morphological and geometrical strengthening techniques addressing building systems. The purpose of this assignment is to introduce you to alternative ways in which the articulation of digital geometry, digital materiality, and human activities define a relationship between site, space, and program. This necessitates a logic between morphological, geometric, and material characteristics of the structure, program, and environmental performance. The notion of performance will be understood as the integrated task of producing form and structure. This class intends to engage design strategies that would allow for the further manipulation of the building enclosure by assuming a thickened poche, one that will add a solid sense to the building mass. As a way of moving away from thin, continuous surfaces, we will investigate techniques that deal with structure, mass, volume, material, color, and animation.
source_fields.description: Architectural Follies is a parametric design studio course on PAACADEMY that teaches computational design and 3D modeling through the creation of an architectural pavilion. Using Autodesk Maya and Grasshopper 3D, participants explore digital geometry, materiality, color, and tectonic form through a blend of software tutorials and architectural theory. The studio investigates follies as a design typology and challenges participants to develop a pavilion that operates between decoration, structure, and spatial experience.
source_fields.objectives: Design pavilions using computational methods and geometrical techniques. Explore the relationship between digital geometry, materiality, and human activities. Investigate the concept of "follies" in architectural design. Develop advanced skills in Autodesk Maya and Grasshopper 3D. Understand the cultural and historical context of architectural forms.
source_fields.methodology: What is folly: The folly is an architectural form that grew out of well-manicured landscapes in 18th-century Europe. Typically, follies were created primarily as forms of decoration, and often served no functional purpose. A lot of their designs were purely sculptural, or even out of place within their context; their scale and proportions were arbitrary. Yet despite classicizing and orientalizing themes, despite attempts to make these structures appear to be from “other” places or “other” realities, traditional vegetated follies were symptomatic of the time and place in which they were made. Many of these structures evoked architecture of the past, while many suggested could suggest timeless origins. Some could also be designed to appear as though miraculously preserved, others were built as ruins. Ironically, these idiosyncratic structures have become referents for contemporary follies. Yet the role of follies has transformed along with the philosophies held by those who create them. In this Design Studio, we will create a project taking on different approaches towards this folly legacy, with varying degrees of loyalty towards tradition. All will take inspiration from individual aesthetics within a garden or urban landscape, yet some projects may deny the possibility of a structure with purely a decorative role. Collectively, they will embrace the ability of architecture to create, so the discussions of beauty, grotesque, whimsy, and parametric can be placed in a contemporary architectural setting. This class will be organized into two combined parts: tutorials and theory lectures. By mixing the highly specific realm of software tutorials and the more expansive cultural framework, students will be asked to articulate their design processes in both manners, by achieving high expertise in the tools and by understanding the role of those tools within the culture of architecture at large. In current times it is expected that contemporary architects have the highest degree of expertise in a large array of tools and technologies, there is no doubt that technology has revolutionized the way we design nowadays, but at the same time, students must engage both technology and theory in a way that coherent thinking goes through all design processes, instead of merely relying on rule-based systems that only follow steps instead of ideas. Objective 1: To investigate novel forms of tectonics by means of 3D computational design modeling. Objective 2: To expand on the notion of color beyond the metaphoric or banal. Objective 3: To develop advanced technical skills within contemporary software (Autodesk MAYA & RHINO). Objective 4: To understand the genealogy of an architectural problem.
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced architectural design software, enabling you to create captivating materials and efficiently render projects. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What is Autodesk Maya used for in architectural design? :: In architectural design, Autodesk Maya is primarily used for complex 3D modeling, surface manipulation, and animation of geometric forms that are difficult to produce in traditional BIM or CAD environments. Its NURBS and polygon modeling tools allow designers to work with highly articulated surfaces, control mass and volume, and explore color and material in ways that go beyond the limitations of standard architectural software. Maya is also used in conjunction with Grasshopper via data exchange or scripting to drive parametric logic through visual forms, making it a tool of choice for experimental and computational design studios. || What does the Architectural Follies course at PAACADEMY cover? :: The course is structured in two combined parts: software tutorials and theory lectures. On the theory side, participants explore the genealogy of follies from their origins in 18th-century European landscapes through their role in contemporary architectural thinking, examining notions of beauty, grotesque, whimsy, and parametric form. On the technical side, participants develop advanced skills in Autodesk Maya and Grasshopper 3D to design a pavilion using computational modeling, morphological techniques, and geometrical strengthening. The design addresses building systems, tectonic logic, digital materiality, thickened poche, structure, mass, volume, color, and animation. || Do I need prior experience in Maya or Grasshopper to take this course? :: The course is designed to develop advanced technical skills, which implies a working baseline in both Autodesk Maya and Grasshopper 3D. Participants who are entirely new to either tool would find the pace demanding, as the tutorials move into complex modeling and design development without covering introductory fundamentals. Some familiarity with 3D modeling and computational design workflows is strongly recommended. The course also asks participants to engage with architectural theory alongside the technical content, so comfort with design thinking and discourse is equally important. || What will I produce by the end of the Architectural Follies course? :: Participants will design a pavilion that responds to a specific site, program, and environmental logic through computational design methods. The project will demonstrate a coherent relationship between morphological form, geometric structure, digital materiality, and human activity. Technically, participants will develop advanced skills in Autodesk Maya and Grasshopper 3D and learn to articulate design processes across both software and theory. Beyond the project itself, participants will gain an understanding of how to move from idea to fabricable design using contemporary architectural tools, with the workflow itself designed as carefully as the object it produces.

source_fields.name: Midjourney Architecture 3.0
source_fields.introduction: Artificial intelligence is now making a huge impact in the field of architecture. Tools like Midjourney, Dalle2, are reshaping the way we approach design. As this tool is constantly improving, early adopters have developed their own techniques to control the A.I. and refine results. In this studio, Tim Fu of Zaha Hadid Architects will guide participants through developing holistic architectural concepts, focusing on techniques, artistry, and how to prepare for the coming A.I. advancements.
source_fields.description: In Midjourney Architecture 3.0, students will learn some of the secrets of prompt-crafting and the ability to control diffusion-model in A.I
source_fields.objectives: Master prompt-crafting techniques to control AI diffusion models in Midjourney. Develop holistic architectural concepts and refine design outputs. Undertake commissioned projects using AI to meet specific design demands. Enhance images through artistic curation and post-processing techniques. Collaborate and share insights with a community of participants to enrich your learning experience.
source_fields.methodology: The new and upgraded studio 3.0 is here! This course will now cover both architecture and interior design. Students will learn some of the secrets of prompt crafting (the ability to control diffusion-model AI) to produce industry-quality outputs. The course is now optimized for 100 participants, where each individual will be able to contribute to the collective knowledge of this community. We will discuss, evaluate, and inspire each other’s work.

courses.name: Computational Kinematics

source_fields.name: Computational Kinematics
source_fields.introduction: The workshop focuses on generative algorithms in Grasshopper3D and their applications in designing deployable and transformable structures. Using Kangaroo3D and Karamba3D plugins, we will simulate and analyze the kinetic behavior of these structures.
source_fields.description: The workshop covers generative algorithms in Grasshopper3D and their applications in designing deployable and transformable structures.
source_fields.objectives: Utilize generative algorithms in Grasshopper3D for designing deployable structures. Apply Kangaroo3D and Karamba3D plugins to simulate and analyze kinetic behaviors. Create three types of deployable structures: technical origami, inflatables, and spatial linkages. Develop your own deployable space-habitat concept with personalized feedback. Engage in group discussions to review and enhance design concepts collaboratively.
source_fields.methodology: Designing deployable habitats is not only practical for transportation by rocket or helicopter but also leads to innovative and mesmerizing kinetic designs that fold, inflate, and expand in unique ways. Participants will learn how to use computational strategies to create three types of deployable structures: technical origami, inflatables, and spatial linkage mechanisms. Under the guidance of Karl-Johan, you will have the opportunity to develop your own deployable space-habitat concept and receive one-on-one feedback. At the end of the workshop, we will review and discuss the concepts as a group. Experience with Rhino and Grasshopper3D is expected.
source_fields.notes: Having the software with a proper license and installing them on the computer is the responsibility of the attendees.

source_fields.name: AI Conceptual Architecture 2.0
source_fields.introduction: Artificial intelligence is not a novel thing in our lives; its existence has surrounded us for a while. And now that it’s knocking on the doors of the creative process, it’s of the utmost importance to understand the true powers (and limitations) of these tools as soon they will become to shape our careers as architects and designers. And while the current diffusion models cannot break the wall of physical reality just yet, It is surely shaking the grounds below everything we know about creativity and inspiration.
source_fields.description: Students will learn the basic prompt crafting techniques in different models of Midjourney.
source_fields.objectives: Master basic prompt crafting techniques for different models in Midjourney. Understand the capabilities and limitations of AI tools in the creative process. Explore how to create conceptual architectural works using AI text-to-image tools. Compare and contrast various AI platforms, including Midjourney, DALL·E 2, and DreamStudio AI. Participate in discussions to refine and develop selected participant works.
source_fields.methodology: In “AI Conceptual Architecture,” participants can expect to learn the basics of working with different Ai text-to-image tools in creating conceptual works using architectural elements, emphasizing Midjourney and briefly touching on other platforms like Dall-E2 and DreamStudioAI. Participants are expected to learn the basic prompt crafting techniques in different models of Midjourney and understand the differences between each one through exploring various concepts about architectural elements. To conclude the workshop, a few participants’ works will be selected for further discussion/development.

courses.name: META-Fluid Studio 3.0

source_fields.name: META-Fluid Studio 3.0
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Design Workshops | Visualization
source_fields.introduction: After the successful launch of the “META-Fluid Studio” and “META-Fluid Studio 2.0” workshops, which had fantastic student results, requests for the second iteration of this studio arose. The “META-Fluid Studio 3.0” takes another step to unlock the potential of Fluid Design with the Maya software to develop cyber-urban environments in virtual cities. The Meta-Fluid Studio 3.0 explores the quality and power of Fluid Design to conceive cyber-urban environments in virtual cities. The goal is to create a free-standing virtual city designed by 30 different designers teamed up in 3s. Some teams will create meta-archi typologies for this studio, and some designers will join skills to create a ‘meta-urban’ base. Combined, they will create a free-standing, fluid virtual urban field and prove the Multi-Author Urban Design to be the directionality for the future of virtual cities. During this studio, the designers will get acquainted with the 3d modeling software Autodesk Maya, the number one software for Fluid Architecture in the current real-life scenario – and Unreal Engine for the immersive experience of their designs. For the Meta-Fluid Studio 3.0, virtual environments are as real as Physical environments. Together, they strengthen the fluid experience of space and push the boundaries of Fluid Design in Architecture. Meta Archi-Typologies: Event Spaces; NFT exhibitions; Crypto Markets; Concert Stages; Sports Stadium; Lice Streamed Arenas / Fashion walkways/ Entertainment and nightlife.Meta-urban Typologies: Master planners; vertical and horizontal voided buildings; water and green ration; multi-layers of urban circulation.
source_fields.description: META-Fluid Studio 3.0 is a collaborative studio course on PAACADEMY that uses Autodesk Maya and Unreal Engine to design fluid cyber-urban environments within a collectively built virtual city. Thirty designers working in teams of three develop either meta-architectural typologies — event spaces, NFT exhibitions, concert stages, sports stadiums — or meta-urban elements such as master plans, vertical buildings, water and green ratios, and multi-layer circulation systems. The combined output is a free-standing fluid virtual urban field demonstrating multi-author urban design as a model for future virtual cities.
source_fields.objectives: Fluid Design Principles: Explore the concepts and methodologies behind Fluid Design to create dynamic and innovative cyber-urban environments. 3D Modeling in Maya: Gain hands-on experience with Autodesk Maya, focusing on its tools and capabilities for designing fluid architectural forms. Collaboration in Teams: Work collaboratively in groups to develop a cohesive virtual city, enhancing skills in teamwork and project management. Immersive Experiences with Unreal Engine: Learn how to integrate your designs into Unreal Engine for immersive visualization and interaction. Multi-Author Urban Design: Understand the principles of multi-author collaboration in urban design, fostering a shared vision for future virtual cities.
source_fields.requirements: This is an applied workshop. We will learn through involvement, so expect homework! You will work in groups of 3 to distribute the tasks and produce a complete project. Each group will have 10 minutes to present their work on jury day.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 6 (teaching sessions) + 1 (final presentation) No previous knowledge of any software is required. You will learn everything in the workshop.

source_fields.faq: What software is used in the META-Fluid Studio 3.0? :: The studio uses Autodesk Maya as the primary 3D modeling environment for designing fluid architectural and urban forms, and Unreal Engine for real-time visualization and immersive experience of the virtual city. No additional software is required. || What does META-Fluid Studio 3.0 cover? :: The studio covers fluid design principles for cyber-urban environments, 3D modeling of architectural typologies in Maya, collaborative multi-author urban design, and real-time visualization in Unreal Engine. Teams develop either meta-architectural elements such as event spaces, concert stages, and fashion walkways, or meta-urban components such as master planning, vertical buildings, and circulation systems. The studio concludes with a jury presentation where each group presents their work. || Is META-Fluid Studio 3.0 suitable for beginners in Maya? :: The studio is described as applied and hands-on, with homework expected between sessions. Participants work in groups of three, which allows different skill levels to contribute to different aspects of the project. Some prior exposure to 3D modeling is beneficial, as the studio focuses on fluid design methodology and collaborative urban design rather than introducing Maya fundamentals from scratch. || What will I produce by the end of this metaverse architecture studio? :: Each team of three produces a complete architectural or urban design contribution to a collectively designed virtual city, presented in a jury session. Combined across all teams, the final output is a free-standing fluid virtual urban field built in Maya and visualized in Unreal Engine, demonstrating multi-author design at urban scale.

courses.name: Parametric Design With Blender

source_fields.name: Parametric Design With Blender
source_fields.introduction: In a field overflowing with various different applications used for architectural concept design, Blender significantly stands out as a program that is; highly capable of extensive modelling tools including subdivision, widely accessible as it’s free and open source, inherently parametric, highly expandable as it has excellent add-ons like Tissue for tessellation and many others, and it’s equally excellent for presentation with Cycles rendering engine and Eevee.
source_fields.description: We will examine what makes Blender unique among 3D apps and how this uniqueness makes it perhaps the best tool for architectural design.
source_fields.objectives: Master polygonal and subdivision modeling techniques to create complex architectural forms. Utilize non-destructive techniques with modifiers for flexible design iterations. Explore tessellation methods using the Tissue add-on for innovative surface designs. Develop skills in architectural representation and visualization using Blender's rendering engines. Work on practical exercises that progress from simple pavilions to more complex structures like office buildings.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will focus on specific workflows for architectural design modeling that encompass the topics of; Polygonal modeling, Subdivision modeling, Non-destructive techniques with modifiers, Tessellations with the Tissue addon, and Representation. In order to achieve this, we will use a number of exercises to build up your Blender skillset, starting from simple pavilion and concluding with an office building. Blender has excellent capabilities for architectural design and we will focus on how fast and easy it is to investigate design concepts with the program. We will look at what makes Blender unique among 3d apps and how this uniqueness makes it perhaps the best tool for architectural and computational design available today.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 2 sessions Please be informed that we won’t be able to provide any license, invitation, or educational account, for any of the software listed above. Having the software with a proper license and installing them on the computer is the responsibility of the attendees.

courses.name: Vertical Sinuosity (Maya +Enscape)

source_fields.name: Vertical Sinuosity (Maya +Enscape)
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Design Workshops | Visualization
source_fields.introduction: The main objective of this workshop is to equip participants with various techniques of polygon mesh modeling utilizing Autodesk Maya for designing complex geometries and architectural forms. The processes covered in these sessions will explore various mesh modeling operations that can be applied to a simple polygon primitive to achieve desired spatial characteristics in creating social and leisure experiences.
source_fields.description: Vertical Sinuosity is a course on PAACADEMY that teaches polygon mesh modeling in Autodesk Maya for designing complex, organic architectural geometries. Participants work from simple polygon primitives through a range of mesh modeling operations to develop spatial forms suited for social and leisure environments, then integrate Chaos Enscape to visualize and experience those designs in an immersive real-time environment. Grasshopper 3D is also used as part of the workflow.
source_fields.objectives: Polygon Mesh Modeling Techniques: Gain hands-on experience in various techniques for creating complex geometries using Autodesk Maya. Spatial Design Characteristics: Learn how to manipulate simple polygon primitives to achieve specific spatial qualities that enhance social and leisure experiences. Creative Expression: Explore the freedom of using Maya to design aesthetic organic forms and push the boundaries of your creative potential. Virtual Architectural Design: Understand how to design architectural projects in a virtual environment, addressing real-world constraints and conditions. Integration with Enscape: Discover how to effectively use Chaos Enscape alongside Maya to visualize and experience your designs in immersive ways.
source_fields.methodology: The goal of this workshop is to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of utilizing Maya as a design tool giving them the freedom to express their creative potential in designing aesthetic organic forms. The processes covered in the workshop will enable participants to design architectural projects within the virtual realm to overcome existing conditions and constraints and create and experience exceptional environments.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 2 Sessions PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance. No previous knowledge of any software is required. You will learn everything in the workshop.
source_fields.day1_program: Session A – Introduction to Maya as an architectural design tool. Understanding of the basic Maya software user interface. Introduction to polygon modeling and application of basic commands in Maya. Session B – Introduction to polygon modeling techniques. Implementation of polygon modeling techniques to develop a complex architectural geometry (Tower typology). Free modeling of the overall form of the Tower and Podium. Q&A session.
source_fields.day2_program: Session A – Detailed modeling of an architectural typology. Achieving parametric patterning on tower façade and landscape as well as the building form detailing and materiality using Maya. Modeling simple interior details within the conceptual geometry. Session B – Introduction to Enscape real-time rendering and 3d walkthroughs. Importing the Maya model into Rhino for Enscape real-time rendering. Introduction to Enscape viewport user interface and other commands. Adding Assets, Materials, and Visual Settings to achieve realistic renders. Introduction to keyframes and visual paths for creating 3d walkthroughs. Q&A session.
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.

Participants also learn to design architectural projects within a virtual environment, addressing real-world constraints and conditions. || Is this course suitable for beginners in Autodesk Maya? :: The course is designed for participants who want to develop creative and technical proficiency in Maya for architectural design. Some familiarity with 3D modeling concepts is beneficial, as the sessions move directly into polygon mesh operations and design methodology rather than introducing software basics from scratch. || What will I produce by the end of this course? :: Participants complete an architectural design project developed through polygon mesh modeling in Maya, refined to achieve specific spatial and experiential qualities, and visualized in Chaos Enscape. The outcome is a portfolio-ready virtual architectural project demonstrating complex organic form-making and real-time rendering.

source_fields.introduction: Welcome to Rhino for Beginners 2.0, a comprehensive course introducing you to Rhinoceros 3D and Grasshopper 3D. Throughout this course, you will learn basic 3D modeling terminology and tools and an introduction to parametric design using Grasshopper. By the end of our sessions, you will thoroughly understand how to use both Rhino and Grasshopper to create and manipulate your own 3D models. The workshop includes hands-on exercises and design challenges to reinforce the material, supplemented by ongoing support and resources after the course. This is an ideal starting point for anyone looking to dive into the world of 3D modeling and design.

courses.name: Spatial Effects with Midjourney

source_fields.name: Spatial Effects with Midjourney
source_fields.introduction: Text-to-image diffusion models are an accessible way for artists, architects, and designers to experiment with Artificial Intelligence. MidJourney is one such platform that engages our imaginations and lets us explore and test design ideas in a fraction of the time it would traditionally take to draw, model, or render. Joshua Vermillion will lead this MidJourney workshop with an emphasis on generating surface, material, and lighting effects and atmospherics. Along the way, we will develop and craft prompts (the instructions we give to the AI model) as a way to sharpen your ideas and augment your design process.
source_fields.description: This fast-paced workshop will focus on generating images of provocative spatial volumes (interior or exterior).
source_fields.objectives: Generating Design Concepts: Use MidJourney to create innovative surface, material, and lighting effects. Crafting Effective Prompts: Develop skills in prompt crafting to refine and enhance design ideas. Exploring Spatial Effects: Focus on producing spatial volumes and atmospherics through iterative editing. Blending Techniques: Learn to integrate traditional design elements with AI-generated imagery. Comparative Analysis: Evaluate outputs from different MidJourney models to understand their creative impacts.
source_fields.methodology: Part of the value of using a diffusion model like MidJourney is getting unexpected interpretationsof your ideas—things you might have never thought of that extend and challenge yourimagination. The first session of this workshop will emphasize generating these non-determinateand surprising outcomes that MidJourney generates so well–the happy accidents, the counter- intuitive, and the uncanny—all focused on spatial effects. The second session will use image prompts and MidJourney’s new blend operation to gain more control over the generated outcomes as well as to integrate traditional design sketches, models, and photos into this generative AI process. Both sessions will use a combination of demonstrations followed by hands-on individual design challenges, culminating in one last group-challenge/project. This fast-paced workshop will focus on generating images of provocative spatial volumes (interior or exterior), along with effects and atmospherics utilizing surface, lighting, textures, materials, shape, etc. We will iteratively edit, generate, re-roll, and blend prompts, as well as the resulting images. We will also examine and compare the differences in the outputs from various MidJourney models and workflows (for instance, MJ’s v3 and v4 models, the remastering and blend options, and adjusting aspect ratios) all of which affect the coherence and “creativity” of the results. By the end of this workshop, participants will have demonstrated and practiced several workflows in MidJourney for developing their design ideas as well as generating visually compelling design imagery. Along the way we will learn about many of the settings in MidJourney that can help us iteratively work through an idea while utilizing expressive design language and prompt-craft. Ultimately, everyone will come away with several different ways to weave AI into their own design process in order to augment their creative endeavors.

source_fields.name: Creative Artifacts
source_fields.introduction: Today, there is a growing demand for art and creative solutions in various settings, including retail spaces, museums, private and public venues, shows, and events. At the same moment, the cross-cutting diffusion of new AI-based tools and technologies is augmenting human capability to generate new ideas, by enabling unprecedented combinations of references, shapes, colors, spaces, and materials. Creative Artifacts workshop aims at promoting a methodology that leverages AI and computational design as new paradigms for creativity and inspiration. The workshop will explore how AI tools can be used effectively and efficiently to address practical design challenges and meet specific design requirements, ensuring the consistency and success of a design concept.
source_fields.description: Creative Artifacts workshop aims at promoting a methodology that leverages AI and computational design as new paradigms for creativity and inspiration.
source_fields.objectives: AI-Driven Creative Methodology: Understand how to leverage AI tools and computational design to enhance creativity and generate innovative ideas for art installations. Practical Design Solutions: Explore how AI can effectively address specific design challenges in various settings, ensuring that concepts meet practical requirements. Interplay of Innovation and Tradition: Learn to balance cutting-edge technology with traditional design contexts, creating harmonious and impactful art pieces. Framework for Creative Strategies: Develop essential skills for informed decision-making and turning concepts into tangible projects in the age of AI. Hands-On Concept Development: Engage in generating concepts that respond to specific briefs across different creative categories, applying learned techniques in real-world scenarios.
source_fields.methodology: The aim of this program is to explore and develop innovative concepts for art installations and creative interventions, such as sculptures, furniture, visual elements, and displays. The focus is on the interplay between cutting-edge solutions and traditional contexts. The ultimate goal is to equip participants with a new framework for creative strategies, informed decision-making, and computational techniques, essential skills for turning concepts into tangible projects in the era of AI. Throughout the program, students will be challenged to generate concepts that respond to specific briefs for various creative categories.

source_fields.introduction: Learn the fundamentals of BIM and dive into your first design project. Building Information Modeling (BIM) is the foundation of digital transformation in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Is the process of creating and managing information for a built asset. Based on an intelligent model and enabled by a cloud platform, BIM integrates structured, multi-disciplinary data to produce a digital representation of an asset across its lifecycle, from planning and design to construction and operations.
source_fields.description: This workshop will focus on introducing participants to Building Information Modeling (BIM) using Autodesk Revit.
source_fields.objectives: Introduction to BIM: Understand the fundamentals of Building Information Modeling (BIM) and its importance in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Getting Started with Revit: Learn the basics of Autodesk Revit, including how to set up a project and navigate the software interface. 3D Modeling Techniques: Gain hands-on experience in creating 3D models of typical building typologies, such as residential structures. 2D Documentation: Discover how to generate essential 2D documentation from your 3D models, including plans, sections, and elevations. Collaborative Workflow: Experience a collaborative workflow by synchronizing changes on a central file, enhancing your understanding of BIM's capabilities in a team setting.
source_fields.methodology: The goal of the Revit workshop for beginners is to deliver an engaging and hands-on learning experience utilizing BIM methodology. Participants will be able to view real-world examples of how the BIM approach is applied in the architectural, engineering, and construction (AEC) sector through project displays as part of the workshop. Furthermore, the workshop will feature a presentation in which the instructor will deliver a “hands-on” experience to demonstrate the Revit software’s functionalities. Following that, students will get the opportunity to practice and become more comfortable with the program by repeating the actions described. Students will work individually and if there will be time, students will work on a local file synchronizing their changes on a central file stored on a dropbox cloud. This workshop will focus on introducing participants to Building Information Modeling (BIM) using Autodesk Revit. We will be working on typical building typologies, such as a residential building, and participants will learn how to create 3D models and generate 2D documentation using Revit. Revit is a powerful BIM software application widely used in the AEC industry that offers a wide range of modeling and documentation tools. The scope of this workshop is to provide participants with a basic foundation in BIM and Revit, enabling them to create their own 3D models and documentation for typical building typologies. By the end of the workshop, students will be able to set up a project, create and edit walls, floors, ceilings, master families, build mass models, and more. The final output will be a BIM model and a basic drawing set of the project.

courses.name: Social Media For Designers

source_fields.name: Social Media For Designers
source_fields.introduction: Why social media? Internet and social media have now become one of the most influential tools that had revolutionized marketing strategies in all professions. Starting with websites from the early 90s, social media platforms like Facebook in 2004, and the birth of other platforms, the old notions of getting published or running ads in printed magazines to get exposure are almost dead. With the rise of fan pages, influencers, communities, chat groups, and new marketing strategies, many new professions emerged that did not exist before. This resulted in the establishment of new departments in companies to manage their websites and social media channels. And by now (2023) almost everyone has understood the power of social media and how it can have a huge impact on anyone’s or any company’s growth. Why architects and designers should use social media? Like all professions, architects are not exceptional in this. Internet and social media have changed the way architects and designers think about their projects. As much as we think this is wrong, getting more exposure on social media became a quality standard for offices and clients on a success of a project. By using social media, architects and designers were able to showcase their work, build their own brands, network with peers, engage with potential clients, and keep up with industry trends. Using the right strategy will result in increasing visibility, establishing credibility, building relationships, showcasing the brand, and staying up-to-date.
source_fields.description: Social Media for Designers is a course for architects, designers, small firms, freelancers, and social media departments covering how to build a professional online presence. Participants learn to identify the right platforms, develop content strategies, analyze performance metrics, create presskits, and produce high-quality posts tailored to design audiences. The course also addresses techniques for audience interaction, brand building, and staying current with industry trends through social media. Two sessions are included and no specialized software is required.
source_fields.objectives: Choosing the Right Platforms: Identify and select the most effective social media platforms for architects and designers to maximize visibility and engagement. Content Creation Strategies: Learn how to create engaging content that showcases your work and resonates with your target audience. Analyzing Data and Metrics: Understand how to analyze social media metrics to measure success and refine your strategies. Building an Online Brand: Develop techniques for establishing a credible online presence and personal brand within the architecture and design community. Effective Audience Interaction: Explore methods for interacting with your audience to build relationships and stay connected with industry trends.
source_fields.methodology: This course aims to showcase the potential of using social media to establish a credible and strong online presence on the internet. We will focus on the ways of choosing the right social media platforms, analyzing their data, and generating effective strategies that align with the target audience. The course will provide a solid understanding of producing presskits, creating engaging content, methods of making high-quality publications, and interacting with their audience. By showcasing great examples, the course will enhance the participants' knowledge of the best curations on social media.
source_fields.notes: This workshop is suitable for Small-sized Architecture Firms, Companies, Freelancers, and Social Media Departments. Total sessions: 2 sessions. Please be informed that we won’t be able to provide any license, invitation, or educational account, for any of the software that will be used during the workshop. Having the software with a proper license and installing them on the computer is the responsibility of the attendees.

courses.name: Computational Dreamscape

source_fields.name: Computational Dreamscape
source_fields.introduction: Discover the power of Grasshopper 3D and learn how to create innovative and socially responsible designs. The Computational Dreamscape workshop is a unique opportunity to explore parametric design tools and methods emphasizing creativity while achieving the most successful results. We’ll demonstrate how Grasshopper 3D can help architects have a dynamic and fast workflow while fully controlling geometries. Using this software, you can generate visually striking, engaging, and efficient geometries.By participating in the workshop, you’ll develop your algorithmic thinking, understand geometry, and generate Grasshopper definitions that can be used for multiple purposes, making your projects unique and adaptable.
source_fields.description: The Computational Dreamscape will demonstrate how Grasshopper 3D can help to have a dynamic and fast workflow, and fully control geometries.
source_fields.objectives: Parametric Design Techniques: Master the use of Grasshopper 3D to create innovative and adaptable designs, focusing on algorithmic thinking and geometry manipulation. Project Development: Work on a final project to design an indoor art installation or outdoor urban space, applying computational design techniques. Dynamic Visualizations: Create a competitive set of static and dynamic visualizations (diagrams, renderings, videos) to effectively communicate your design process and outcomes. Community-Centric Design: Explore how design can enhance community engagement and social interaction through thoughtful spatial applications. Iterative Design Process: Learn to experiment with multiple design iterations and optimize your solutions based on specific constraints, integrating theoretical knowledge with practical skills.
source_fields.methodology: During the workshop, we’ll use a hands-on approach to learning. The workshop requires a basic understanding of Grasshopper, and the level is intermediate, starting with simplicity and building up complexity.The final project will involve designing either an indoor art installation or an outdoor sculptural urban space. The workshop will focus on applying computational design techniques to create physical and digital matrices of parametric models, which will be used to suggest different spatial applications. The final assignment will involve putting together a competitive set of static and dynamic visualizations (diagrams/renderings/videos) to illustrate their progress. The students will work individually or in teams, depending on their preferences, and will receive guidance and feedback from the instructor throughout the process. The workshop will explore the different ways in which design can contribute to enhancing a sense of community, identity, and relationship with others, offering spaces where everyone can play, rest, and enjoy time with their loved ones. These recreational areas can encourage active movement, creative exploration, and the development of social skills. During the workshop, we´ll generate exciting designs, from the small scale of a room to the large urban scale. We will deal with sculptural installations with ever-changing effects, sinuous and colorful landscapes, and intriguing urban spaces, which can be inhabited in multiple ways and float between reality and fantasy. Grasshopper 3D is crucial to generate these geometries that are difficult or impossible to achieve through traditional methods. Additionally, Grasshopper 3D enables us to experiment with several design iterations, test different scenarios, and optimize the design for specific constraints. The workshop students are expected to learn a combination of theoretical and practical knowledge and gain professional experience. They will be taught to think outside the box and apply algorithmic approaches to solve architectural problems efficiently. The final project will give them something tangible to add to their portfolio.The focus is on creating exciting and innovative projects, ensuring that the skills learned in the workshop can be applied in their everyday workflow. The aim is to produce work that is not just for show, but that can be used or inspire changes in how they work.

The attendees are responsible for having the software with a proper license and installing it on their computers.

source_fields.name: Midjourney Design
source_fields.introduction: With the recent release of Midjourney V5, we have now arrived at a new paradigm of AI -aided design. This tool empowers us to convert our imagination into industry quality visuals in seconds. But with the capability to conjure up such quality results, it becomes increasingly vital to understand the principles of design and how to guide the technology towards intention and success. In this studio, Tim Fu of Zaha Hadid Architects will share his experience using AI to design for architecture, product, and fashion, and will guide participants through the process of developing their own design of their choice.
source_fields.description: Participants will learn to undertake commissioned projects using AI, learning to curate, evaluate, and critique their results towards their own goals.
source_fields.objectives: Understanding AI-Aided Design: Gain insights into the principles of design and how to effectively guide AI tools like Midjourney V5 to achieve your design intentions. Practical Techniques: Learn various techniques and methods for using Midjourney V5 to create high-quality visuals quickly and efficiently. Curating and Evaluating Work: Develop skills to curate, evaluate, and critique AI-generated results in relation to your design goals. Interactive Collaboration: Engage with fellow participants to share ideas, critique work, and inspire each other throughout the design process. Real-World Application: Discover how to undertake commissioned projects using AI, applying the knowledge gained in practical, industry-relevant contexts.
source_fields.methodology: This course will be an interactive and fun session where participants can listen, participate, and ask questions. Various techniques and spreadsheets for Midjourney V5 will be shared. Participants will learn to undertake commissioned projects using AI, learning to curate, evaluate, and critique their results towards their goals. The course is optimized for 100 participants, and each individual can contribute to this community's collective knowledge. We will discuss, evaluate, and inspire each other’s work.

source_fields.introduction: Welcome to Grasshopper for Beginners 2.0, an in-depth course designed to explore the capabilities of the Grasshopper3D plugin. This workshop is tailored for those eager to learn advanced applications of this powerful tool in creating intricate and visually stunning architectural structures. Through hands-on learning and expert guidance, participants will master the skills needed to design sophisticated parametric models. By the end of this course, you will be able to transform complex concepts into precise 3D models and gain precise control over your designs for more accurate outcomes. Join us to elevate your architectural modeling skills to new heights.
source_fields.description: The workshop will have a more in-depth view of the Grasshopper3D and its applications in creating complex and breathtaking structures.
source_fields.objectives: Advanced Grasshopper Techniques: Dive deep into the advanced capabilities of the Grasshopper3D plugin for creating complex parametric models. Complex 3D Modeling: Learn to transform intricate design concepts into precise 3D models, enhancing your architectural visualization skills. Model Control and Accuracy: Master techniques for controlling and fine-tuning your models to achieve more accurate and refined outcomes. Hands-On Learning: Engage in hands-on exercises that allow you to apply your knowledge in real-time, reinforcing the concepts taught. Integration with Rhinoceros 3D: Gain insights into how to effectively use Grasshopper3D in conjunction with Rhinoceros 3D to maximize your design potential.
source_fields.methodology: Grasshopper for Beginners 2.0 is a weekend-long workshop where participants will have a more in-depth view of the Grasshopper3D plugin and its applications in creating complex and breathtaking structures. This course will equip the students with the skills to create advanced parametric models using Grasshopper3D. At the end of the workshop, the students will be able to convert their complex ideas to 3D and learn how to control their models to get more accurate results.

courses.name: Biomorphic Topologies

source_fields.name: Biomorphic Topologies
source_fields.softwares: Adobe After Effects | Adobe Photoshop | Chaos Corona | Cinema 4D
source_fields.introduction: The workshop ‘Biomorphic Topologies’ offers an in-depth introduction to organic-parametric design tools for architects and designers, using Cinema 4D and Corona Renderer. Students will learn to use the advantages of a CGI software in the context of various design stages – from concept models, sculpted geometries, and procedural architectural details to environments and animations. Additionally, the workshop covers rendering and post-processing, using Corona Renderer, Adobe Photoshop, and Adobe After Effects.
source_fields.description: The workshop ‘Biomorphic Topologies’ offers an in-depth introduction to organic-parametric design tools for architects and designers, using Cinema 4D and Corona Renderer.
source_fields.objectives: Parametric Geometry Creation: Master workflows for creating organic-parametric geometries using Cinema 4D's tools, including splines, meshes, and subdivision surfaces. Animation Techniques: Learn to combine keyframe animations with parametric tools like MoGraph Effectors, Volume Builder, and Cloner for dynamic design presentations. Rendering Skills: Understand the Corona Renderer workflow, including materials, lighting, camera setups, and environment creation for high-quality renderings. Post-Processing: Gain proficiency in image and video post-production using Adobe Photoshop and Adobe After Effects to enhance your visual outputs. Project Application: Apply learned techniques to various architectural projects, such as biomorphic pavilions and animated facades, integrating complex workflows throughout.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop covers various workflows to use Cinema 4D’s tools to create parametric geometry, animations, and renderings. Introduction to Splines, Mesh, and Subdivision Surfaces Interconnected parametric tools and workflows using MoGraph Effectors and Fields, Volume Builder, Cloner, Atom Array, Voronoi Fracture, Displacements and many more. Combining keyframe animation with the parametric tools above Sculpting tools Introduction to Corona Render workflow (materials, lights, camera, environments, etc) Image Post-Production in Adobe Photoshop. Video Post-Production in Adobe After Effects The assignments will be conducted individually. Starting from a beginner’s level, the workshop procedurally introduces increasingly complex and interconnected workflows to create parametric systems and animations in Cinema 4D. Each tutorial in the workshop uses different architectural projects as vehicles to learn various operations: covering biomorphic pavilions and skyscrapers, faceted interiors, animated facades, organic objects, and scene environments. Every project introduces different methods and workflows, including powerful tools such as MoGraph Effectors, Volume Builder, and Cloner. As CGI software Cinema 4D is best equipped to bring geometries to life and introduce animation to parametric geometries. Using the Corona render engine, students will learn how to use materials, light, cameras, and environments, as well as a post-processing workflow in Adobe Photoshop for images and Adobe After Effects for time-based animations. The introduction lecture ›A holistic approach to design: speculative futures and organic hybrids‹ will provide insights into relevant projects from the worlds of design, fine art, architecture, and fashion and will introduce geometric processes we can find in nature and biology. Students will be able to use and interconnect various parametric workflows in Cinema 4D. They will learn to work with spline- and mesh-based geometry, subdivision surfaces, sculpting tools, and procedural operations such as the MoGraph Effectors and Fields, Volume Builder, Cloner, Atom Array, Voronoi Fracture, Displacements, and many more. Additionally, students will be introduced to keyframe animations. The workshop teaches to set up a rendering workflow using materials, lights, cameras, and environments to create high-quality renderings with Corona Renderer, as well as post-processing in Adobe Photoshop and After Effects.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 2 sessions (8 Hours). PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance for students. Having the software with a proper license and installing them on the computer is the responsibility of the attendees.

source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | ControlNet | Grasshopper 3D | Midjourney | Stable Diffusion
source_fields.introduction: Design workflow has been completely redefined since AI platforms such as Midjourney and Stable Diffusion impacted Architecture and Design. This workshop offers technical knowledge and fosters creative thinking by integrating Midjourney and Stable Diffusion with Rhinoceros to produce open-ended, controlled designs with industry-ready standards. On one hand, we will learn to expand architectural concepts using Midjourney’s commands, such as /image, /blend, and /remix, including image prompts as guidance. On the other hand, we will develop solid skills further to control geometry, materiality, and atmosphere creation using Stable Diffusion + Controlnet, including inpainting techniques. The workshop will combine both tools to maximize potential and optimize them for various design objectives.

source_fields.name: Spatial Effects with Midjourney 2.0
source_fields.introduction: Text-to-image diffusion models are an accessible way for artists, architects, and designers to experiment with Artificial Intelligence. MidJourney is one such platform that engages our imaginations and lets us explore and test design ideas in a fraction of the time it would traditionally take to draw, model, or render. Joshua Vermillion will lead this MidJourney workshop with an emphasis on generating surface, material, and lighting effects and atmospherics. Along the way, we will develop and craft prompts (the instructions we give to the AI model) as a way to sharpen your ideas and augment your design process.
source_fields.description: This fast-paced workshop will focus on generating images of provocative spatial volumes (interior or exterior), along with effects and atmospherics utilizing surface, lighting, textures, materials, shape, etc.
source_fields.objectives: Prompt Crafting: Develop skills in creating effective prompts to guide MidJourney, enhancing your ability to generate desired design outcomes. Exploration of Spatial Effects: Experiment with generating surprising and innovative spatial volumes, focusing on surface, lighting, textures, and materials. Image Integration Techniques: Learn to use image prompts and blending operations to integrate traditional design sketches and models into the generative process. Workflow Comparisons: Compare outputs from different MidJourney models (v3, v4, v5) to understand how settings affect creativity and coherence in results. Iterative Design Processes: Practice workflows for iteratively refining design ideas and imagery, incorporating AI into your creative process for enhanced exploration.
source_fields.methodology: Part of the value of using a diffusion model like MidJourney is getting unexpected interpretations of your ideas—things you might have never thought of that extend and challenge your imagination. The first session of this workshop will emphasize generating these non-determinate and surprising outcomes that MidJourney generates so well–the happy accidents, the counter-intuitive, and the uncanny—all focused on spatial effects. The second session will use image prompts and MidJourney’s new blend operation to gain more control over the generated outcomes as well as to integrate traditional design sketches, models, and photos into this generative AI process. Both sessions will use a combination of demonstrations followed by hands-on individual design challenges, culminating in one last group-challenge/project. This fast-paced workshop will focus on generating images of provocative spatial volumes (interior or exterior), along with effects and atmospherics utilizing surface, lighting, textures, materials, shape, etc. We will iteratively edit, generate, re-roll, and blend prompts, as well as the resulting images. We will also examine and compare the differences in the outputs from various MidJourney models and workflows (for instance, MJ’s v3, v4, and v5 models, the remastering and blend options, and adjusting aspect ratios) all of which affect the coherence and “creativity” of the results. By the end of this workshop, participants will have demonstrated and practiced several workflows in MidJourney for developing their design ideas as well as generating visually compelling design imagery. Along the way we will learn about many of the settings in MidJourney that can help us iteratively work through an idea while utilizing expressive design language and prompt-craft. Ultimately, everyone will come away with several different ways to weave AI into their own design process in order to augment their creative endeavors.

source_fields.introduction: Evolutionary Computation (EC) is a sub-field of artificial intelligence (AI) which used the “Evolutionary Algorithm” (EAs) to solve problems that have too many variables for traditional algorithms. This method uses to select the best alternatives between various solutions based on problems’ criteria and constraints known as “Optimization”. The engineering community (including architects and structural Eng.) could benefit from this design method as a rapid and high-quality decision-making method and tool to increase the speed and quality of their design choice in the building design field. This workshop’s participants would learn how to use the EAs to study the effect of architectural design decisions on buildings’ structures’ performance and how to select optimum design alternatives among various design solutions. To achieve this goal, we use “Karamba3D” as a Finite Element (FE) analysis tool which provides an accurate analysis of spatial trusses, frames, and shells in the early design stage, and, “Galapagos” as an optimization tool based on the genetic algorithm. They are both fully embedded in the parametric design environment of Grasshopper, a plugin for the 3D modeling tool Rhino. This makes it easy to combine parameterized geometric models, finite element calculations, and evolutionary optimization algorithms altogether.
source_fields.description: This workshop is for architecture and structural designers and/or students who are interested in the simultaneous design of structure.
source_fields.objectives: Element Analysis: Understand the main criteria and evaluation factors for conducting Element analysis using Karamba3D. Modeling Structures: Learn how to model and analyze simple structures in the early design stage with Karamba3D. Evolutionary Algorithms: Grasp the basic concepts and applications of Evolutionary Algorithms (EAs) in architectural design. Genetic Algorithm Optimization: Discover how to use Galapagos for optimization and establish a design framework in the architectural design process. Design Workflow Integration: Learn to create a generative structure and optimize architectural designs by integrating modeling, analysis, and evolutionary optimization techniques in Grasshopper.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop presents a computer-aided design framework for the generation of non-standard structural forms in static equilibrium using Karamba3D and Galapagos, as Finite Element analysis tools and Genetic Algorithm optimization tools, respectively. The design workflow relies on the implementation of a series of operations (generation, evaluation, optimization, and regeneration) that allow to the creation of multiple design alternatives and to navigate in the architectural design space according to objective and subjective Criteria defined by the designer. This workshop is for architecture and structural designers and/or students who are interested in the simultaneous design of structure and architecture. All modeling and computational analysis will be done in the grasshopper/Rhino7. Having beginner to intermediate knowledge of Grasshopper is a must. Karamba3D will be used for modeling and analyzing the structure during sessions. No prior Karamba3D knowledge is required. The trial Karamba3D version is sufficient. The Evolutionary Optimization Algorithms will be explained from scratch and Galapagos, as the single objective optimization tool based on the genetic algorithm will be introduced. Prior knowledge of optimization algorithms is an advantage but not necessary.
source_fields.notes: The workshop is free for Digital Members. Total sessions: 2 sessions PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance for students who deliver a final project. Please be informed that we won’t be able to provide any license, invitation, or educational account, for any of the software listed above. Having the software with a proper license and installing them on the computer is the responsibility of the attendees.

courses.name: Topology-Based Modelling With Blender

source_fields.name: Topology-Based Modelling With Blender
source_fields.introduction: Blender is becoming an important player in the Architectural field. It is a great software for rendering and animation and an extremely powerful tool for mesh modeling. Working with meshes makes it possible to easily generate complex and organic shapes, allowing architects and designers to express their creativity without constraints. With this workshop, the participants will be able to move the first steps inside the software, creating complex shapes with a modular approach by working with a combination of simple components. In addition, carefully controlling the mesh's topology makes it possible to articulate directional patterns that follow the main shape. The workshop is for beginners and intermediates, so a basic understanding of Blender’s interface and the basic modeling commands is recommended.
source_fields.description: ‘Topology-Based Modelling With Blender’ explains the correlation between mesh-topology and tessellation strategies to create parametric models.
source_fields.objectives: Mesh Modeling Techniques: Gain foundational skills in mesh modeling using Blender, focusing on creating complex and organic shapes through a modular approach. Topology Principles: Understand the importance of mesh topology and how it influences the design and articulation of forms. Tissue Add-on Utilization: Learn to use the Tissue add-on for tessellation, allowing for the creation of intricate parametric models without scripting. Organic Shape Creation: Develop an architectural pavilion by combining form-finding strategies with parametric modeling techniques. Scalability of Techniques: Discover how the modeling principles taught can be applied across various scales, from architectural objects to urban design and beyond.
source_fields.methodology: The scope of the workshop is to model a small architectural pavilion.The first part is dedicated to tutorials about mesh modeling and Tissue. During this part, the participants will understand the principles of mesh topology combined with Tissue’s tessellation. Working on an individual exercise, they will produce an organic main shape and a system of components that will characterize its skin. During the workshop, we will work with Blender and the Tissue add-on to combine the flexibility of mesh modeling with the different tessellation strategies of Tissue. We will understand the correlation between mesh topology and tessellation strategies. Thanks to a combination of modifiers and Tissue, we will be able to create complex parametric models without the need for scripting or node interfaces. These methods will be applied to an architectural object, but their principles can be easily applied to different scales, from urban design to wearable products. The students will learn the basic principles of Mesh modeling in Blender. In addition, thanks to a combination of form-finding strategies and parametric modeling using the Tissue add-on, they will also understand how to obtain functional and appealing architectural objects.
source_fields.notes: Sessions: 2 sessions (8 Hours) PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance for students. Please be informed that we won’t be able to provide a license, invitation, or educational account for any of the software listed above. The attendees are responsible for having the software with a proper license and installing it on their computers.

courses.name: Ideation to Creation With AI

source_fields.name: Ideation to Creation With AI
source_fields.introduction: AI text-to-image tools such as Midjourney have revolutionized form generation in architecture by allowing designers to quickly and easily generate visual representations of their ideas. architects generally visualize and communicate their ideas through different formats. Perspectives provide a visual representation of the design from a specific viewpoint, allowing the architect to evaluate the form, scale, and proportion of the building. On the other hand, the architectural model representations usually convey more information and can help architects evaluate the spatial relationships between different elements of the building. This workshop is led with an emphasis on form generation and exploring different formats these forms might be represented in (architectural models/ perspectives). Through this course, we will develop new skills to integrate various spatial elements and arrangements in prompts and turn them into complex interesting forms and architectural aesthetics.
source_fields.description: This workshop is led with an emphasis on form generation and exploring different formats these forms might be represented in (architectural models/ perspectives).
source_fields.objectives: Prompt Crafting Techniques: Develop skills to create effective prompts for generating architectural forms using AI tools. Iterative Design: Learn how to refine and evolve design ideas through iterative processes to enhance creativity. Integration of Spatial Elements: Master the integration of various materials and spatial arrangements into complex architectural forms. Curating Images and Aesthetics: Explore techniques for curating forms based on composition and spatial interest, leading to new architectural aesthetics. Presentation Formats: Understand how to present generated forms in diverse architectural formats, including models and perspectives.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop consists of two sessions, each with a unique focus. The first session is primarily aimed at prompt craft, iterative design, and technical skills necessary for students to develop innovative forms. The second session centers on creating advanced forms by integrating various spatial elements and arrangements, curating images based on composition, and developing new architectural aesthetics. Assignments are incorporated into both sessions for participants to implement the techniques they have learned into their projects. This workshop will mainly focus on form generation and presenting them in various architectural formats, such as models and perspectives. Participants will learn how to create intricate architectural forms and integrate different materials, spatial elements, and arrangements to add diversity to them. The workshop will also cover techniques for curating forms in terms of composition and spatial interest, as well as exploring new architectural aesthetics. Additionally, the workshop will examine various techniques for form generation and combine them to create greater variety.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 2 Sessions PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance. No previous knowledge of any software is required. You will learn everything in the workshop.

source_fields.name: Cyber Pavilion
source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: The workshop's main aim is to introduce participants to a range of step-by-step techniques for modeling polygon meshes using Autodesk Maya to design fluid, complex, and rich architectural forms. This workshop will provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of Maya as a design tool, allowing them to express their creative ideas in designing fluid, organic forms. The processes covered in the workshop will enable participants to design architectural projects within virtual conditions and create and experience exceptional virtual environments. The course will include an introduction to Twinmotion, a real-time rendering engine as a tool that allows rapid visualization and presentation of a given design.
source_fields.description: The course focuses on the development of the topology of the pavilion as an architectural form.
source_fields.objectives: Polygon Mesh Modeling: Master step-by-step techniques for creating complex polygon meshes in Autodesk Maya, enabling fluid and organic architectural designs. Topology Development: Understand the principles of topology in architectural modeling, focusing on the pavilion form and its applications in various urban contexts. Creative Expression: Gain skills to effectively translate creative ideas into virtual designs, enhancing your ability to visualize and realize architectural concepts. Real-Time Rendering: Learn to use Twinmotion for rapid visualization, enabling quick presentation and exploration of your designs in immersive environments. Individual Project Execution: Apply learned techniques in a final project, allowing for personal exploration and development of unique architectural forms within a guided framework.
source_fields.methodology: Students will be exposed to a range of polygon modeling techniques inside Autodesk Maya. They will be working individually for the final project. The course focuses on the development of the topology of the pavilion as an architectural form commonly used in a wide range of applications and embedding it in an urban scenario.
source_fields.notes: Total sessions: 2 Sessions PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance. No previous knowledge of any software is required. You will learn everything in the workshop.
source_fields.day1_program: Introduction to the Autodesk Maya interface and navigation. Creating basic geometries and understanding of modeling principles. Modeling basics exercises. Application of previously learned 3d modeling techniques to create a spatial Low Poly model of the ‘Cyber Pavilion.’
source_fields.day2_program: Continuation of 3d modeling using the learned techniques from session 01 and work on detailing the completed model. Introduction of new specific modeling techniques for obtaining architectural details and realism. Generate various inspiring images using a simple light conjuration inside Autodesk Maya for creating conceptual screenshots. Introduction to the Twinmotion interface and importing a previously generated Pavilion model from Maya into Twinmotion. Develop visualizations using simple and fast working methods with Twinmotion to obtain the conceptual vision needed to present the project.
