courses.name: PixelSpace: Intro to 3D Generative AI

source_fields.name: PixelSpace: Intro to 3D Generative AI
source_fields.softwares: Chaos Corona | Luma AI | Unreal Engine
source_fields.introduction: Recent image and video generation advancements have revolutionized content creation, offering unprecedented possibilities. While we rapidly approach seamless interaction with scenes and videos through text inputs, 3D scene generation remains a fertile ground for exploration. Over the past two years, significant progress has been made in 3D and 4D object generation, mainly through multiview diffusion models. More recently, the application of consistent video generation as a proxy for 3D spatial representation has emerged, paving the way for comprehensive 3D scene generation. These developments present a unique opportunity to harness deep learning algorithms, allowing us to envision and create immersive 3D scenes, thereby unlocking a new dimension of creative expression.This workshop will explore the cutting-edge techniques of multiview diffusion models conditioned on camera paths for 3D scene generation. We will dive into the latest methods for representing 3D scenes and geometry and investigate how current research in 3D generative AI leverages pre-trained image and video models for a 3D generation. Participants will learn how to use text and image inputs to generate scenes, which will then be imported into Unreal Engine for post-production and to create a concept reel. This workshop focuses on the automation of 3D scene generation from text and images. Through theoretical discussions and practical exercises, participants will explore the capabilities of 3D generative AI and its application in fast-tracking design exploration. Key topics include: Introduction to Multiview Diffusion Models : Understanding the principles and techniques behind multiview diffusion models. Exploring case studies of successful applications in 3D scene generation. 3D Scene and Geometry Representation : Examining recent advancements in the 3D scene and geometry representation. Discussing the role of different representation techniques in enhancing 3D consistency. Leveraging Pretrained Models : Learning how to adapt pre-trained image and video models for a 3D generation. Hands-on sessions with state-of-the-art algorithms for scene creation. Text and Image Inputs for Scene Generation : Text and image inputs are used to automate the generation of 3D scenes. Practical exercises on integrating inputs to produce coherent scenes. Integration with Unreal Engine : Importing AI-generated scenes into Unreal Engine for further development. Techniques for enhancing interactivity and immersion in Unreal Engine.
source_fields.description: PixelSpace: Intro to 3D Generative AI focuses on automating 3D scene creation using AI models and Unreal Engine.
source_fields.objectives: Exploring 3D Generative AI : Understand and utilize advanced AI algorithms for scene generation. Scene Creation : Learn to automate the process of 3D scene creation using text and image inputs. Interactive Design : Develop skills in creating interactive and immersive experiences in Unreal Engine. Creative Exploration : Foster innovation and creativity in architectural design through AI tools.
source_fields.methodology: Inspirational Inputs: Text and Images : Use descriptive text and images to generate 3D scenes. These inputs will serve as the foundation for your scene’s development. Scene Development : Experiment with different inputs to see how they influence the generated scenes. Scene Generation: Multiview Diffusion Models : Apply these models to generate consistent scenes across multiple views. Representation Techniques : Use various methods to represent geometry and scene details effectively. Interactive Experience Creation: Unreal Engine Integration : Learn to import and refine your AI-generated scenes in Unreal Engine. Enhancing Immersion : Develop interactive elements to create a fully immersive experience. Project Showcase: Concept Reel : Compile your generated scenes into a cohesive concept reel. Presentation and Feedback : Present your work and receive feedback from peers and instructors. By the end of this workshop, participants will have a solid understanding of how to leverage 3D generative AI to automate scene generation and create immersive architectural experiences, opening new avenues for creative expression and design exploration.

source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: FormVerse 3.0 enhances the exploration of architectural creativity using AI, Cinema 4D, Corona Renderer, and Unreal Engine. This advanced workshop will teach how to use these powerful tools to transform AI-generated forms into complex, interactive 3D models. From initial concept generation to creating an immersive metaverse experience, FormVerse 3.0 offers a comprehensive journey into the new realm of AI and immersive digital architecture.
source_fields.description: FormVerse 3.0 will focus on transforming AI-generated forms into interactive 3D models with Cinema 4D for an immersive metaverse experience.
source_fields.objectives: Creating Striking Images with Midjourney for Design Concepts Selecting Optimal Variations: Turning Ideas into 3D Models High-Quality Rendering Techniques with Corona Renderer Interactive Design: Building Experiences in Unreal Engine 5 From Concept to Creation: A Comprehensive Journey in 3D Architecture
source_fields.methodology: This course will showcase a complicated approach that bridges concept generation using Midjourney and the adoption into a Cinema 4D modeling environment. Starting with thinking and concept form generation in Midjourney, We will move into Cinema 4D, covering the basics briefly before diving into advanced modeling. This workshop will teach participants to use parametric tools like SubD, MoGraph, effectors, and fields. After refining the model, we will render it using Corona and export it to Unreal Engine 5 to create a human-scale interactive experience and explore the metaverse’s digital architecture. This workshop will focus on developing an architectural form concept using Midjourney, providing detailed tactics for selection and refinement, and transforming these concepts into a Cinema 4D modeling environment. FormVerse 3.0 will showcase valuable skills in selecting the most promising images, understanding different perspectives, reimagining underlying shapes, and learning the best methods to model them with clean topology. The final stages will involve rendering the model with Corona Renderer and creating an interactive experience in Unreal Engine.

courses.name: Parametric Optimizations: Decoding Spaces and Places

source_fields.name: Parametric Optimizations: Decoding Spaces and Places
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Design Workshops | Structural Analysis
source_fields.introduction: The technological decade between 2010 and 2020 was mainly characterized by the global explosion of the Big Data phenomenon the implications that this has on society are still ongoing and are the subject of numerous studies. The amount of data generated in that period has proven infinitely more significant than that created in the previous millennia. The quantity of “input” is constantly increasing. Thus, the level of complexity consequently increases. The information we gather from different situations are stimuli that actively influence the places we live in, determining their space, geometry, sociability, and beauty. We can and must use them to design more consciously.
source_fields.description: Parametric Optimizations: Decoding Spaces and Places is a course on PAACADEMY that teaches participants to manage design data and optimize architectural projects for sustainability and performance using Grasshopper 3D and Rhinoceros 3D. Led by Stefano Bastia, the course traces projects from initial environmental analysis through performance improvement, using Ladybug for solar and environmental analysis, Galapagos for evolutionary algorithm-based optimization, and LunchBox for parametric facade design and pattern generation. The workshop is designed for Grasshopper first-timers and teaches a data-driven workflow for making location-specific, performance-aware design decisions.
source_fields.objectives: Introduction to parametric and computational design principles. Understanding sustainability principles in architectural design. Enhancement of participants' skills in Rhinoceros (Rhino 3D). Proficiency in using Grasshopper 3D for design analysis and optimization. Practical applications of various Grasshopper plugins, such as: LadyBug for environmental analysis and sustainability. Galapagos for evolutionary algorithm-based optimization. LunchBox for parametric facade design and pattern generation. Additional plugins to be announced. Exploration of sustainability analysis, parametric design, and performance-driven design through Grasshopper plugins. Application of these tools in real-world design projects focused on performance and optimization.
source_fields.methodology: Through a series of example projects led by Stefano Bastia, we will trace a reverse path to understand how a project is conceived, from the initial analyses to improving its performance. Participants will individually learn to develop and manage a small project through a series of exercises using Rhinoceros, with the support of Grasshopper. This workshop aims to equip participants with skills to find and manage all these inputs (design data) for more conscious design. Through a series of software and plugins, we will be able to capture and channel them and consequently control them. The more information we have as input, the better and more precise the results will be, giving us more assets at our disposal and enhancing our ability to “solve” problems in a targeted way.
source_fields.requirements: The workshop is designed for Grasshopper’s first-timers . This workshop will teach you a workflow that allows you to control projects while considering different locations’ specific characteristics and contexts.
source_fields.notes: Students must have all the software installed before starting the workshop.

source_fields.name: Computational Dreamscape 2.0
source_fields.introduction: Explore Grasshopper 3D and learn how to create interactive and dynamic designs. The Computational Dreamscape 2.0 Studio is an opportunity to dive into parametric design and showcase your work using Unreal Engine.The workshop is split into two parts. In the first part, we’ll demonstrate how Grasshopper 3D helps designers work efficiently and control geometries. In the second part, we’ll focus on bringing your designs to life in real time using Unreal Engine 5, a world-class, state-of-the-art game engine. This engine is renowned for visualizing designs in a photorealistic manner, enabling real-time changes to lighting and materials. Additionally, it allows you to create interactive experiences where you can play and modify your creations in real time.
source_fields.description: The Computational Dreamscape 2.0 Studio is an opportunity to dive into parametric design and showcase your work using Unreal Engine.
source_fields.objectives: Mastering Grasshopper 3D: From Algorithmic Concepts to Dynamic Designs Seamless Workflow: Integrating Rhinoceros with Unreal Engine for Real-Time Visualization Creating Photorealistic Environments: Lighting and Materials in Unreal Engine 5 Developing Interactive Experiences: Turning Designs into Playable Installations Final Project Showcase: Crafting Unique Sculptural Installations for Your Portfolio
source_fields.methodology: During the workshop, we’ll use a hands-on approach to learning. Experience with Rhinoceros3D is required. However, no experience with Grasshopper is required, as we’ll start with simple algorithmic concepts and gradually increase complexity from day one. Prior knowledge of Unreal Engine is not mandatory before the workshop, as it will be explained to beginners, starting from the basics. We’ll explore a seamless workflow from Rhinoceros to Unreal Engine, allowing us to harness the power of Unreal Engine to make real-time changes to designs created in Rhinoceros. The Unreal Engine part will cover essential topics like project creation, interface navigation, and main controls. Participants will learn to visualize in real-time design from Grasshopper/Rhino into Unreal Engine, create basic materials, and focus on lighting techniques specifically for interior environments. This workshop will demonstrate how to render images and animations. This workshop will help you develop algorithmic thinking, understand geometry, and create versatile Grasshopper definitions, making your projects unique and adaptable. During the workshop, we’ll work on sculptural installations with dynamic effects and colorful, flowing artistic landscapes that can be experienced in various ways, blending reality and fantasy. Grasshopper 3D is essential for generating these complex geometries that are hard to achieve with traditional methods. It also allows us to experiment with multiple design iterations, test different scenarios, and optimize designs for specific constraints. Unreal Engine is a famous tool for creating images and animations. Still, its unparalleled power lies in enabling users not only to visualize but also live within your architectural models, transforming them into dynamic, playable experiences. The final project will consist of designing indoor art installations. You’ll create competitive static and dynamic visualizations for the final assignment to showcase your progress (including diagrams, renderings, and videos). Students can choose to work individually or in teams and will receive guidance and feedback from the instructors throughout the process.

courses.name: AI-Driven Fashion Design

source_fields.name: AI-Driven Fashion Design
source_fields.introduction: In an era where technology intertwines with every facet of our lives, the fashion industry is not left behind. This workshop is designed to unveil the immense potential of generative tools in revolutionizing the fashion design process. This workshop delves into the novel ways artificial intelligence can enhance and expedite your creative workflow, offering endless variations and expanding the horizons of innovation. By leveraging these cutting-edge tools, designers can capture and interpret their clients’ visions more precisely, opening new realms of creativity and precision. Throughout the workshop, we will explore the technical nuances of working with generative tools, developing a mindset that integrates these technologies seamlessly into your creative process. We will discuss various techniques tailored specifically for the fashion industry, ensuring you are well-equipped to harness these technologies effectively. Moreover, the workshop will delve into curation and artistic vision, emphasizing the crucial role of your unique perspective in shaping the future of fashion design.In addition, we will take a practical journey through the entire design process of projects the studio is currently working on, showcasing the software and methodologies employed alongside generative tools. This comprehensive exploration will provide a holistic understanding of how AI can seamlessly integrate into the design workflow, empowering you to elevate your fashion creations to new heights.
source_fields.description: AI-Driven Fashion Design is a course on PAACADEMY that teaches fashion designers and multi-disciplinary creatives how to integrate generative AI tools into the fashion design process using Midjourney and ChatGPT. Participants learn to navigate Midjourney workflows, develop advanced prompts for unique fashion concepts, and apply curation techniques that merge AI output with their own artistic vision. The course also covers real-world project examples from the instructor's studio, demonstrating how generative tools are integrated into active design workflows from concept through to final output.
source_fields.objectives: Unlocking Creativity: Harnessing Generative Tools in Fashion Design Mastering Midjourney: Techniques for Seamless Workflow Integration Developing Advanced Prompts for Unique Fashion Concepts Curating Artistic Vision: Merging AI with Your Design Perspective Hands-On Project Development: Elevating Fashion Creations with AI
source_fields.methodology: This workshop is designed to cater to individuals with different backgrounds in design, whether they are fashion designers or experts in other design fields interested in exploring fashion design with generative tools to bring their vision to life. Participants’ levels of expertise in AI will also vary, including those new to AI tools. This workshop will focus on mastering technical tools, navigating Midjourney workflows, and honing curation techniques. Subsequently, the focus will shift towards the concept design process and mastering advanced prompt development techniques. By the end of the workshop, participants will have the skills to effectively develop and articulate their unique vision in fashion design using AI tools. The workshop’s hands-on approach ensures that participants can immediately apply their new skills to their own projects, fostering practical and tangible skill development.

Both technical skills and creative methodology are addressed. || Is this course suitable for designers with no AI experience? :: Yes. The course is designed for participants with varying levels of AI experience, including those completely new to generative tools. It is open to fashion designers and professionals from other design fields who want to explore AI-assisted fashion design workflows. || What will I produce by the end of this AI fashion design course? :: Participants develop a fashion design concept using Midjourney and ChatGPT, applying advanced prompting and curation techniques to produce a set of AI-generated visuals that reflect their personal design vision and are immediately applicable to their own projects.

courses.name: Creative Perspectives: Architectural Concepts with AI

source_fields.name: Creative Perspectives: Architectural Concepts with AI
source_fields.categories: Architectural Design | Artificial Intelligence | Design Workshops
source_fields.softwares: Adobe After Effects | ControlNet | Midjourney | Stable Diffusion
source_fields.introduction: With the advent of image-generative platforms and their ability to create concepts and themes faster than traditional modeling, many individuals—whether familiar with the field or not—are using their imagination to develop innovative ideas. In this competitive environment, designers must leverage their prior knowledge and ability to perceive great designs through traditional means and incorporate quick image generation into their workflow for concept designs or social media management. Platforms like Midjourney and Stable Diffusion can significantly enhance the design process, client discussions, renderings, and marketing. Therefore, learning these software tools is essential for modern designers.
source_fields.description: Creative Perspectives: Architectural Concepts with AI is a workshop on PAACADEMY that teaches designers to use Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and ControlNet for concept development, mood board creation, and image editing. The workshop concludes with a video production phase using Runway, Immersity AI, and Adobe After Effects to turn AI-generated images into project videos for clients and social media. No prior AI tool experience is required.
source_fields.objectives: Mastering Image Generation: Leveraging Midjourney for Architectural Concepts Exploring Creative Command Techniques for Mood Boards and Themes Enhancing Your Design Process with Stable Diffusion and ControlNet Creating Engaging Project Videos Using AI and Premiere Pro/After Effects Developing Publishable-Quality Designs Through Precise Image Editing
source_fields.methodology: This workshop will teach the tips and tricks of precise image creation using prompting techniques for mood board creation, concept exploration, theme development, and social media. We will focus on using Midjourney to master its use and achieve concepts that align with the designer’s vision and reflect the theme of their project. This workshop will explore the extensive range of commands available to create unique images, personalize them, and edit them to achieve publishable-quality designs. Additionally, we will cover the basics of Stable Diffusion and its use as an alternative or supplement to Midjourney, including upscaling and editing images locally. Finally, we will learn how to use these still images to create project videos for clients and social media using Immersity AI, Runway, and Premiere Pro/After Effects. Students will develop themes and create engaging videos as their final project.
source_fields.notes: Software Installation is NOT a part of the workshop! Participants must have all the software installed and ready before the workshop.
source_fields.day1_program: Session 1: Introduction to AI generative imagery, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and related software and their potential usage in a designer’s workflow Learning Midjourney: Introduction to Discord interface and chat organization Official website and image organization Midjourney commands and their usage Basic prompting techniques Assignment 01: Create an image of the field/subject of your choice Student Discussion: Imagination vs. Results – Tips to Improve Results Advanced prompting and complex methods Session 2: Introduction to Stable Diffusion: ComfyUI vs. Automatic 1111 (local install vs. web use) Using ComfyUI: Commands and connectors Basic image creation – Img2Img & Txt2Img Assignment 02: Create a set of images using prompts focused on one theme of choice.
source_fields.day2_program: Session 1: Discussion of Assignment 02: Tips and tricks, prompt refinement, and error correction Inpainting, Correction & Miscellaneous Editing Workflows in Stable Diffusion. Image Upscale models – Local and web (ComfyUI vs. Magnific AI) Finalising Image Set from Assignment 02. Session 2 – Video Creation: Introduction to SVD, Runway & Immersity AI – Depth map video/GIF vs. Image to video. Introduction to Premiere Pro/After Effects. Edit videos, overlays, and export HQ videos for professional & Social uploads. Final Project: Creating an immersive video using the best images created so far for clients and social media publishing. Discussion – Q&A

source_fields.faq: How is ControlNet used with Stable Diffusion for architectural image generation? :: ControlNet is a conditioning model that works alongside Stable Diffusion to give designers precise spatial and compositional control over generated images. Instead of relying solely on text prompts, ControlNet accepts inputs such as depth maps, edge detection images, line drawings, or pose references to guide where the model places structure, mass, and detail. In architectural workflows, this allows designers to use existing plans, sections, or 3D renders as generation references, producing AI-enhanced visuals that remain spatially coherent with the original design intent. This workshop covers ControlNet as part of the Stable Diffusion workflow for concept editing and image refinement. || What does the Creative Perspectives workshop at PAACADEMY cover? :: The workshop covers Midjourney in depth, including its full command range for mood board creation, concept exploration, theme development, and social media use, with a focus on achieving precise prompting outcomes that align with a designer's vision. It then introduces Stable Diffusion as a local alternative for upscaling and editing using ControlNet. The final phase teaches how to animate and sequence still AI images into project videos using Immersity AI, Runway, and Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects, ending with a final project combining theme development and video production. || Is this AI workshop suitable for designers with no prior experience in Midjourney or Stable Diffusion? :: Yes. The workshop is designed for designers who want to integrate AI image generation into their workflow, whether or not they have used these tools before. The course begins with the fundamentals of Midjourney prompting before progressing to more advanced command techniques, then introduces Stable Diffusion as a supplement. Prior architectural or design experience is beneficial for understanding how to apply these tools to concept development and client communication, but no coding or technical AI knowledge is required. || What will I produce by the end of the Creative Perspectives workshop? :: Participants will develop a complete set of AI-generated concept images across multiple architectural themes, refined using Midjourney's editing commands and Stable Diffusion with ControlNet for upscaling and local adjustments. The final project is an AI-generated project video combining still images into a sequenced, animated output using Immersity AI, Runway, and Adobe After Effects, suitable for client presentations or social media publishing.

source_fields.name: AI-Driven Architectural Design
source_fields.softwares: ComfyUI | Krea.AI | Luma AI | Midjourney | Runway ML | Stable Diffusion
source_fields.introduction: In the fast-changing field of architecture, incorporating AI tools during design has become inevitable. New applications of these tools are being discovered and experimented with daily, becoming a new norm in the profession. This workshop aims to empower architects by enabling AI to be one of their valuable assistants throughout design development. This workshop will take participants on a journey of learning how to successfully integrate and work with artificial intelligence tools to speed up their daily design methods.The focus will be on the collaborative side of AI, illustrating how these tools can be effortlessly incorporated into personal design workflows, whether in the early ideation stage or during design development, to visualize and express materiality & atmosphere. This workshop will help you determine how these technologies can boost architects' creativity and streamline architectural design methods.
source_fields.description: AI-Driven Architectural Design focuses on integrating AI tools to enhance creativity and streamline design processes in architecture.
source_fields.objectives: Integrating AI Tools into Your Architectural Design Process Accelerating Creativity: AI-Driven Workflows in Design Mastering Effective Prompting Techniques for AI Applications Transforming Sketches and Models with AI Image-to-Image Methods Creating Dynamic Visuals: From Images to Video Animation in Architecture
source_fields.methodology: Our two-day workshop will take a hands-on approach, allowing space and opportunity for participants to work both independently and collaboratively on the seamless applications of AI-driven workflows into the design process. It will begin with a comprehensive lecture on all the available AI tools. Setting the foundation for practical application. Then, we will continue with the demonstrations of various workflows.Participants will engage in various AI methodologies, developing practical skills and confidence in using and experimenting with the tools. By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to implement these techniques effectively in their architectural design practices. This workshop will teach participants the practical application of AI tools in the architectural design process. We will start with the latest AI technologies, concepts, and applications. Showcasing tools like Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Comfy UI, Runway, and Luma AI. We will demonstrate architecture-focused approaches and shortcut methods in each tool. This workshop includes techniques for effective prompting, image-to-image methods like transforming sketches and 3D models into detailed renders, and image-to-video animation.
source_fields.notes: Software Installation is NOT a part of the workshop! Students must have all the software installed before starting the workshop. The AI-Driven Architectural Design - Innovative Workflows Studio workshop by PAACADEMY will start at 14:00 (GMT) on Saturday, September 28th. Total sessions: 2 Sessions The teaching duration per session will be around 4 hours. Students will have time for a break between teaching hours. Each session and the entire studio will be recorded, and videos will be available for participants just a day after the class for unlimited time. PAACADEMY will provide a certificate of attendance. The studio has limited seats. Tickets are non-transferable & non-refundable. Please read carefully before you register.

courses.name: Capturing Space And Time

source_fields.name: Capturing Space And Time
source_fields.introduction: Whether you have a lot of experience or you are just getting started with a new camera, this online workshop will take you from beginner to advanced photographer in the architecture field.You will learn professional techniques to develop and advance your photography skills.This online course covers the fundamentals of photography including everything on how the camera and lenses work as well as the technical aspect of photography like exposure, focus, depth, lighting, and more.
source_fields.description: Capturing Space and Time is a 4-day online architectural photography workshop taught by Nancy Da Campo, a freelance architecture and interiors photographer based in Milan. The course covers the full photography workflow from camera fundamentals through post-processing, including DSLR and mirrorless camera operation, manual exposure control with shutter speed, aperture and ISO, composition techniques, lighting, and image editing and rescue strategies. The workshop is suitable for both beginners and photographers with existing experience looking to advance to a professional level.
source_fields.objectives: Master your DSLR or mirrorless camera for advanced photography. Balance shutter speed, aperture, and ISO for optimal exposure. Techniques for effective composition and capturing engaging shots. Editing strategies to enhance and rescue problematic images.
source_fields.methodology: How to fully understand and master your DSLR or mirrorless cameraBalance shutter speed, aperture, and ISO for perfect exposure and getting out of “auto-mode.”How to correctly shoot for a quick and smooth editHow to get the perfect compositionRescuing a problematic image through editingFilled with detailed walk-throughs, easy-to-follow explanations, and plenty of examples, you will learn to train your eye to capture dynamic and engaging architecture shots, crafting subtle changes to enhance your images and bring your photography work to a professional level.
source_fields.notes: Software and Techniques: The Workshop will run using Adobe Lightroom Classic CC and Adobe Photoshop CC for the photo editing section – no previous experience is necessary. The free app Snapseed will be used for the mobile editing tutorial – no previous experience is necessary. Level of knowledge: This workshop is designed for Beginner photographers with little to no experience who want to improve their photography skills, Intermediate photographers who want a deeper understanding of photography concepts, and anyone who wants to improve their general knowledge of photography to capture beautiful architectural images.
source_fields.day1_program: Camera settings Balancing the exposure triangleFocus on shutter speed, aperture, and ISO Preparing to shoot RAW vs JPEG Understanding white balance Composition Gear – cameras, lenses, and accessories Understanding focal length.
source_fields.day2_program: How to approach your edit Shooting tips to ease your edit Choosing your selects Basic editing workflow Advanced edits Exporting your edited work.

The course teaches you to move out of auto mode and take full manual control of your camera settings, so any DSLR or mirrorless body with manual controls is sufficient. Specific lens recommendations and camera setup guidance are covered in the course. No particular camera brand or model is required. || What does the Capturing Space and Time photography workshop cover over 4 days? :: The workshop covers four core areas across its four days. First, camera and lens fundamentals including how DSLR and mirrorless systems work. Second, exposure control covering the relationship between shutter speed, aperture, and ISO to achieve correct exposure without auto mode. Third, composition and shooting techniques for capturing dynamic and engaging architectural shots. Fourth, editing strategies including how to enhance well-shot images and rescue problematic ones in post-processing. || Is this architectural photography course suitable for complete beginners? :: Yes. The workshop is explicitly designed to take participants from beginner to advanced level within the four-day format. Whether you are just starting with a new camera or already have photography experience and want to move into the architecture field professionally, the course adapts to your level. Walk-throughs are detailed and examples are used throughout to build practical skills progressively. || What will I be able to do after completing this architectural photography course? :: After the workshop you will be able to operate your DSLR or mirrorless camera in full manual mode, achieve correct exposure across varied architectural lighting conditions, compose and capture professional-quality architectural and interior shots, and edit your images to a portfolio-ready standard. You will have trained your eye for architectural photography and developed a repeatable professional shooting and editing workflow.

courses.name: Adaptive Fashion: Procedural Design with Bio-Materials

source_fields.name: Adaptive Fashion: Procedural Design with Bio-Materials
source_fields.introduction: Humans are recognized as the most adaptable species on Earth, as demonstrated by parts of our body that are no longer of actual use but essential for survival. However, despite their advancements, our technological creations lack the same adaptive intelligence, remaining static in the face of rapid changes and evolving environments. But if we could, even for a moment, imagine using all the technologies at our disposal in a tailored manner and pushing them to their limits, what materials and geometries could we create, and how would they interact with our bodies and the environment? What issues could we improve, and how would our lives change? We could undoubtedly develop solutions with unprecedented adaptive intelligence, capable of responding in real-time to climate changes on Earth and future needs in hostile environments such as space or new planets yet to be explored. The human body remains an organism in evolution, and with this workshop, we will explore possible scenarios for its future. Here , you can find a list of what to download before the workshop.
source_fields.description: The "Adaptive Fashion" workshop will explore using data-driven design and bio-materials to create sustainable and adaptive textiles.
source_fields.objectives: AI in Design : Learn how AI enhances concept design processes. Surface Analysis : Master techniques for effective user needs assessment. Parametric Geometry : Generate adaptable designs from diverse data sources. Material Recipes : Develop custom material formulations from a material library. Holistic Design Strategy : Integrate AI, analysis, geometry, and materials into cohesive designs.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop will focus on generating textures based on data and the selection of bio-material from the material library. Using data from the body or environment, we will investigate the generation of geometry in textile forms, patterns, and microstructures, from a single layer to multiple layers, able to respond to different needs. By the end of this workshop, participants will develop a robust approach to building a wide variety of geometry systems based on data. The main objective is to embed biomaterial know-how in the design workflow. This workshop explores design methodologies that connect the information around us, understood as Data, and the physical world, understood as Materials. With the "Adaptive Fashion: Procedural Design with Bio-Materials" workshop, the choice of bio-materials is placed at the center of the design process. Participants will be able to generate complex geometries, from which it will be possible to extract useful information to select the most appropriate materials. This integrated approach aims to create a relationship between design and materials, making the product more functional in its mechanical properties and more sustainable in its end-of-life. The proposed methodology will be applied to creating and visualizing a second skin for the human body. This does not exclude the fact that this approach can be adapted to different design scales, expanding its potential to various design areas.

courses.name: PA Editorial Fellowship 2024

source_fields.name: PA Editorial Fellowship 2024
source_fields.introduction: The PA Editorial Fellowship aims to encourage new editors and writers to contribute to the field of architecture and design. We want to ensure that diverse voices from different backgrounds have visibility in this field. The 3-month program, which will take place between 17 August- 23 November 2024, will provide training in writing about architecture and design, digital publishing, blogging, research methods, and the impact of emerging technologies on digital publishing. PA Editorial Fellows will have the opportunity to observe, create, and receive feedback on content production processes with the PA Editorial Team. Their responsibilities include writing regular articles on specific topics and participating in trainings.
source_fields.description: The PA Editorial Fellowship 2024 aims to encourage new editors and writers to contribute to the field of architecture and design.
source_fields.objectives: Experience in working collaboratively with the editorial team. You will learn how to write an article on architecture and design, how to plan an outline for your article, and which tools you can use during that process. Experience with developmental and conceptual editing, copy editing, permissions, design, publicity, and social media. The training will take place on weekends. After 5 article submissions, the Fellow will receive access to PAACADEMY’s member-only workshops. An in-depth understanding of the publication process that can be applied to future jobs and projects. Certificates.
source_fields.requirements: Experience in editorial work is preferred but not required. We aim to help aspiring writers and editors learn more about architecture and design-based content publication. The Fellow must feel confident working independently. Applicants do not need to have an editorial project to apply. Applicants can from all around the world but must be able to attend scheduled Zoom meetings; we are mainly using Greenwich Mean Time (UK).
source_fields.notes: The application has been closed.

source_fields.name: Sculpture Synergy in VR
source_fields.softwares: Gravity Sketch | Krea.AI | Midjourney | Substance Modeler | Substance Painter | Unreal Engine
source_fields.introduction: Sculpture Synergy with VR is a 2-day workshop that explores the integration of VR sculpting with AI-powered creativity, advanced texturing techniques, and professional-grade video production. In today’s rapidly evolving creative landscape, blending human artistry with artificial intelligence can unlock new realms of possibility. This workshop is designed for artists and designers looking to enhance their VR sculpting skills using tools like Gravity Sketch, Substance Modeler, and Substance Painter while integrating AI-driven inspiration through Krea.ai. Participants will learn how to bring their creations to life by producing high-quality video outputs using Unreal Engine 5.
source_fields.description: Sculpture Synergy in VR is a 2-day workshop on PAACADEMY that combines VR sculpting, AI-assisted creativity, advanced texturing, and cinematic video production. Participants use Gravity Sketch and Substance Modeler for 3D sculpting in virtual reality, Krea.AI for AI-driven design inspiration, Substance Painter for realistic materials, and Unreal Engine 5 to produce professional video outputs of their work. A VR headset such as Quest 2, Quest 3, or Quest Pro is required.
source_fields.objectives: VR Sculpting: Create detailed 3D sculptures using Gravity Sketch and Substance Modeler. AI Tools: Utilize Krea.ai for creative inspiration and enhancements. Texturing: Apply realistic materials with Substance Painter. Video Production: Produce cinematic outputs using Unreal Engine 5. Workflow Development: Develop a personalized workflow combining these techniques.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop is structured around individual learning, with instructional demonstrations and hands-on practice. Each participant will work independently on their projects, with guidance and feedback provided throughout. The focus will be developing a personal workflow combining VR sculpting, AI integration, texturing, and video production. This workshop will guide you through creating detailed 3D sculptures in VR using Gravity Sketch and Substance Modeler, harnessing AI, and incorporating it into your creative process with Krea.ai. Followed by adding realistic materials and textures with Substance Painter. On the second day, we’ll dive into Unreal Engine 5 to produce cinematic video outputs of your sculptures, showcasing your work in a professional and visually compelling manner.
source_fields.requirements: Hardware Requirements: Participants will need a VR headset (e.g. Quest 2/3 Quest Pro) and a computer capable of running Gravity Sketch, Substance Modeler, Substance Painter, and Unreal Engine 5. Ensure your hardware and software are set up before the workshop begins. CPU: Intel i7-8700K / AMD Ryzen 7 or higher GPU: NVIDIA RTX 2070 / AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT or higher RAM: 16 GB or more Storage: General: 2-5 GB SSD for most software Substance Painter: 50 GB SSD specifically required Unreal Engine 5: 100 GB SSD for installation Operating System: Windows 10/11 Additional Requirements: VR headset (Quest 2/3/Pro or equivalent) for Gravity Sketch and Substance Modeler Pen & tablet optional for Substance Painter High-speed internet for Krea.ai
source_fields.notes: Participants MUST have all the software Installed before starting the workshop! Pre-Workshop Preparation: It’s recommended that participants familiarise themselves with the interfaces of Gravity Sketch, Substance Modeler, Substance Painter, and Unreal Engine 5. Pre-workshop tutorials are available on the respective websites.

For this workshop, participants are required to have a Quest 2, Quest 3, or Quest Pro headset set up and ready before the sessions begin. The computer running Gravity Sketch and the other required software should meet the workshop's hardware specifications: an Intel i7-8700K or AMD Ryzen 7 or higher CPU, an NVIDIA RTX 2070 or equivalent GPU, 16 GB of RAM, and Windows 10 or 11. || What does the Sculpture Synergy in VR workshop at PAACADEMY cover? :: Day 1 focuses on VR sculpting using Gravity Sketch and Substance Modeler, incorporating AI-driven design enhancements through Krea.AI, and applying realistic textures and materials with Substance Painter. Day 2 moves into Unreal Engine 5, where participants learn to produce cinematic video outputs that showcase their sculpted and textured work in a professional, visually compelling format. Each participant works independently on their own project throughout, with guided demonstrations and ongoing feedback. || What hardware and software do I need before joining this VR sculpting workshop? :: Participants must have all software installed and hardware configured before the workshop begins. Required tools include Gravity Sketch, Substance Modeler, Substance Painter, and Unreal Engine 5, along with a compatible VR headset such as Quest 2, Quest 3, or Quest Pro. Storage requirements are significant: Substance Painter requires 50 GB SSD and Unreal Engine 5 requires 100 GB SSD. A high-speed internet connection is also needed for Krea.AI. A pen and tablet is optional for Substance Painter work. || What will I produce by the end of the Sculpture Synergy in VR workshop? :: By the end of the two days, participants will have a fully sculpted and textured 3D model built in VR, enhanced with AI-assisted design decisions from Krea.AI, and rendered as a cinematic video output in Unreal Engine 5. The workshop is designed to help each participant develop a personal, repeatable workflow that combines VR sculpting, AI integration, professional texturing, and video production into a single end-to-end creative process.

source_fields.name: AI & Parametric Negotiation
source_fields.softwares: ComfyUI | Luma AI | Midjourney | Rhinoceros 3D | Stable Diffusion
source_fields.introduction: Can there be a dialogue between designers and AI where their intelligence comes together?This workshop focuses on the collaboration between designers and AI. "Artificial Intelligence: Parametric Negotiation" workshop explores how minimal interventions from the designer can transform AI into a creative companion. The goal is to find a ground where designers maintain some control while allowing AI to suggest options that might not have been considered.In the workshop, we will neither fully control AI nor blindly accept what it generates. Instead, we will create a shared human-AI latent space where both contribute to the design process.
source_fields.description: This workshop focuses on the collaboration between designers and AI.

source_fields.scope: This workshop is designed for beginners without prior knowledge of Rhino, Grasshopper, or ComfyUI. We will primarily focus on image-to-image creation and achieving precise results based on the design or pattern created during the workshop. To enhance the designs, we will use IPAdapter in ComfyUI for style transfer, utilizing Midjourney’s latent space to generate images. To help AI better understand the design, we will use Depth, Sketch, and Canny ControlNet, ensuring that AI can interpret the design more accurately while allowing flexibility to apply its creative interpretation.

source_fields.name: Building Envelope(d) Data
source_fields.introduction: The workshop is designed to provide a deep understanding of a professional workflow applicable to various scales and design contexts. Participants will learn how to create fully parametric-informed 3D models using Rhino and Grasshopper, which can efficiently improve the design processes from concept development to detailed facade design.
source_fields.description: Building Envelope(d) Data offers a comprehensive exploration of parametric 3D modeling for building envelope design.
source_fields.objectives: Develop a systematic approach to managing design complexity. Utilize Rhino and Grasshopper for automated workflows and design iterations. Familiarize yourself with Elefront and its capabilities for coordinating complex 3D models within the Rhino environment. Implement techniques to embed information into geometries for enhanced coordination. Split up the process into steps that multiple users can use for further development. Integrate structural or functional considerations seamlessly into the design process. Explore 3D facade detailing in a real case study.
source_fields.methodology: We will adopt a hands-on learning approach tailored for intermediate to advanced Grasshopper users. While the exercise will provide a structured framework, participants will have the opportunity to personalize their designs and details based on their interests. The workflow is split into steps of increasing complexity allowing participants to progressively build on their skills. Collaborative discussions and Q&A sessions will also help everyone to get a comprehensive understanding of this method. By the end, participants will have gained confidence in applying the same principles to different design goals and purposes. This workshop will explore the key aspects of typical shell and core design, from geometry set out to facade detailing. This course will teach you how to manage design complexity by developing a BIM-like model within Rhino environment. Using Elefront, participants will learn how to combine geometric and non-geometric data and how to interrelate them to ensure a smooth transition across multiple design iterations and different levels of detail. Storing metadata inside Rhino objects allows the splitting of a complex process into manageable parts, facilitating various users to use them for further development. With this approach, participants will also automate some repetitive tasks and minimize errors inherent in manual modeling.
source_fields.requirements: Good knowledge of Rhino & Grasshopper is required. Basic knowledge of Elefront is welcome but not required.

Basic familiarity with eleFront is welcome, but not necessary. || How is non-geometric data managed within Rhino and Grasshopper? :: You will use eleFront to embed metadata and parameters directly into Rhino geometries, creating a BIM-like, information-informed 3D model that streamlines multi-user coordination. || What real-world architectural design scale is used in the course exercises? :: The workshop focuses on shell-and-core design, geometry set-out, and 3D facade detailing, applied to a real architectural case study. || What practical outcomes can I expect to achieve by the end of the workshop? :: You will master automated, step-by-step data management workflows that reduce manual modeling errors, simplify complex facade iterations, and allow multiple team members to work on split, coordinated parts of a model.

source_fields.introduction: Join us for an insightful Design Panel Talk featuring three distinguished experts who will explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, design, and emerging tools and technologies that are reshaping industries today. Each guest will present for one hour, offering an in-depth look at AI’s transformative potential across various fields and the latest advancements in architectural design. From innovative applications to the future of AI-driven development, this panel is a unique opportunity to gain valuable insights from leading voices at the forefront of the Architectural revolution.
source_fields.description: This Design Tech Talk features three expert-led presentations and a dynamic discussion on the latest advancements and emerging technologies shaping the future of architecture.
source_fields.objectives: Frameworks for AI-native spatial design and advanced concept iteration. Methods for nature-inspired product design and sustainable material integration. Strategies behind parametric execution and advanced computational design leadership. Techniques in symbiotic urbanism, generative AI, and bio-data integration. Foundations of complex structural geometry and spatial experimentation. Approaches to computational workflows and evolving contemporary typologies.
source_fields.scope: The Design-Tech Talk will feature engaging live Q&A sessions, where attendees can directly interact with the speakers and explore the more profound implications of AI's role in design. These discussions will allow participants to share ideas and learn from leaders' experiences at the cutting edge of architectural and technological innovation. The event aims to foster a collaborative environment for learning and networking. This event is ideal for anyone interested in the intersection of architecture, technology, and AI. Whether you're looking to deepen your understanding of parametric design, learn about the latest computational tools, or discover how AI is shaping the future of the design industry, this talk will offer valuable insights and inspiration. Learn from industry pioneers and explore the future of design technology.

source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | ControlNet | Rhinoceros 3D | Runway ML | Stable Diffusion
source_fields.introduction: As the architectural profession continues to evolve, technological advancement is reshaping how designers approach their work. The transition from traditional drafting to digital tools like CAD, Rhino, and Grasshopper brought significant shifts in practice while rendering engines such as V-Ray and Enscape revolutionized visualization. The rapid rise of Artificial Intelligence, primarily through diffusion models and AI-driven generative tools, is introducing a new paradigm for architectural design. This workshop is designed to harness AI technologies effectively while remaining in control of the creative process. Through two targeted, hands-on sessions, participants will explore how AI can be thoughtfully integrated to enhance the creative design process. The focus will be on practical application—using AI as an extension of the designer’s toolkit without losing sight of core architectural principles. This workshop will be interactive, with dedicated time to address participants' questions and thoroughly explain the key concepts to avoid confusion, Offering ample opportunities for discussion so participants can leave with a confident understanding of how to apply AI tools effectively in their own design workflows.
source_fields.description: This workshop explores integrating AI-driven tools like Stable Diffusion and ControlNet into architectural design workflows, enhancing creativity while maintaining control over the design process.

source_fields.name: Transforming Architecture: 3D Models to Ethereal Art
source_fields.softwares: Grasshopper 3D | Luma AI | Midjourney | Rhinoceros 3D | Runway ML
source_fields.introduction: In a world where technology and creativity converge, knowing how to transform 3D models into captivating visual narratives is essential for modern architects. This workshop will explore the use of AI tools like Midjourney, Luma AI, and Runway Gen 3 to bring ephemeral architecture and ethereal sculptures to life. Participants will learn to create images from scratch with Midjourney, utilizing pre-prepared 3D models in Grasshopper that will be shared for greater efficiency. Additionally, we will employ Meshy and Hyperhuman to produce 3D models from AI-generated images, allowing students to explore new creative dimensions. By harnessing these technologies, you will uncover the power of visual storytelling in architecture.
source_fields.description: Transforming Architecture: From 3D Models to Ethereal Art focuses on transforming 3D models into captivating visual narratives using AI tools through interactive sessions and hands-on projects.
source_fields.objectives: By the end of the course, you will be able to: Create intricate 3D models using Grasshopper. Generate and enhance 3D models from Midjourney images with AI tools. Produce visually striking videos that effectively communicate your architectural vision.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will include interactive sessions, hands-on exercises, and collaborative projects. Students will work individually and in pairs on their final projects. Key workflows will consist of: Modeling in Grasshopper: Creating 3D models. Midjourney Integration: Generating images from scratch and combining them with Grasshopper models. 3D Model Creation: Using Meshy and Hyperhuman to create models from images or prompts. Video Production: Creating engaging videos with Luma AI and Runway Gen 3.

courses.name: EcoFusion: Robotic Manufacturing

source_fields.name: EcoFusion: Robotic Manufacturing
source_fields.introduction: From preservation to sustainability, Going forward, design will benefit significantly from the hybridities that emerge from the misalignments of materiality, design methodologies, and fabrication techniques. The workshop will cover crucial design concepts directly dealing with building materials and construction, focusing specifically on the evolution and design of architectural components such as columns, facade panels, and roof systems. We will try to find answers that influence design decision-making within the behavior of natural materials, the plasticity of synthetic material, the intricacies of components entanglement, and the resolution of the robotic fabrication process.
source_fields.description: EcoFusion: Robotic Manufacturing is a 2-day workshop on PAACADEMY that explores the integration of natural and synthetic materials through robotic digital fabrication. Using Rhinoceros 3D, Grasshopper 3D, KUKA PRC, and Termite, participants learn geometry toolpath generation, robotic 3D printing, and six-axis robotic milling to design architectural components including facade panels and columns. Advanced Rhino knowledge and basic Grasshopper experience are required.
source_fields.objectives: Digital fabrication design for immediate geometry generation. Merging natural and synthetic materials to explore hybrid aesthetics. Fundamentals of translating complex geometry into robotics code. Workflow from design to robotic fabrication using additive and subtractive techniques. Development of architectural components like columns and facade panels.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will explore merging additive and subtractive manufacturing through robotics fabrication. It will cover the basics of fabrication-based geometric design, robotics 3D printing, and six-axes robotics milling. We will cover the basics of geometry tool path translation into points and planes and the translation of points and planes into robotics code. It is an attempt to speculate on ecological components and fabrication-based design that is only guided by the potentials and the limitations of the fabrication tools as well as promoting eco-friendly materiality through digital design and robotics fabrication. This workshop will focus on designing architectural components such as facade panels, columns, and structural components. Participants must have advanced knowledge of Rhino and basic knowledge of Grasshopper. The workshop will introduce the KUKA PRC Grasshopper plugin to simulate and operate the KUKA robotic arms directly. This workshop will cover three primary topics within digital design and robotics fabrication: Natural Material Hybrids: We will discuss the ecology and behavior of natural materials, their structural properties, and their influence on robotics and digital fabrication. Multi-materiality: We will discuss the transitional phase that requires us to hybridize naturally with synthetic materials in a component-based architecture and its aesthetic implications for design and functionality. 3D Resolution through Fabrication: We will explore the role of toolpathing as a design methodology, enhancing the autonomy of digital fabrication tools, particularly robotics.
source_fields.notes: Students must have all the software ready before the workshop! Be Prepared to work in groups of 2- 4 participants. We will have at least 30 minutes of discussion for all participants before the beginning of the tutorial to brainstorm and start forming groups. We will have 30 minutes at the end of day 1 for assignment briefs and questions. At the end of Day 2, there will be 30 minutes for Q&A and closing remarks of the workshop.

source_fields.faq: What is the difference between additive and subtractive robotic fabrication in architecture? :: Additive robotic fabrication, such as robotic 3D printing, builds up material layer by layer based on a programmed toolpath, allowing complex geometries and material hybridization to be constructed without formwork. Subtractive robotic fabrication, such as six-axis robotic milling, removes material from a block or composite mass using a cutting tool guided by toolpath data. In architecture, combining both within a single workflow allows designers to exploit the structural and aesthetic properties of each technique, which is the core focus of this workshop using KUKA robotic arms programmed through KUKA PRC and Grasshopper. || What does the EcoFusion: Robotic Manufacturing workshop at PAACADEMY cover? :: The workshop covers three interconnected topics: natural material hybrids, examining the ecology and structural behavior of natural materials and their influence on robotic fabrication; multi-materiality, exploring the hybridization of natural and synthetic materials in component-based architecture and its aesthetic and functional implications; and 3D resolution through fabrication, where toolpathing is treated as a design methodology rather than a post-design step. Participants learn fabrication-based geometric design, geometry-to-toolpath translation, and points-and-planes-to-robotics-code translation using KUKA PRC inside Grasshopper. || What prior experience do I need for the EcoFusion robotic fabrication workshop? :: Participants must have advanced knowledge of Rhinoceros 3D and at least basic familiarity with Grasshopper before the workshop begins. All software, including Rhinoceros, Grasshopper, KUKA PRC, and Termite, must be installed and ready before the first session. The workshop introduces KUKA PRC as the primary tool for simulating and operating KUKA robotic arms, so prior robotic fabrication experience is not required, but comfort with computational geometry in Rhino and Grasshopper is essential. || What will I produce through the EcoFusion robotic fabrication workshop? :: Working in groups of 2 to 4, participants will develop a set of architectural component designs, including facade panels, columns, or structural elements, developed through a fabrication-led workflow in Grasshopper with KUKA PRC simulation. The output includes geometry generated with robotic production constraints in mind, toolpath data translated into robotic code for KUKA arms, and design proposals that integrate natural and synthetic material hybridization as a core aesthetic and structural strategy.

source_fields.name: Advanced Grasshopper 2.0: Integrating Voxel and Mesh Modelling Approaches
source_fields.softwares: Dendro | Grasshopper 3D | Kangaroo | Ladybug | LunchBox | Pufferfish | Weaverbird
source_fields.introduction: Current design and architecture practice is highly adopted to use parametric modeling tools and procedural workflows. Such methods help designers to explore a wide range of outcomes for a defined design question. Conventionally, 3D software were limited to certain geometrical modifiers that could be used, but algorithmic modeling tools such as Grasshopper offer the possibility to develop custom modifiers in your design workflow. This workshop will comprehensively explore the Grasshopper environment and how this tool can be used for advanced 3d modeling procedures.
source_fields.description: This workshop explores advanced Grasshopper modeling techniques, focusing on integrating voxel and mesh approaches alongside essential data structures and mathematical operations.
source_fields.objectives: Fundamental understanding of algorithmic modeling in GH. Precise control of Data structure flow in Grasshopper. Apply mathematical operations and equations to create complex geometries, including foldable surfaces and structures. Utilize physics and force simulation tools to generate tensile and minimal surfaces. Explore mesh-based modeling plugins and strategies for designing intricate geometries and morphing surface patterns. Develop skills to identify and apply appropriate modeling methods (mesh, NURBS, or voxel-based) for different design challenges. Combine various Grasshopper tools and plugins to achieve advanced 3D modeling outcomes.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop will comprehensively explore several modeling methods in Grasshopper. First, we will go through the data structure in Grasshopper as it is the fundamental need for our next steps. Then, we will explore the use of mathematical operations and equations in Grasshopper. At this stage, we will practice modeling foldable surfaces and structures as they are well-related to mathematic operations. Physics and force simulation is the next part of this workshop, in which examples of tensile and minimal surfaces will be provided. Mesh-based modeling plugins and strategies will be covered to design complex geometries and morphing surface patterns. The other part of our workshop will focus in-depth on the voxel-based model and its integration. Students will work individually on their projects. This workshop will explore different ranges of Grasshopper tools and plugins; in terms of typologies, we will use three main methods to produce geometries, Mesh nurbs, and voxel-based objects. For each method, we will provide different examples, understand the difference between them, and have the ability to identify the appropriate use of each of them.

source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online conference. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced architectural design software, enabling you to create captivating materials and efficiently render projects. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What software and Grasshopper plugins will I need for this workshop? :: You will use Grasshopper 3D along with plugins including Dendro (for voxel modeling), Weaverbird (for mesh editing/refinement), Kangaroo (for physics simulations), Pufferfish , LunchBox , and Ladybug . || What distinct modeling approaches are covered, and how will I learn to choose between them? :: The workshop covers three primary geometric generation methods: NURBS , Mesh , and Voxel-based modeling . You will learn the structural differences between each approach to identify and apply the correct technique for specific architectural challenges. || How are mathematical equations and physics simulations integrated into the design workflow? :: You will apply mathematical formulas to model complex foldable structures and surfaces and use Kangaroo physics solvers to simulate forces to generate tensile and minimal surface forms. || What advanced surface pattern and growth simulation techniques will Platinum users learn? :: You will learn precise data structure and data flow control, morphing organic surface patterns, and implementing growth pattern simulations to generate adaptive, intricate geometries. || What practical outcomes can I expect to achieve by the end of the course? :: You will build a custom computational workflow combining voxel, mesh, and NURBS modeling strategies, giving you the skills to develop complex, multi-plugin 3D scripts for parametric architecture and digital fabrication.

courses.name: Additive Footwear Design: FDM and Resin

source_fields.name: Additive Footwear Design: FDM and Resin
source_fields.introduction: This workshop explores 3d printed footwear design using procedural tools, allowing students to create professional-level manufacturing-ready 3d models of the highest quality using Houdini and blender. Students will explore a wide range of manufacturing technologies, empowering them to unlock their full design potential.
source_fields.description: Additive Footwear Design workshop will focus on using Houdini and Blender to create professional 3D printable footwear designs optimized for FDM and Resin printing technologies.
source_fields.objectives: How to design footwear for FDM and Resin Manufacturing constraints for FDM and Resin footwear, as well as pros and cons for both Use Houdini to create an adjustable design Create textures that don’t cause overhangs Create lattices for specific materials Maintain constraints by translating textures into geometry
source_fields.methodology: In this workshop, we will use Sidefx Houdini and Blender to procedurally create 3d printable shoes that maintain manufacturing constraints through parametric methods. Participants will first learn how to model a simple shoe for FDM procedurally, then how to generate and apply textures so that overhangs are not created. Participants will submit their 3d models to the Zellerfeld Auto Check and fix common errors. In this workshop, we will translate the first design into something suitable for Resin (SLA, DLP) or Powder (MJF, SLS) printing. We will learn how to generate lattices for the said shoe for specific shore hardnesses of material. This workshop will teach participants how to use Houdini and Blender to design 3d printable shoes that may be printed using FDM, SLS, MJF, SLA, DLP, and other methods. The main focus will be FDM and SLA, but workflows will apply to most 3d printing technologies. Participants will be encouraged to print out their creations on their own or with a manufacturer. However, this is not compulsory, and any manufacturing costs are not included in the price and depend on the manufacturer and design.
source_fields.notes: Students are not required to print the shoes. Manufacturing costs are not included in the workshop price and depend on the manufacturer and design.
source_fields.certificate_text: As congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive workshop, this course offered in-depth insights into using Houdini and Blender for creating professional, manufacturing-ready 3D footwear designs optimized for FDM and Resin printing technologies, exploring advanced parametric design techniques, and mastering manufacturing constraints. Your dedication to learning these cutting-edge design and manufacturing methods is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: What software will I use throughout this workshop? :: You will use SideFX Houdini and Blender to procedurally model, texture, and optimize 3D-printable footwear designs. || What specific 3D printing technologies and materials are covered in the curriculum? :: The primary focus is on FDM and Resin (SLA, DLP) printing, while also exploring lattice and geometry workflows applicable to Powder-based technologies like SLS and MJF for different material shore hardnesses. || How will we ensure our footwear designs meet manufacturing constraints without support structures? :: You will learn to procedurally build shoe lasts, generate overhang-free textures, and run models through Zellerfeld Auto Check to fix common printing errors. || Are participants required to physically print their footwear creations? :: No, physical printing is not compulsory, and any optional manufacturing costs are separate from the workshop price. || What practical outcomes can I expect to achieve by the end of the course?] :: You will master an end-to-end procedural workflow to translate raw shoe concepts and textures into manufacturing-ready, 3D-printable footwear models.

courses.name: Parametric Workflows with Blender: Animating Robots for Digital Fabrication

source_fields.name: Parametric Workflows with Blender: Animating Robots for Digital Fabrication
source_fields.introduction: Learn to use Blender's Geometry Nodes to develop custom digital fabrication workflows. This hands-on workshop will teach you different approaches to developing tailored machine instructions, from drawing with plotters and cutting with CNCs to 3D printing and robotic fabrication.
source_fields.description: Parametric Workflows with Blender: Animating Robots for Digital Fabrication is a workshop covering procedural toolpath generation for 3D printing, CNC machining, and robotic arm control using Blender's Geometry Nodes system. Participants begin with Blender fundamentals and workspace setup, then progress to node-based toolpath creation for plotters and CNC machines before advancing to additive manufacturing and robotic fabrication workflows. The robotic section uses the Animaquina addon for multi-axis toolpath simulation and robotic arm animation within Blender. Safety protocols and fabrication constraints are addressed throughout. A final individual project integrates all techniques covered, and basic Blender 3D modeling experience is recommended.
source_fields.objectives: Develop toolpaths for 3D printers, CNC machines, and robotic arms usingBlender and Geometry Nodes. Harness the power of Geometry Nodes for parametric design. Utilize attributes to customize your toolpaths. Develop custom visualization and debugging tools for your projects. Troubleshoot common digital fabrication challenges. Apply your knowledge to real-world fabrication projects.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop will explore several digital fabrication workflows using Blender. We will begin by introducing the fundamentals of Blender's interface and navigation to ensure all participants are comfortable with the softwareenvironment. We'll set up a workspace tailored for digital fabrication tasks and familiarize ourselves with Blender. We will export some manually generated toolpaths to get conformable with blender's main interface. Next, we'll delve into Geometry Nodes, Blender's powerful system for procedural and parametric modeling. We'll explore how node-based workflows can generate toolpaths, and we'll practice creating toolpaths for drawing and cuttingapplications using plotters and CNC machines. We will then focus on 3D printing workflows. Starting with basic toolpath generation using Geometry Nodes to create optimized toolpaths for additive manufacturing. We'll address common 3D printing issues and constraints,ensuring that your designs are print-ready. The final part of our workshop will cover robotic fabrication workflows. We'll introduce Animaquina, a Blender addon for animating, simulating, and controlling robotic arms. You'll learn how to create multi-axis toolpaths suitable for robotic fabrication and understand the constraints and possibilities of working with robots. We'll also cover essential safety protocols and best practices in robotic fabrication. Throughout the workshop, we'll emphasize the use of attributes within Geometry Nodes to tailor and customize your toolpaths. Students will work individually on a final project that integrates the techniques covered in theworkshop.
source_fields.requirements: Basic Blender 3D modeling knowledge is highly recommended.
source_fields.notes: A curated list of online tutorials (1-2 hours) will be provided before the workshop. Please install all required software before the workshop begins. A computer with a numpad and 3-button mouse is strongly recommended. While not required, access to a 3D printer, CNC machine, or robot will allow for hands-on testing of your designs.
source_fields.day1_program: Session 1: Intro● Introduction to Blender 3D Modeling● Introduction to Geometry Nodes● Understanding Machine Code● Workspace setup● Design and generate 2D toolpaths for drawing or cutting● Exercise: Design your first toolpath (Parametric portrait)Session 2: 3D printing toolpaths● Basic 3D printing toolpaths● Advanced toolpaths with Geometry Nodes● Resolving common 3D printing issues● Exercise: Generate a 3D printing toolpath
source_fields.day2_program: Session 3: Working with Robots● Fundamentals of robotic fabrication and safety protocols● Introduction to Animaquina● Developing multi-axis toolpaths for robotic arms● Exercise: Simulate and visualize a robotic toolpathSession 4: Advanced workflows● Leveraging attributes as parameters for toolpath customization● Exploring real-time toolpathing methods● Final project: Design a complete fabrication workflow
source_fields.certificate_text: As congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive workshop, this course offered insights into using Blender and Geometry Nodes for creating custom digital fabrication workflows optimized for 3D printers, CNC machines, and robotic arms. You explored parametric design techniques, mastered toolpath customization, and developed solutions for fabrication challenges. Your dedication to these cutting-edge methods is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: What software and add-ons will I need to use for this workshop? :: You will use Blender alongside the Tissue add-on and Animaquina, a specialized add-on for animating, simulating, and controlling robotic arms. || What prior knowledge or hardware setup is recommended before joining? :: Basic Blender 3D modeling knowledge is highly recommended, and using a computer equipped with a numpad and a 3-button mouse is strongly advised. || What digital fabrication machines and toolpath workflows will be covered? :: You will learn to create custom toolpaths for plotters, CNC cutting machines, 3D printers, and multi-axis robotic arms using Blender’s Geometry Nodes. || How will we learn to simulate and control robotic arms inside Blender? :: You will use the Animaquina add-on to generate multi-axis robotic toolpaths, simulate movement, control robotic arms, and apply essential safety protocols for robotic fabrication. || What practical project will I build to apply these procedural fabrication techniques? :: You will work individually on a final project that integrates Geometry Nodes attributes to create tailored G-code and custom machine instructions for real-world fabrication.
