source_fields.name: Curvilinear Concepts 2.0: AI Exploration to Fabrication
source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: This workshop explores Midjourney to create interesting, invigorating, and curvilinear forms and 3D Modelling using Autodesk Maya, we will also learn to prepare files to fabricate models on Bambu Studio. In this workshop, the students will work on creating curvilinear architectural forms, much like MAD Architects/Zaha Hadid Architects (For reference only), using generative artificial intelligence and then use the generated form to create a unique geometry on a 3D Modelling tool, in particular, Rhino 3D and Autodesk Maya. Prompt-crafting using Midjourney develop concepts for sophisticated and complex building design, using an iterative process we will arrive at our desired results which can be highly iterative for precise results. We will also explore how we can set up a file on a Digital Fabrication/3D Printing software like Bambu Studio. A few examples, which include a high-density housing complex, a Google campus, etc.
source_fields.description: Curvilinear Concepts 2.0: AI Exploration to Fabrication is a workshop that teaches designers to generate curvilinear, MAD- and ZHA-inspired architectural forms with Midjourney and turn them into fabrication-ready 3D models. Students replicate and refine AI-generated forms through procedural polygon modeling in Autodesk Maya and line-drawing-based modeling in Rhino, then prepare files in Bambu Studio for 3D printing, setting up supports, materials, print speed, and scale. The workshop is Beginner level and results in a clean, 3D-printable curvilinear design.
source_fields.objectives: Generate curvilinear forms using Midjourney Explore design styles inspired by MAD Architects and ZHA Master prompt-crafting for architectural concepts Create 3D geometry in Rhino 8 and Autodesk Maya Learn procedural polygon modeling in Maya Build 3D models from line drawings in Rhino Prepare models for digital fabrication in Bambu Studio Set up supports, materials, print speed, and scale for 3D printing
source_fields.methodology: In this workshop we will use Midjourney to create curvilinear or fluid forms, this can be from product to city scale and then we will use the generated form and replicate/modify it on Autodesk Maya/Rhinoceros, we will then proceed to set up a part or full file on Bambu Studio to learn how we can 3D Print models depending on scale from product to building scale. We will make sure that our geometry is clean, easy to handle, and 3D Printable. The students will be given a general tutorial on how to use Midjourney and then given time to generate interesting, complex, and sophisticated forms/images on Midjourney, most likely a large-scale architectural project. Each student can focus on developing different parts of the project, for example: Façade, Landscaping, Interiors, Furniture, Lighting, Textures, etc. We will quickly dive into Maya and/or Rhinoceros initially to get the hang of the tool with a specific form, procedural 3D Modelling from a primitive polygon, or using Rhino 3D from line drawing to 3D Model using simple commands to come up with a very interesting form. Thereafter, the exercise will be combinatorial, using the generated form and replicating/altering it on the 3D Modelling tool. The students will then learn to set up the file on Bambu Studio to prepare for digital fabrication/slicing with details such as support, material, print speed, and scale taken into consideration.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course explored the integration of AI and 3D modeling tools to generate curvilinear architectural forms, guiding you through Midjourney concept creation, modeling in Rhino and Maya, and preparing designs for fabrication in Bambu Studio. Your dedication to mastering these interdisciplinary design and fabrication techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What will I learn to create with AI-driven curvilinear design? :: You’ll learn to use Midjourney to generate and iteratively refine complex curvilinear architectural forms, from product-scale concepts to large-scale building designs. || Which 3D modeling software will I use to turn AI concepts into geometry? :: You’ll work with Autodesk Maya to replicate or modify AI-generated forms, including procedural polygon modeling in Maya and creating 3D models from line drawings in Rhino. || Will I learn how to prepare my architectural models for 3D printing? :: Yes, you’ll use Bambu Studio to prepare models for digital fabrication, considering supports, materials, print speed, scale, and clean, printable geometry. || What type of design project can I develop during the workshop? :: The workshop focuses on sophisticated curvilinear architectural forms, with examples including high-density housing and a Google campus, and participants can explore elements such as facades, interiors, landscaping, furniture, and lighting. || What is the complete workflow covered in the workshop? :: You’ll follow a hands-on process from Midjourney prompt-crafting and AI concept generation through Rhino or Maya modeling to Bambu Studio preparation for 3D printing.

source_fields.name: Design-Tech Talk 7.0
source_fields.instructors: Hamid Hassanzadeh | Cosimo Scotucci | IOUS Studio | Leonardo Nuevo Arenas
source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: Join us for Design-Tech Talk, an exclusive and engaging panel discussion featuring distinguished experts, each offering unique insights into the latest advancements in architecture, design innovation, and emerging technologies reshaping industries today. This dynamic event will explore the intersection of these fields, with each expert delivering a one-hour presentation that provides an in-depth look at the transformative potential of architectural design, the role of AI in shaping the future of design, and the groundbreaking capabilities of 3D printing in revolutionizing the way we build and create. Don’t miss this chance to engage with innovators who are pushing the boundaries of creativity and technology, driving change in architecture, design, and beyond. Whether you're a professional, student, or simply passionate about the future of design, Design-Tech Talk promises to inspire and equip you with the insights needed to navigate the exciting future of these fields. Program: Day 1 - Saturday, November 8th Opening session: 18:00 - 18:15 GMT 1st Speaker: Cosimo Scotucci 18:15 - 19:15 GMT Closing session: 19:15 - 19:30 GMT Day 2 - Sunday, November 9th Opening session: 16:00 - 16:15 GMT 1st Speaker: IOUS Studio 16:15 - 17:15 GMT 2nd Speaker: Leonardo Nuevo-Arenas 17:30 - 18:30 GMT Closing session: 18:30 - 18:45 GMT Cosimo Scotucci Cosimo Scotucci is a Rotterdam-based architect, artist, and innovator. He works to contribute to a more resilient world through speculative design, exploring how architecture can reshape ecosystems. Since 2016, he has been a Senior Project Leader and Architect at MVRDV, where he leads projects from concept to execution. His portfolio includes large-scale cultural, residential, and mixed-use developments in China and Taiwan. Scotucci’s work emphasizes sustainability, adaptive reuse, and the integration of public and cultural programs within dynamic urban contexts, reflecting his vision for thoughtful and future-focused architecture. IOUS Studio IOUS Studio is an architecture and design studio specializing in emerging technologies, computational design, and digital fabrication. Founded in 2023 in Rotterdam, it explores new architectural possibilities through 3D printing and innovative materials. The studio has collaborated with leading companies and exhibited worldwide, gaining recognition in prominent publications. Led by Argentine-born, Netherlands-based architect duo Sol Sanchez Cimarelli and Agustin Ros, both graduates of Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, IOUS Studio merges a multidisciplinary, high-tech approach with global expertise. Their work spans architecture, interiors, pavilions, and installations, redefining design through technology, customization, and sustainability. Committed to innovation, IOUS Studio envisions the future of architecture as dynamic, experimental, and impactful. Leonardo Nuevo-Arenas Leonardo Nuevo-Arenas is the Head of Computational Design at Kinetica, where he leads the integration of algorithmic workflows, digital fabrication, and robotic manufacturing. Trained as an industrial designer, he belongs to Latin America’s first generation of computational design practitioners. At Kinetica, he established the Computational Design Department, developing custom processes that bridge architectural vision with precision manufacturing. Leonardo has collaborated with leading firms such as Foster + Partners, Zaha Hadid Architects, Heatherwick Studio, and AS+GG, and is an active educator and speaker across Latin America.

courses.name: Chad Oppenheim - Rethinking Architecture

source_fields.name: Chad Oppenheim - Rethinking Architecture
source_fields.introduction: In a world where cities grow denser and landscapes face unprecedented pressures, the role of architecture has never been more critical. Architecture today is not only about creating buildings, it is about designing with empathy, responding to climate, culture, and community while crafting spaces that resonate emotionally. The most forward-thinking architects are blurring boundaries between the natural and the built, shaping environments that restore our connection to the earth.
source_fields.description: Chad Oppenheim - Rethinking Architecture is a free lecture in which Chad Oppenheim, founding principal of Oppenheim Architecture, shares his design philosophy and project inspirations. The one-hour session includes a 45-minute talk followed by a 15-minute live Q&A, covering how empathy, climate response, and a deep connection to place shape his firm's hospitality, residential, and cultural projects worldwide. The lecture is free to attend and open to all levels.
source_fields.methodology: Chad Oppenheim, founder of Oppenheim Architecture, is one of the most influential voices at the intersection of design and ecology. Known for projects that celebrate the poetry of place, his work embraces simplicity, authenticity, and the timeless relationship between human beings and nature. Whether it’s a resort carved into the cliffs of the Middle East or a home seamlessly merging into the Florida landscape, Oppenheim’s architecture tells stories that transcend function. Join us on October 10th at 13:00 GMT as PAACADEMY hosts Chad Oppenheim for an exclusive 45-minute open talk, followed by a 15-minute live Q&A. During the session, he will walk us through some of his most iconic projects, sharing the inspirations, ideas, and processes that guide his practice.
source_fields.notes: An active membership is required to watch the event's recording.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our online conference. This conference explored the evolving role of architecture in fostering deeper connections among people, nature, and place. Through inspiring presentations and discussions, you gained valuable insights into site-specific design, ecological thinking, and the creation of meaningful, context-driven architecture. Your commitment to expanding your architectural knowledge and engaging with innovative design philosophies is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: What is this lecture about? :: The lecture explores Chad Oppenheim's design philosophy, covering how empathy, climate response, and cultural context shape architecture that blurs the boundary between the natural and the built environment. || Who is speaking? :: Chad Oppenheim, founding principal of Oppenheim Architecture, a Miami- and Basel-based practice recognized with over 90 industry awards, including the AIA Silver Medal. The session is hosted by Hamid Hassanzadeh. || Is this lecture free, and do I need prior architecture knowledge? :: Yes, the lecture is free to attend and set at Beginner level, so no prior architecture background is required.

courses.name: Multimodal Architecture: Context Creation with AI

source_fields.name: Multimodal Architecture: Context Creation with AI
source_fields.introduction: Multimodal Architecture: Context Creation is a compact, production-oriented workshop that turns today’s fragmented multimodal stack into a clear, controllable pipeline for early-stage design. You’ll author design rules in plain language and convert them into workable constraints, build proto-projects, and place them on real sites with environmental and geometric controls. The workshop will focus on Formas.ai (basic plan included), with Processing for interactive tests, concise ComfyUI demos to read node graphs, and LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok) to push conceptual depth while staying grounded in structure, material, and space. You will orchestrate prompts, masks, depth, and point clouds, then shape lighting, texture, and shot sequence to produce clear narrative fragments.
source_fields.description: Multimodal AI means using different types of AI input together — images, text, data, and drawings — rather than relying on a single tool. This workshop teaches architects and designers how to move from site conditions through concept generation to a developed design proposal using a coordinated multimodal AI workflow, where each stage feeds the next rather than operating in isolation.
source_fields.objectives: Author constraint-driven concepts using natural-language “rule sets” that control massing, hierarchy, material intent, and geometry. Contextualize proposals on real sites using site cues, program, topography, scale, and circulation to move from proto-ideas to context-driven schemes. Shape atmosphere and narrative with lighting, materials, and camera logic to communicate intent in stills and short videos. Bridge sketched, 2D to 3D spatial data by transforming different media to point clouds for volumetric checking, spatial cues, and camera planning.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop follows a hands-on, iterative methodology that combines natural-language rule authoring with multimodal workflows across text, image, video, and 3D data. Participants move from abstract constraints to tangible proto-projects, situating them in real contexts using site and environmental cues. By alternating between conceptual exploration in LLMs, interactive testing in Processing, and structured design development in Formas.ai, the process emphasizes rapid translation of ideas into controlled design outputs. Program: Day 1: Concept and Contextualization Overview The first day introduces the spectrum of multimodal models such as text, image, video, point clouds, and image-to-3D. Participants will receive access to the Formas.ai platform (basic plan) and explore how to use it in combination with Processing for interactive elements. Brief demonstrations of ComfyUI workflows will provide insight into advanced pipelines. We’ll also introduce large language models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok) as conceptual development tools. Content Concept Creation + Instant Interfaces Hands-on exploration of “fluid” or “instant” interfaces. Using natural language to define constraints and rules. Early materialization of conceptual designs through rules and design constraints. Turning Concepts into Proto-Projects Developing fast, low-resolution design experiments from the constraints and rules defined earlier. Iterating through multiple options to test feasibility and expression before full contextualization. Beyond Images: Context Creation Situating projects within contextual, site, and environmental constraints. Transitioning from proto-projects to fully context-driven design proposals. Day 2: Narrative and Atmosphere Creation Overview The second day shifts focus toward storytelling and atmosphere. We’ll use video-based workflows to shape design narratives, refine stylistic choices, and create immersive atmospheres. Emphasis will be on interior mood-making through light, material, and detail, while also extending into point cloud and 3D-based workflows. Content Narrative and Style Development Using video models to build and control design narrative: Timelapses, Constructive Sequences, Design Rationale, Building in use. Crafting interior atmospheres by combining light, texture, and stylistic elements. Moodboard, furniture. Personal touch: training our own model sets and applications. Point Cloud and 3D Integration Converting images into point clouds for immersive spatial exploration. Contextual creation in 3D : world generations. Applying point clouds and image-to-3D models in design scenarios.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into multimodal design workflows for early-stage architecture, enabling you to craft context-aware narratives and generate spatial visuals across text, image, video, and 3D workflows. Your dedication to mastering these cutting-edge methods in Formas.ai for concept development and visual reasoning is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What is Multimodal Architecture: Context Creation about? :: This workshop shows how to turn natural-language rules and multimodal tools into clear, context-driven design workflows. || How is the workshop structured? :: Day 1 focuses on concept creation, proto-projects, and site context; Day 2 develops narrative, atmosphere, and 3D point cloud integration. || Which software will we use? :: Mainly Formas.ai (basic plan will be provided), plus Processing for interactive tests and LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok) for concept development. || What skills will participants gain? :: You’ll learn to author design rules, contextualize projects on real sites, shape atmosphere with materials and lighting, and transform sketches into 3D point clouds. || Who is this workshop for? :: This workshop is designed for architects and designers eager to explore AI and multimodal tools in the early stages of architectural design.

courses.name: Reverse Modeling: AI-Inspired Architecture

source_fields.name: Reverse Modeling: AI-Inspired Architecture
source_fields.introduction: Dream to Reality: AI-Powered Architecture explores how artificial intelligence can amplify human creativity, while maintaining precision and design intent. This hands-on workshop guides participants through a workflow that starts with AI-generated imagery using MidJourney, moves into Rhino SubD modeling, and culminates in Krea visualization. By combining generative AI with parametric and manual modeling, participants will learn to reverse-engineer AI concepts into buildable, detailed 3D architectural models, bridging the gap between imagination and execution.
source_fields.description: Reverse Modeling: AI-Inspired Architecture is a course that teaches architects to transform AI-generated concepts into precise 3D models and refined visualizations using Midjourney, Rhino SubD, and Krea. Students generate architectural concepts in Midjourney, reverse-engineer that imagery into detailed SubD models in Rhino with iterative MIRO board feedback, then render and refine outputs with Krea and Nano Banana to balance AI aesthetics with human design decisions. The course is Beginner level and results in a buildable, detailed 3D architectural model.
source_fields.objectives: Generate and explore architectural concepts using AI-driven imagery. Reverse-engineer AI concepts into detailed 3D models using Rhino SubD. Create high-quality visualizations with Krea , integrating AI and human design thinking. Apply a structured workflow from ideation to execution, blending AI creativity with human precision. Critically evaluate AI outputs and translate them into actionable architectural designs.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop follows a step-by-step, practice-driven approach, emphasizing active learning and iterative feedback: 1. AI Ideation (MidJourney) Participants generate a variety of architectural concepts using AI prompts. Exploration and experimentation are documented via a shared MIRO board, enabling collaborative feedback. 2. Reverse Engineering into 3D (Rhino SubD) AI-generated imagery is analyzed and translated into precise 3D models. Emphasis on SubD modeling techniques to capture organic and complex forms. Continuous feedback is provided through MIRO reviews to refine designs in real time. 3. Visualization & Refinement (Krea / Gemini Studio) Models are rendered and enhanced using Nano Banano (Krea / Gemini Studio) for high-quality architectural visualization. Participants learn to balance AI aesthetics with human design decisions. Iterative review ensures designs evolve with both technical accuracy and creative vision. The methodology is interactive, blending lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on exercises, with constant instructor feedback to guide participants from concept to fully realized 3D visualizations.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into transforming AI-generated architectural concepts into precise 3D forms, guiding you through MidJourney ideation, Rhino SubD modeling, and Krea-based visualization. Your dedication to mastering this advanced workflow and refining AI-inspired designs into buildable models is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: Which software and AI tools are used in this course? :: The course uses Midjourney for AI concept generation, Rhino SubD for reverse-engineering those concepts into 3D models, and Krea.AI together with Nano Banana for final visualization and refinement. || What does the curriculum cover? :: The workflow moves through three stages: AI ideation in Midjourney with collaborative feedback on a shared MIRO board, reverse-engineering that imagery into precise SubD models in Rhino, and rendering and refining those models with Krea and Nano Banana. || Is this course suitable for beginners? :: Yes. The course is set at Beginner level and follows a step-by-step, practice-driven approach with constant instructor feedback, so no prior AI or advanced Rhino experience is required. || What will I produce by the end of the course? :: A buildable, detailed 3D architectural model that reverse-engineers an AI-generated concept, complete with a refined, presentation-ready visualization.

courses.name: Sanjay Puri - Rethinking Architecture

source_fields.name: Sanjay Puri - Rethinking Architecture
source_fields.introduction: In a rapidly transforming world where climate, culture, and community demand equal attention, architecture must move beyond form to embody responsibility. For Sanjay Puri, design is about more than aesthetics — it is about responding to context, embracing local traditions, and creating spaces that are inherently sustainable. His projects are sculptural yet deeply rooted in place, shaped by climate responsiveness and cultural memory.
source_fields.description: Sanjay Puri - Rethinking Architecture is a free lecture in which Sanjay Puri, founder and principal architect of Sanjay Puri Architects, shares his design philosophy and award-winning projects. The one-hour session includes a 45-minute talk followed by a 15-minute live Q&A, covering how climate responsiveness, local tradition, and sculptural form-making shape his firm's residential, cultural, and institutional work across India. The lecture is free to attend and open to all levels.
source_fields.methodology: From large-scale townships to intimate cultural spaces, Puri’s work redefines Indian architecture on a global stage, proving that innovation and sustainability can coexist with bold form-making. Each project is a narrative of light, material, and environment, a dialogue between the built and the unbuilt. Join us on October 24th at 13:00 GMT as PAACADEMY hosts Sanjay Puri for an exclusive 45-minute open talk, followed by a 15-minute live Q&A. During the session, he will share his design philosophy and walk us through some of his most iconic projects, offering insights into how architecture can be both visionary and deeply contextual.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our online conference. This conference explored the evolving role of architecture in responding to climate, culture, and community through innovative and context-driven design. Through inspiring presentations and discussions, you gained valuable insights into sustainable architecture, climate-responsive design, and the integration of local identity with bold architectural expression. Your commitment to expanding your architectural knowledge and engaging with forward-thinking design philosophies is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: What is this lecture about? :: The lecture explores Sanjay Puri's design philosophy, covering how climate responsiveness, cultural context, and sustainability shape sculptural, site-rooted architecture across residential, cultural, and institutional projects. || Who is speaking? :: Sanjay Puri, founder and principal architect of Sanjay Puri Architects, a Mumbai-based firm recognized internationally for redefining Indian architecture through contextual, sustainable design. The session is hosted by Hamid Hassanzadeh. || Is this lecture free, and do I need prior architecture knowledge? :: Yes, the lecture is free to attend and set at Beginner level, so no prior architecture background is required.

courses.name: Architectural Intelligence: From Prompt to Concept with Snaptrude AI

source_fields.name: Architectural Intelligence: From Prompt to Concept with Snaptrude AI
source_fields.introduction: This intensive workshop reveals how Snaptrude's intelligent design tools can transform your workflow from concept to presentation. Learn to use AI-powered features for faster, smarter design processes that actually work. Module 1: Introduction and Snaptrude AI Mode: Start Smarter Learn how to go from a simple text prompt to a working building concept. Explore techniques for refining prompts, ensuring compliance, adjacency planning, and testing layouts. Participants will experiment with multiple iterations, learn prompting best practices, and generate varied outputs. Module 2: Snaptrude Design Mode: Taking Control & Designing Move beyond AI-mode into Snaptrude Design Mode, where participants will begin detailed design using Snaptrude’s powerful tools. This workshop will teach you how to navigate and model effectively, refine area planning and adjacencies, and apply advanced features such as sunlight analysis, toposolid imports, and refine exterior facades. Module 3: Snaptrude Program Mode and BIM Mode: Design meets Data With Snaptrude’s Program Mode, participants will learn advanced skills on how to structure and manage live-linked tables with departments, spaces, and area targets. With BIM mode, they will learn how to transition sketches and massing into fully developed BIM models, along with advanced features on using room templates for rapid iteration and adding furniture from libraries. Module 4: Snaptrude Presentation Mode (Program to Proposal) This module focuses on transforming design outputs into compelling client presentations. Participants will learn to create renders and walkthroughs, auto-generate diagrams and inspirations, and integrate program data, analysis, and design into a cohesive client presentation ready for delivery.
source_fields.description: Architectural Intelligence: From Prompt to Concept with Snaptrude AI is a free course that teaches architects Snaptrude's AI-powered workflow from prompt-based concepts to BIM-ready models. Across four modules, students generate building massing from text prompts in AI Mode, refine area planning, sunlight analysis, and facades in Design Mode, structure live-linked program data and develop full BIM models with room templates and furniture libraries, then produce renders, walkthroughs, and client-ready presentations in Presentation Mode. The course is Beginner level and free to attend.
source_fields.objectives: Generate and refine building concepts with prompt engineering. Move from AI outputs to detailed design in Snaptrude. Manage data-driven design through Program Mode to BIM Mode. Create client-ready presentations with renders and walkthroughs. Streamline workflows to cut effort and boost collaboration.
source_fields.methodology: We will adopt a hands-on, project-based learning approach tailored for architects and designers who want to integrate AI seamlessly into their workflows. While each module provides a structured framework, participants will have the freedom to experiment with prompts, design strategies, and presentation techniques that align with their own project interests. The workflow is designed to move progressively from AI-assisted ideation to detailed design, data structuring, BIM integration, and final client presentations. Each step builds on the previous one, ensuring participants develop both confidence and fluency in moving across Snaptrude’s modes. Collaborative discussions, peer feedback, and guided Q&A sessions will reinforce key concepts and best practices. By the end of the workshop, participants will have gained practical experience in transforming their work into compelling client-ready deliverables. This methodology not only minimizes repetitive manual tasks but also helps participants focus on what matters most- designing with creativity and precision.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into Snaptrude’s AI-powered workflow, guiding you from prompt-based ideation to BIM-ready models. Your dedication to mastering these intelligent design techniques throughout this workshop is commendable.

courses.name: AI-Powered Design Ideation: Midjourney, mnml & Nano Banana

source_fields.name: AI-Powered Design Ideation: Midjourney, mnml & Nano Banana
source_fields.introduction: Imagine being able to transform your imagination into vivid design concepts within minutes. This workshop shows you how. AI-Powered Design Ideation is a hands-on journey into the future of creative design, where artificial intelligence becomes your collaborative partner. This workshop will explore cutting-edge tools – Midjourney for generating stunning visuals from simple text, Nano Banana for magically editing images with a few words, and harnessing the power of Stable Diffusion in a visual node-based workflow. These specific platforms were chosen because they represent the forefront of AI in design: Midjourney excels at rapid concept generation, Nano Banana offers intuitive image manipulation, and gives you unparalleled control over AI image outputs. Whether you’re a student or a seasoned professional, learning these AI-driven techniques will supercharge your creativity and efficiency in the design process. This Workshop provides practical skills grounded in real-world architectural vision. By the end, you’ll understand why AI tools are becoming indispensable in ideation and how to wield them to bring your ideas to life.
source_fields.description: AI-Powered Design Ideation: Midjourney, mnml & Nano Banana is a course that teaches designers AI-driven ideation workflows for architecture and spatial design. Students use Midjourney for text-to-image and image-to-image concept generation, Nano Banana for inpainting and targeted image edits, and mnml.ai's Stable Diffusion-based node workflow for controlled outputs, with optional SketchUp integration for combining 3D massing with AI visualization. The course is Beginner level and results in a complete AI-driven concept presentation, developed solo or in a small team.
source_fields.objectives: Craft effective prompts in Midjourney for rapid concept generation Use Nano Banana for inpainting and AI-powered image editing Explore image-to-image and hybrid AI workflows Integrate AI with sketches and basic 3D models Develop a complete AI-driven concept design Gain confidence using emerging AI design tools
source_fields.methodology: This workshop focuses on conceptual design and ideation across architecture and spatial design. We will delve into creating visionary designs – from futuristic architectural facades and imaginative pavilions to artistic interior scenes or even urban interventions – using a diverse array of AI tools. You’ll get insight into generative workflows that can be applied to any design typology, with a focus on early-stage concept development. Using Midjourney, we will generate broad creative visions and mood boards at the click of a button, exploring styles ranging from photorealistic to abstract. Nano Banana, Google’s latest AI image editor, will be introduced as a way to fine-tune and tweak images by simply highlighting parts and describing changes – imagine changing the material or lighting of a render just by telling the AI what you want. The scope isn’t limited to purely digital workflows: we’ll also touch on integrating AI output with traditional design methods. For instance, we might use SketchUp (optional) to create a quick 3D massing or model and then feed it into our AI tools for further visualization, or take an AI-generated image and interpret its form in a 3D model. By covering a range of design approaches, from AI-generated imagery to basic 3D modeling, the workshop demonstrates how AI can fit into and enhance your existing design process rather than replace it. Expect a creative, exploratory atmosphere – this is about experimenting with new possibilities in design and finding innovative visual directions for your projects. We adopt a learn-by-doing methodology that keeps you actively engaged from start to finish. Short lectures and demonstrations will introduce each tool and workflow, but the core of the workshop is interactive practice. We’ll walk through several distinct AI-driven workflows step by step: Text-to-Image Ideation: You’ll start by writing simple text prompts in Midjourney to instantly generate diverse concept images. This workflow helps kickstart the imagination – you can produce multiple ideas in minutes and then zero in on the promising ones. Image-to-Image Transformation: Next, we’ll introduce how to build on existing content. For example, you can sketch a rough outline of a building or upload a basic SketchUp model screenshot, and then use Midjourney’s variations to reinterpret and refine that initial idea. This teaches you to guide the AI with a design you’ve begun, marrying human intuition with machine creativity. Inpainting & AI Editing: We’ll use Nano Banana's inpainting capabilities to modify specific parts of images. Is there a detail in your AI-generated render you don’t like? You’ll learn to mask it and change it – perhaps swap out the sky for a sunset, change a facade material, or add trees and people – all by instructing the AI. This workflow is incredibly powerful for iterating and polishing your concepts without starting over each time. Diverse Workflow Integration: Throughout, we emphasize that there’s no one “right” way – often the best results come from hybrid workflows. You might start in Midjourney, touch up with Nano Banana, and even loop back to sketching or modeling. We’ll demonstrate how to blend these tools seamlessly to suit different design needs. For instance, one workflow might be generating concept art in Midjourney and then using it as a style reference in Stable Diffusion to apply that style to another shape or model. Collaboration and Creative Freedom: For the final project, you will have full freedom to decide whether to work solo or form a small team. We encourage collaboration for those who want to brainstorm together, but individual exploration is equally supported. The instructor will be continuously available to guide and support both individuals and groups as needed. The workshop is very much hands-on and iterative: try something, see the results, then iterate or pivot to a new approach. We want you to leave not just with cool images, but with a robust understanding of how those images were generated and how you can incorporate these AI techniques into your daily design toolkit. Every step of the way, real-world tips and best practices will be shared – from crafting effective prompts to dealing with common AI quirks – ensuring you gain practical skills alongside creative confidence. One intensive day split into two sessions (4 hours each, plus short breaks). Mixed-level workshop: suitable for both beginners and experienced designers. Session 1: Foundations of AI Creativity Inspiration & Overview (Lecture/Demo): Kick off with how AI is transforming design ideation, with examples of architecture and products created using Midjourney and Stable Diffusion. Midjourney Hands-on Basics: Set up access and practice prompt-crafting live. Experiment with different prompt styles, from simple descriptive phrases to complex stylistic references, and generate a gallery of concept images. Learn how keywords like “ultramodern,” “wooden pavilion,” or artist names can change outcomes. Experimentation & First Project Ideation: Choose a theme (e.g., “futuristic cabin in the woods” or “floating city pavilion”) and apply what you’ve learned. Generate styles and moods in Midjourney, then refine or evolve them. Session 2: Advanced Workflows & Final Concept Development Advanced Techniques Demo: Explore image-to-image generation and Nano Banana inpainting. Learn to remove objects, change façade styles, and control randomness with seeds for design continuity. Integrating SketchUp (Optional): See how simple models can enhance AI workflows. Capture a view of a massing model and feed it into Midjourney to combine spatial geometry with AI-driven aesthetics. (Optional – participants not using SketchUp continue refining with AI.) Final Project Work Session: Guided studio time to finalize your concept. Generate last images, edit, or apply style transfers, and assemble your presentation. Work solo or in teams; the instructor will provide feedback and technical guidance. By session’s end, you’ll have a complete set of images or boards representing your AI-augmented design. Presentations & Wrap-up: Share your outcomes, discuss effective workflows, and celebrate progress. Open discussion on lessons learned, real-world applications, and tips for continued skill development. Leave inspired and ready to apply AI in future projects. Note: The schedule may be adjusted to match the group’s pace, ensuring no one is left behind.

courses.name: SubD Intelligence: Architectural Modeling & AI Rendering

source_fields.name: SubD Intelligence: Architectural Modeling & AI Rendering
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Artificial Intelligence | Visualization
source_fields.introduction: This intensive two-day workshop dives into the power of SubD modeling in Rhino, real-time visualization with Enscape, and the integration of AI tools to enhance architectural workflows. Through a blend of theoretical introductions and guided hands-on exercises, participants will develop a conceptual design from scratch, refining complex geometries and producing compelling renderings using cutting-edge tools. Whether you’re new to SubD or looking to elevate your visualization game, this workshop offers a structured pathway to mastering both form generation and presentation techniques in a short timeframe.
source_fields.description: SubD Intelligence is a two-day course on PAACADEMY that teaches SubD modeling in Rhinoceros 3D, real-time visualization in Chaos Enscape, and AI-assisted rendering using ReRenderAI and Gemini. Participants develop a conceptual architectural design from scratch, applying SubD tools to create and refine complex forms, then set up materials, lighting, and camera views in Enscape before using AI tools to elevate the final rendered outputs. The course is suitable for both participants new to SubD and those looking to strengthen their visualization and presentation workflow.
source_fields.objectives: Create and edit complex forms using Rhino’s SubD tools Develop a complete conceptual model through guided exercises Optimize geometry for rendering and visualization workflows Set up materials, lighting, and camera views in Enscape Enhance visual outputs with ReRenderAI and Gemini Produce polished final renderings ready for presentation
source_fields.methodology: The workshop emphasizes hands-on learning through a structured sequence of demonstrations, guided exercises, and individual exploration. Participants will follow a prepared parametric design example, applying SubD techniques step-by-step to build and refine their models. Key workflows will be demonstrated live, with time allocated for troubleshooting and personalized guidance. Once the geometry is finalized, the focus shifts to visualization, where participants will set up real-time rendering environments and experiment with AI tools to elevate their outputs.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into SubD modeling in Rhino, real-time visualization with Enscape, and the integration of AI tools like ReRenderAI and Gemini, enabling you to develop complex architectural forms and produce polished renderings. Your dedication to mastering these advanced techniques in both design and presentation is commendable.

source_fields.name: Dynamic Sketching 2.0: AI-Powered Architecture
source_fields.introduction: AI 3D Architecture Rendering 4.0 is not just a workshop; it’s a creative leap for architects, designers, and students who want to redefine the way they visualize and present their projects. In this hands-on experience, you’ll discover how to harness the most advanced AI tools integrated within 3D platforms to achieve exceptional rendering quality, dynamic animations, and cinematic post-production. From creating AI-generated assets to enhancing 3D scenes with professional-level detail, this workshop bridges design creativity with next-generation visualization workflows. Whether you work in architecture, interior design, or concept visualization, you’ll learn how to transform your static models into emotionally engaging visual stories that captivate clients and audiences alike. Say goodbye to traditional rendering routines and step into a new era where AI and 3D design merge to elevate your architectural storytelling.
source_fields.description: AI 3D Architecture Rendering 4.0 is not just a workshop; it’s a creative leap for architects, designers, and students who want to redefine the way they visualize and present their projects.
source_fields.objectives: D5 Render AI Techniques and Tricks. SketchUp AI Rendering Capabilities. 3D models and props are the best AI creation methods and platforms for 3d scenes. Advance AI Post Production for 3D Platform Renderings AI Image Upscaling Methods AI Render Animation Nano Banana AI Architecture Capabilities
source_fields.methodology: The workshop follows an intensive, hands-on methodology that combines guided instruction, real-time experimentation, and project-based learning. Participants will begin by exploring the integration of AI within 3D platforms through live demonstrations and practical exercises in tools such as D5 Render, Meshy AI, Rendair, and Tripo 3D. Each session progressively builds from asset generation to advanced post-production and animation workflows, allowing participants to experience the complete AI-enhanced visualization pipeline. Program: Day 1 The Future of AI-Driven 3D Visualization Session 1 – Introduction to AI Rendering and D5 Render Overview of AI integration in 3D architectural visualization. Learn D5 Render’s interface, AI-assisted lighting, materials, and real-time rendering features for high-quality visuals. Session 2 – AI 3D Model Generation with Meshy AI, Tripo 3D & Others Hands-on session using Meshy AI, Tripo 3D, Rodin, and Hitem 3D to generate 3D models, textures, and environments. Learn seamless integration into 3D design workflows. Session 3 – SketchUp AI Rendering Capabilities Practical exploration of SketchUp’s AI plugins and extensions such as SUAPP and Rendair. Enhance modeling, lighting, and composition for presentation-ready scenes. Day 2 From Static Renders to Animated Visualizations Session 4 – AI Post-Production for 3D Renderings Learn AI-enhanced post-production with ChatGPT and Rendair to upscale, relight, and apply cinematic effects for professional presentation results. Session 5 – AI Render Animation Techniques Explore AI-powered animation in D5 Render. Animate camera paths, environmental motion, and cinematic transitions to bring spaces to life. Session 6 – Nano Banana AI for Architecture Experiment with Nano Banana’s advanced AI visualization features to create interactive, experimental architectural outputs and expand design possibilities. By the end of the workshop, participants will have completed a full AI-based 3D rendering and animation pipeline from asset creation and rendering to post-production and motion. Mastering the most relevant tools shaping the future of architectural visualization.

source_fields.name: RunDiffusion: End-to-End AI Visuals for Architecture
source_fields.introduction: Learn end-to-end visualization workflows for architecture in RunDiffusion . In this free live event, you will build mood boards from references, iterate materials, form and tone, make precise image edits, and turn hero stills into short motion for client narratives. You will also train a lightweight style model for brand or office consistency and get clear guidance on licensing, permissions, and data protection. Leave with a finished board, an iteration set, a short video loop, and reusable presets and templates.
source_fields.description: RunDiffusion: End-to-End AI Visuals for Architecture is a free course that teaches architects and designers end-to-end AI visualization workflows in RunDiffusion. Students build reference-driven mood boards, iterate materials, form, and tone using seeds and presets, make targeted edits with masking and in/out-painting, and convert hero stills into short, loopable motion cuts for client previews, while also training a lightweight style LoRA for brand consistency and exploring Gaussian Splat 3D world generation. The course is Beginner level, free to attend, and includes an optional ComfyUI module for more granular control.
source_fields.objectives: Craft effective prompt scaffolds for architectural intent Understand the advantages and limitations of various models Manage seeds, versions, and presets for repeatable results Turn hero stills into short motion for client-ready loops Create a web viewer integration with Rhino and Google Maps Explore 3D worlds with Gaussian Splat
source_fields.methodology: You’ll work hands-on in RunDiffusion from start to finish: build a reference-driven mood board, craft a tight prompt scaffold, and run controlled iterations on materials, form, and tone using seeds, batches, and presets for repeatable results. You’ll make targeted edits—masking, in/out-painting, and global color/tone passes. In this workshop, you will convert 2–3 hero stills into a short, loopable motion cut for client previews. We’ll also demonstrate training a lightweight style LoRA (Flux Dev) for brand/office consistency and outline firm-ready practices for licensing, permissions, and data protection. Program: Rollout, Adoption + Enterprise Readiness Understanding decision-making in platform adoptions for a multinational company RunDiffusion Introduction to the platform, tools, boards, templates, features, and administrator controls. History of Image Diffusion How a deep understanding of the models can help understand the process and control outputs LoRA vs. the Prompt When and why to use LoRAs versus effective prompt structures. Vibe Code the World Fully AI-integrated workflow from image to building in Google Maps without leaving the browser. Gaussian Splat Explore and create Instant 3D worlds from a single or multiple images ComfyUI for Granular Control (optional) Batch prompts, seed control, model/LoRA swaps; export a reusable node-graph template. Q&A + Next Steps Assets hand-off; adoption checklist; follow-up resources.

Your dedication to mastering these end-to-end techniques—including precise image editing, iterative material refinement, and lightweight style model training is commendable.

source_fields.name: AI & Parametric Negotiation 2.0
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Artificial Intelligence | Visualization
source_fields.softwares: ComfyUI | Flux | Grasshopper 3D | Kling AI | Nano Banana | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: Generative AI as a technology is typically seen as a command-and-follow relationship. We rarely find a middle ground where the designer can employ the statistical probability of AI, and the AI can draw from the designer’s experience. This workshop continues our exploration of that balance between generative AI and parametric design, building on the pedagogy established in Part 1, where we converted parametric patterns into architectural space. In this workshop, we will push this methodology further with Video, specifically abstract pattern videos from Grasshopper, and convert them into architectural spaces. While doing this, we will also consider the site where our design proposal will be implemented, creating a flow from abstraction to design to on-site realization. The aim is neither to control AI fully nor to accept what it generates passively, but to cultivate a shared human-AI latent space in which both agents contribute to the design process. For detailed installation guides, please check the workshop’s Google Drive. To access it, click "Watch Now" → "Files" → "Download Course Files."
source_fields.description: AI & Parametric Negotiation 2.0 is a course that teaches designers to merge parametric design with generative AI, transforming Grasshopper animations into site-integrated architectural visuals. Building on Part 1's pedagogy, students convert abstract pattern videos into architectural renders inside ComfyUI using Flux, ControlNet, and IPAdapter, then upscale and composite selected frames onto real sites with Nano Banana before assembling a final video with Kling AI and Adobe Premiere Pro. The course is Beginner level and expects basic familiarity with Rhino3D, with no prior ComfyUI experience required.
source_fields.objectives: Explore how designers can create hybrid workflows with AI. Critically think about how much AI influence we want in our designs by controlling the inputs. Create a negotiable space between parametric design processes and AI tools. Learn the language and workflows that AI understands, and identify where its limitations arise. Understand how small changes in the workflow can drastically alter the output. Develop workflows connecting parametric modeling to site integration with AI. Build an iterative design mindset, redefining the role of architects and designers in the AI landscape.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop is designed for participants who are new to ComfyUI but have a basic understanding of Rhino3D. We will begin by exploring different generative AI models to identify which ones best suit our workflow. Newer models often produce higher-quality results but take longer to generate, while older models are faster but may compromise on quality. Participants will then create short animation sequences in Grasshopper and convert them into architectural spaces using AI models such as Flux, SDXL, and Gemini 2.5 inside ComfyUI. Throughout the process, we will use concepts like upscaling, ControlNet, IPAdapter, and image refinement. Finally, selected frames will be morphed onto real sites chosen by the participants. By the end of the workshop, participants will have developed an iterative workflow that connects parametric logic, generative AI interpretation, and contextual design visualization. The workshop aims to move beyond standalone generative AI tools and integrate them directly into design processes such as parametric modeling. Participants will use Grasshopper3D to create parametric animations, ComfyUI to convert those animations into architectural spaces placed on real sites, and Premiere Pro to combine them into cohesive video sequences. This workshop aims to move beyond standalone generative AI tools and integrate them directly into design processes such as parametric modeling. Participants will use Grasshopper3D to create parametric animations, ComfyUI to convert those animations into architectural spaces placed on real sites, and Premiere Pro to combine them into cohesive video sequences. Stage 1 | Parametric Animations Participants will learn key Grasshopper3D concepts like data trees, color coding, and wire connections, and explore how to animate frames using sliders and different plugins. In this stage, we will be working with abstract patterns, but participants can choose their own designs as well. The focus is on building an understanding of animation within the Grasshopper interface. Stage 2 | Animation to ComfyUI Render This stage introduces core AI concepts such as checkpoint models, VAEs, and prompts before translating Grasshopper frames into architectural renders using ComfyUI. Participants will use ControlNet models (Depth and Sketch) and IPAdapter to guide and style their outputs. Stage 3 | Render to Site Participants will select preferred designs and integrate them onto real sites using upscaling with SDXL and FLUX, followed by compositing through Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview. Image editing will refine lighting, weather, and time of day for contextual realism. Stage 4 | Combining in Adobe Premiere Pro Participants will bring their sequences together in Premiere Pro, learning basic editing, keyframing, adding text, and making video adjustments to create smooth animations. Program: Day 1 – Parametric Animation to Rough Architectural Space Tools: Rhino3D, Grasshopper3D (Plugin – Heteroptera), ComfyUI (SDXL Turbo, SDXL Depth + Sketch ControlNet, IPAdapter), Adobe Premiere Pro Generating Parametric Animation from Grasshopper Introduction to data trees, color coding, sliders, and wire connections Adjusting camera location for better output Extracting animation frames Animated Frames to Architectural Space Retaining the design language of animation using ControlNet Transferring style from an existing image with IPAdapter Combining Frames into Video in Adobe Premiere Pro Introduction to the Premiere Pro interface, importing stills, and learning key frames Adjusting motion properties to get a smooth animation Assignment 1 + Q&A Outcome: Final video output Day 2 – Site Implementation of the Design Tools: ComfyUI (Flux.1 Dev, Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana), Flux Kontext Max), Adobe Premiere Pro, Kling or WAN 2.2 Upscaling One Frame from Day 1 Cropping the image Comparing SDXL and FLUX upscaling methods Exploring denoising and image refinement concepts Merging the Upscaled Design with the Site Upscaling the site photograph Morphing the generated design onto the site context Image Editing Changing views, climate, or interior scene of the design Combining Everything Video generation with Kling or WAN 2.2 Combining in Adobe Premiere Pro Assignment 2 + Q&A Outcome: Final video and 3D model output

source_fields.name: Parametric Brickscapes: Grasshopper, Augmented Reality & AI
source_fields.introduction: Parametric Brickscapes is a two-day intensive workshop for beginners that bridges parametric design, augmented reality, and AI visualization into a single creative workflow. Participants will gain an understanding of parametric and geometric logic in Grasshopper, enabling them to design a fully parametric brick wall and translate code-based geometry into physical form through AR-guided assembly with Jenga blocks. The workshop concludes with an introduction to AI tools for transforming photographs of these physical prototypes into architectural renders and animated visuals - demonstrating how emerging workflows are evolving beyond traditional modeling. With AI now capable of visualizing atmosphere, context, and materiality directly from physical experiments, designers can explore new ways of thinking, building, and communicating form.
source_fields.description: Parametric Brickscapes is a 2-day beginner workshop on PAACADEMY that combines parametric design, augmented reality fabrication, and AI visualization into a single hands-on workflow. Using Grasshopper and Rhinoceros 3D, participants design rule-based brick wall systems, then translate them into physical Jenga block assemblies guided by Fologram AR, and finally use Midjourney to generate rendered and animated visuals from photographs of their prototypes. No prior Grasshopper experience is required.
source_fields.objectives: Understand the foundations of parametric design thinking and how to structure geometry using parameters, relationships, and data trees in Grasshopper. Develop a rule-based brick wall system, exploring how form, pattern, and density can be controlled computationally. Translate digital models into physical assemblies through AR-guided construction using Fologram and Jenga blocks. Capture and process physical prototypes into AI-based renders and animations using Midjourney, learning how to visualize atmosphere, context, and materiality without detailed digital modeling. Experience the complete digital-to-physical-to-AI workflow, gaining confidence in combining computational design, fabrication, and visualization tools.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop introduces students to the fundamentals of parametric design thinking through a complete, hands-on workflow — from digital modeling to physical prototyping and AI-based visualization. This workshop will focus on designing parametric brick wall systems using Grasshopper, exploring geometry, density, and pattern. These digital models will be translated into physical assemblies using Augmented Reality tools and Jenga blocks. The final phase introduces AI tools such as Midjourney to render and animate photographs of their prototypes—demonstrating how emerging technologies are reshaping how designers model, visualize, and communicate form. The workshop follows a hands-on, step-by-step methodology that guides participants through a complete digital-to-physical workflow. Students will begin by learning the fundamentals of parametric modeling in Rhino and Grasshopper, developing a rule-based brick wall system through iterative experimentation with parameters, data trees, and geometric logic. These digital models will then be translated into physical assemblies through AR-guided construction using Jenga blocks, and subsequently visualized using AI tools such as Midjourney to create rendered and animated outputs. All work will be conducted individually, allowing each participant to experience the full code-to-construction pipeline independently. Program: Day 1: Parametric Thinking and Digital Design The first day introduces participants to the fundamentals of parametric design using Rhino and Grasshopper. Students will learn how rule-based logic can generate adaptable systems, focusing on the design of a parametric brick wall as an entry point into computational thinking. Introduction and Setup Overview of the workshop objectives, outcomes, and tools Introduction to instructors and participant onboarding Foundations of Grasshopper Interface navigation and visual scripting logic Understanding data flow, parameters, and geometric relationships Parametric Brick Wall Design Developing rule-based wall systems Exploring variations in pattern, density, and form Preparing models for physical fabrication Day 2: Augmented Reality and AI Visualization The second day focuses on extending the digital model into physical and visual form through Augmented Reality fabrication and AI-based visualization workflows. Participants will experience how digital design, making, and image generation merge into a continuous design-to-reality process—bridging the gap between computational design and architectural communication. AR-Guided Fabrication Introduction to Fologram and setup for AR-based visualization Physical assembly of the parametric brick wall using Jenga blocks Discussion on the scalability of AR workflows and their real-world applications in on-site fabrication, installation, and full-scale construction AI Visualization and Animation Introduction to Midjourney and AI-based image generation Converting photographs of physical walls into architectural renders Generating short animated visualizations to explore atmosphere, context, and materiality Wrap-Up Discussion on evolving workflows from code to construction to visualization Reflection on outputs and insights for scaling these methods into architectural practice

source_fields.faq: What is Fologram and how is it used for augmented reality fabrication in architecture? :: Fologram is an augmented reality software that overlays digital geometry onto a physical space through a headset or mobile device, allowing designers and builders to use 3D models as real-time construction guides without paper drawings or traditional templates. In architecture and fabrication, Fologram is used for AR-guided assembly, formwork placement, installation verification, and on-site construction. In this workshop, Fologram is used to guide participants in physically assembling a parametric brick wall using Jenga blocks, with the Grasshopper model projected into the real environment as the assembly reference. || What does the Parametric Brickscapes workshop at PAACADEMY cover? :: Day 1 covers Grasshopper fundamentals including interface navigation, data flow, parameters, and geometric relationships, then moves into designing a rule-based parametric brick wall system with variations in pattern, density, and form. Day 2 introduces Fologram for AR-guided physical assembly of the digital brick wall using Jenga blocks, followed by an AI visualization session using Midjourney to transform photographs of the physical prototypes into architectural renders and short animated visualizations. The workshop closes with a discussion on scaling these workflows into real architectural practice. || Is this workshop suitable for beginners with no Grasshopper experience? :: Yes. The workshop is explicitly designed for beginners and introduces Grasshopper from the fundamentals in Day 1, covering visual scripting logic, data trees, and geometric relationships before building the parametric brick wall system. No prior parametric design or coding experience is required. Participants work individually throughout, allowing each person to progress through the full digital-to-physical-to-AI pipeline at their own pace with guided instruction. || What will I produce at the end of the Parametric Brickscapes workshop? :: By the end of the two days, participants will have a fully parametric brick wall model built in Grasshopper, a physically assembled prototype constructed with Jenga blocks using AR guidance through Fologram, and a set of AI-generated architectural renders and animated visualizations produced in Midjourney from photographs of the physical model. The outcome is a complete demonstration of the code-to-construction-to-visualization pipeline from first principles to shareable visual outputs.

source_fields.introduction: Step into the future of design innovation with Design-Tech Talk 8.0, a two-day online event bringing together the world’s leading thinkers and creators at the crossroads of architecture, technology, and digital design. Explore how emerging technologies are transforming creative practice—spanning AI-driven design workflows, computational thinking, digital fabrication, and sustainable innovation. Each session will feature a thought-provoking presentation from industry experts, followed by discussions that bridge conceptual exploration with real-world application. Whether you’re an architect, designer, researcher, or enthusiast eager to understand the technologies shaping tomorrow’s built environment, Design-Tech Talk will offer inspiring insights, practical knowledge, and a glimpse into the evolving landscape of design intelligence. Program: Day 1, January 10th: Opening Session: 14:00-14:15 GMT 1st Speaker: Edoardo Tibuzzi 14:15 – 15:15 GMT 2nd Speaker: Daniel Koehler 15:30 – 16:30 GMT 3rd Speaker: Lucas Epp 16:45 – 17:45 GMT Closing Session: 17:45 – 18:00 GMT Day 2, January 11th: Opening Session: 14:00-14:15 GMT 1st Speaker: Aldo Sollazzo 14:15 – 15:15 GMT 2nd Speaker: Ana Gabriela Loayza 15:30 – 16:30 GMT Closing Session: 16:30 – 16:45 GMT Edoardo Tibuzzi Edoardo is Design Director at AKTII and specialises in complex design, leading the applied research team. His portfolio includes The Vessel, a complex, high-profile collaboration with Heatherwick Studio in New York, the Heydar Aliyev Museum in Baku with Zaha Hadid Architects, and the Bloomberg Headquarters with F+P. Ed has been involved in several collaborations with KTH University in Stockholm, the AA and the RCA in London, and the Harvard GSD, where he is currently running various lectures and workshops. He published various papers and books on digital fabrication, sustainable design, new technologies, and material research. Daniel Koehler Compositional Intelligence: Architectural Typology Through Generative AI Daniel Koehler is Assistant Professor of Architecture at the University of Texas at Austin and a member of the Board of Directors of ACADIA. He leads the Lab for Environmental Design Strategies (lab‑eds) with research sites in Austin, Shenzhen, and Innsbruck, focusing on Generative AI, environmental performance, and architectural typology. Formerly a researcher at the Bartlett School of Architecture, UCL, and the University of Innsbruck, he completed his doctorate on part‑to‑whole methodologies, later published as The Mereological City (transcript / Columbia UP, 2016), now a standard reference on mereology in modernism. Koehler’s work has been exhibited internationally at the Centre Pompidou, the Venice Architecture Biennale, and in Prague, Milan, Montreal, London, and Austin. He consults for computational‑design startups such as Sengine AI. His recent book Compositional Intelligence (Routledge) positions Generative AI as an intellectual partner for rethinking architectural typology across scales. Ana Gabriela Loayza Ana Gabriela Loayza is an architect and designer currently working as an Architectural Designer & AI Lead at Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG) in New York. She holds an M.Arch II degree from the Harvard University Graduate School of Design (GSD), where her research explored AI-driven design workflows and urban growth boundaries in projects such as Center–Periphery: Encoding New Processes in Shenzhen’s Boundaries. At BIG, she specialises in integrating computational design and artificial intelligence within architectural practice, leveraging her expertise at the intersection of emerging technologies and built-environment innovation. Aldo Sollazzo Aldo Sollazzo is an Italian entrepreneur and innovator, an expert in robotics, computer vision, and computational design. He has been the CEO of Noumena since 2011, a data-driven company implementing computer vision and machine learning to study and analyze spatial dynamics. As part of the Noumena Group, he is also the CEO of PURE.TECH, a material-driven company operating to promote sustainability at the industrial scale, and of LAMÁQUINA, a large-scale 3D printing factory, shaping new architectural solutions integrating advanced manufacturing and computation. At the Institute for Advanced Architecture of Catalunya in Barcelona, he is the Director of the Master's in Robotics and Advanced Construction. In 2019, Aldo received, from the Italian President of the Republic, the title of Knight of the Order of the Star of Italy for the promotion of national prestige abroad as a recognition of his scientific and technological activities. Aldo has made many appearances as a guest speaker at Conferences and University Seminars, amongst them the European Conference on Computer Vision, Barcelona Urban Tech, Future City Summit, The Venice Biennale, and TEDx Barcelona. Lucas Epp Lucas Epp is a structural engineer whose work sits at the intersection of architecture, engineering, and craft. His work advances timber and natural materials as primary, high-performance structural systems - from mass timber to long-span, free-form geometries. He has pioneered modern all-wood structural systems and joinery techniques at the new National Performing Arts Centre in Barbados and the School of Architecture and Design at the University of Kansas, blending ancient craft with state-of-the-art computational design and robotics – and opening new possibilities for timber architecture. In 2021, he founded Branch, an in-house software venture creating the next generation of digital tools for structural design-to-manufacture, informed by direct feedback from engineers, fabricators, and field crews. Epp has practiced across the UK, New Zealand, China, the United States, and Canada. He has taught at ETH Zurich, the Architectural Association, and MIT; serves on Canadian and American timber code committees; and has authored multiple industry guidelines. His practice points toward a near future in which structural engineering, fabrication, and software merge - a return to the master builder mindset.

source_fields.name: Fibrous Architecture: Robotic Fabrication & AI Rendering
source_fields.softwares: Grasshopper 3D | KUKA PRC | Nano Banana | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: The workshop will be a loop between design and fabrication revolving around emerging morphologies of fibrous trajectories. The Workshop will delve into creating a workflow from design to digital fabrication for architectural-scale installation of an aggregated fibrous structure using a six-axis KUKA robotic arm. For projects where accessibility to a robotic arm would not be possible, a low-tech system for a manual wound strategy will be implemented. Participants will learn how to create computational workflows within Grasshopper 3D using ‘MutAnt’ for aggregation of polygonal planar geometries and ‘Weaver Ant’ to design fibrous systems for robotic winding through ‘KUKA Prc’.
source_fields.description: Fibrous Architecture: Robotic Fabrication & AI Rendering is a two-session workshop on PAACADEMY that teaches participants to design computational fibrous workflows, simulate robotic winding using a six-axis KUKA robotic arm, and produce AI-assisted visualizations with Nano Banana. Working in Grasshopper 3D with the MutAnt and Weaver Ant plugins, participants develop both manual low-tech winding strategies and fully robotic winding workflows from design to digital fabrication at architectural scale.
source_fields.objectives: Create a computational workflow linking digital design and fabrication in Grasshopper 3D. Design installations for low-tech fabrication using CNC cutting and manual cable winding. Generate planar aggregations using boundary rule sets through MutAnt. Build and simulate a robotic winding workflow using Weaver Ant and KUKA Prc for architectural-scale fabrication. Rendering through Nano Banana.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop guides participants through a complete workflow that moves from fabrication strategies to full robotic winding. It begins with the design of filament paths for manually wound systems using CNC-cut frames, developed through Grasshopper definitions that include formwork modeling, anchor fixtures, notching, and data extraction using Weaver Ant. The workshop shifts to robotic fabrication, where planar frames generated through MutAnt aggregations are prepared with precise coordinates for KUKA robotic winding. Throughout the process, participants build a continuous chain from conceptual modeling and aggregation to winding pattern generation, frame preparation, robotic simulation, and final AI-assisted rendering with Nano Banana. Program: First Session This session begins with the design of rope winding on a single-curved stay-in-place formwork. The filament strategy will be designed to be provided for manual winding onto a CNC-cut frame. The workshop will focus on scripting a computational workflow within Grasshopper, from designing the frames to incorporating nuts and bolts with notches for fixing the frames together. ‘Weaver ant’ will be used to generate the filament pattern and to generate data for winding. Introductory presentation of projects by UN[MOULD]™ pertaining to fibrous systems from an array of executed product to architectural scale strategies. Conceptual modeling within grasshopper with required proportions of an installation Designing formwork and anchor fixtures Understanding Weaver Ant workflow, generating winding patterns. Unrolling frame, text tags and making files required for CNC cutting. Assignment with Q&A Second Session The second day will look into the design of rope winding on planar frames derived from aggregations. These frames will be designed with precise nuts and bolts; these coordinates will provide the anchor points for robotic winding using Weaver Ant and KUKA PRC. Creating planar frame systems derived from aggregations generated through MutAnt. Designing detailed planar frames in Grasshopper, including precise nuts and bolts used as anchor coordinates for robotic winding. Generating winding geometries and knots using Weaver Ant for robotic execution. Focusing on robotic fabrication: understanding TCP, end-effector behavior, TCP setup, KUKA movements, and simulation using KUKA Prc. Producing final renders using Nano Banana for AI-assisted visualization. Assignment and Q&A.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of computational design, robotic fabrication, and AI rendering, enabling you to design complex fibrous structures and simulate winding workflows for architectural installations. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated digital-to-physical techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What is KUKA PRC and how is it used for robotic fabrication in Grasshopper? :: KUKA PRC is a Grasshopper plugin that allows designers to program, simulate, and export robotic tool paths for KUKA six-axis robotic arms directly from within the Grasshopper environment. It handles TCP (tool center point) setup, end-effector behavior, joint configurations, and movement sequences, and exports the final code for physical execution on the robot. In this workshop, KUKA PRC is used alongside Weaver Ant to generate and simulate robotic winding paths for fibrous architectural installations. || What does the Fibrous Architecture workshop at PAACADEMY cover across its two sessions? :: Session 1 focuses on manual winding strategy: scripting a Grasshopper workflow for single-curved stay-in-place formwork, designing frames with anchor fixtures and notching using Weaver Ant, generating winding patterns and data, and preparing files for CNC cutting. Session 2 introduces robotic fabrication: creating planar frame aggregations using MutAnt, designing detailed frames with anchor coordinates for robotic winding, simulating the full KUKA robotic process with KUKA PRC, and producing final AI-assisted renders using Nano Banana. || Do I need access to a KUKA robotic arm to join this fibrous architecture workshop? :: No. The workshop is designed to accommodate participants without access to a robotic arm. A low-tech manual winding strategy using CNC-cut frames is implemented as an alternative, covering the same design logic and computational workflow. Participants working with the robotic track will use KUKA PRC for simulation and fabrication data generation, while the manual track uses the same Grasshopper definitions for winding patterns and frame preparation. || What will I produce by the end of this fibrous architecture workshop? :: Participants will complete a full design-to-fabrication workflow for a fibrous architectural installation, including a Grasshopper script covering formwork design, winding pattern generation, and aggregation logic using MutAnt and Weaver Ant, fabrication-ready files for either CNC cutting and manual winding or KUKA robotic arm execution, and final AI-assisted visualizations of the installation produced in Nano Banana.
