source_fields.name: AI-Driven Retail Architecture: From Animation to Construction
source_fields.softwares: 3ds Max | ChatGPT | Kling AI | Meshy | Midjourney | Nano Banana | Rendair
source_fields.introduction: This workshop teaches architects and designers how to integrate the latest, most relevant AI tools into 3D retail workflows to design stores, supermarkets, product displays, pop-ups, and commercial stands. Participants will learn the fundamentals of professional retail design in 3D, how to generate AI-based assets for commercial environments, and how to apply cutting-edge AI techniques for conceptualization, post-production, and animation in retail architecture. AI-Driven 3D Retail Architecture Design is a comprehensive, hands-on experience designed for architects and designers, especially those accustomed to residential design, who want to enter the world of commercial and retail architecture with next-generation AI tools.
source_fields.description: AI-Driven Retail Architecture is a two-day course on PAACADEMY that teaches architects and designers how to design, visualize, and animate commercial retail environments using a full AI-accelerated production pipeline. Participants learn retail design fundamentals including user flow, visual merchandising, and product hierarchy, then apply AI tools at every stage: Midjourney 7.0 for conceptual generation, Meshy AI, Tripo 3D, Rodin, and Hitem 3D for rapid 3D asset creation, Nano Banana Pro for AI post-production and relighting, and Kling AI, Rendair, and Veo for animation. Traditional 3D tools including Blender, SketchUp, 3Ds Max, and Maya are integrated throughout. A bonus session covers AI sketching for plans, elevations, and design diagrams.
source_fields.objectives: Fundamentals of Retail Architecture Design Professional 3D Retail Modeling Midjourney 7.0 for Conceptual Retail Design AI-Generated 3D Assets and Scenes for Commercial Environments Advanced AI Post-Production for Retail Renderings AI Image Enhancement & Upscaling AI Animation: image-to-video, video-to-video, start and end frames & upscaling Bonus: AI Sketching for Retail Architecture: plans, elevations, diagrams, and technical sketching with AI
source_fields.methodology: In this workshop, participants will learn how to design commercial environments such as stores, supermarkets, retail displays, and exhibition stands, integrating AI into every stage of the workflow: conceptual design, 3D modeling, texturing, post-production, and professional-grade animation. This workshop utilizes tools such as Midjourney 7.0, Meshy AI, Tripo 3D, Rodin, Hitem 3D, Nano Banana Pro, Kling AI, Rendair, and traditional 3D applications (3Ds Max, Blender, SketchUp, Maya). You will master a hybrid workflow that merges high-level retail design principles with AI-accelerated production pipelines. Whether you work in architecture, interior design, commercial environments, or brand experiences, this workshop will teach you to transform retail concepts into immersive, emotionally engaging visual stories crafted for clients, stakeholders, and professional presentations. Welcome to the new era where AI and retail architecture merge to reshape brand spaces. This intensive hands-on workshop combines guided instruction, real-time practice, and project-based learning. Participants will experience a complete end-to-end retail design workflow using real retail assets and scenes, while experimenting with: Midjourney 7.0 for conceptual generation Meshy AI, Tripo 3D, Rodin, Hitem 3D for rapid 3D asset creation Blender, SketchUp, 3Ds Max, or preferred 3D tool Nano Banana Pro for post-production Kling AI, Rendair, Veo for animation ChatGPT for ideation, troubleshooting, and design assistance Each session progressively builds from foundation to concept to 3D to post-production to animation, enabling participants to complete a full AI retail architecture pipeline. Day 1 – The Foundations of AI-Driven Retail Architecture Session 1 – Fundamentals of Retail Design and 3D Implementation User flow and customer journey Visual merchandising and product hierarchy Focal points, lighting strategies, and materials POS structures, displays, toy stores, supermarkets, stands Transitioning from housing design to high-performance retail design Hands-on: Analyze a real retail layout and redesign focal points and experiential zones. Session 2 – AI-Accelerated 3D Retail Modeling Model creation using Meshy AI, Tripo 3D, Rodin, Hitem 3D When to use manual modeling vs AI generation Creating shelves, totems, display units, signage, props Optimizing 3D assets for scenes and animation Hands-on: Generate and refine a retail display or product stand using AI tools. Session 3 – Midjourney 7.0 for Retail Conceptualization Store interiors Retail stands and exhibition booths Display units and POS furniture Elevations, plans, and sections Style variations, brand identities, materials, lighting Hands-on: Create a full retail design concept (store plus stand plus display variants). Day 2 – From Static Concepts to Animated Retail Visualizations Session 4 – AI Post-Production for Retail Architecture Nano Banana Pro in depth (Google AI Plus) Relighting, material enhancements, realism optimization Cinematic post-production workflows Creating brand-ready visuals for clients Session 5 – AI Retail Animation Techniques Kling AI, Rendair, Veo 3 Image-to-video retail animations Start and end frames Camera movement for retail storytelling Upscaling and frame interpolation Preparing renders for animation Session 6 – Bonus: AI Sketching for Commercial Architecture Plans, elevations, sections Design diagrams Hybrid sketch-over techniques Rapid ideation for client presentations By the end of the workshop, participants will have completed a full AI-enhanced retail architecture pipeline, including: Retail concept creation 3D asset generation 3D scene preparation AI post-production for retail visuals AI retail animation AI sketching and diagramming Participants will gain the skills to design, visualize, and animate professional retail environments using the leading AI tools shaping the future of commercial architecture.
source_fields.requirements: Basic skills in any 3D software (Blender, SketchUp, 3Ds Max, Maya, etc.) Basic understanding of architectural design concepts
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of AI-driven retail design and 3D visualization, enabling you to transform commercial concepts into professional-grade animations and immersive brand spaces. source_fields.name: Tectonix: Kangaroo Form-Finding & AI Narrative Design
source_fields.softwares: Grasshopper 3D | Kangaroo | Kling AI | Magnific AI | Midjourney | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: Tectonix is a comprehensive workshop that unites physics, mathematical form-making, and digital tools with culture and narrative to build a new, integrated design workflow. It guides participants from the earliest stage of coarse geometry toward meaningful, narrative-driven outcomes showing how form, force, and storytelling can operate together rather than as isolated steps. The workshop positions computational tools and AI systems not just as utilities, but as collaborators that help frame atmosphere, context, and cultural intent.
source_fields.description: This workshop merges physics-based form-finding and AI-driven narrative design to transform meshes into expressive architectural concepts.
source_fields.objectives: Preparation of coarse meshes for physics-based, doubly curved form-finding. Force-driven geometric transformation using Grasshopper and Kangaroo. Narrative-based concept generation informed by form, culture, and AI prompts. AI integration of Kangaroo geometries through Nano Banana Pro for advanced visual outcomes. Refinement and presentation of results using Kling AI and related tools. Cohesive workflow linking tools, form logic, and narrative design.
source_fields.methodology: The methodology unfolds through two interconnected streams. The first is a parametric, physics-based form-finding, where Grasshopper and Kangaroo are used to transform coarse meshes into smooth, doubly curved surfaces. This process demonstrates how force simulations, topology adjustments, and mathematical logic can generate expressive architectural forms with structural intuition embedded in their geometry. The second stream is AI-driven conceptual exploration, where tools like Midjourney and Nano Banana expand the physics-generated geometries into cultural and urban narratives. Prompt crafting, image inputs, and form-derived references guide the AI outputs, which are then enhanced, animated, and refined using Magnific AI and Kling AI. Program: Session 1: Fundamentals and Parametric Modeling Part 1 — Theoretical Introduction A conceptual walk-through of Parametric Design, Form-Finding, AI, and Narrative, establishing how these elements converge into a unified workflow. Part 2 — Minimal Surface Modeling Building a coarse mesh in Rhino and preparing it for force simulation. Students learn how mesh topology and boundary conditions influence minimal surface behavior. Key Tool: Rhino Part 3 — Force Simulation / Form-Finding Applying force components through Grasshopper + Kangaroo to transform the coarse mesh into a stable, doubly curved minimal surface. Includes mesh relaxation, stability checks, and exporting a clean mesh for downstream use. Key Tools: Grasshopper, Kangaroo Session 2: Narrative, AI, and Output Part 1 — Exploring Visual Narrative with AI Generating narrative-based morphological studies using Midjourney—participants craft prompts inspired by minimal surfaces, structural logic, and cultural influences. Key Tool: Midjourney Part 2 — Linking Modeling to AI Generation Integrating the Grasshopper/Kangaroo geometry with Nano Banana Pro to interpret AI results, refine visual direction, and set up final views grounded in the simulated form. Key Tool: Nano Banana Pro Part 3 — Narrative Scenes & Presentation Output Creating presentation videos using Kling AI to combine the simulated form, AI concepts, and narrative into a cohesive visual sequence. Key Tool: Kling AI

source_fields.name: Synthetic Architecture: AI-Powered Adaptive Workflows
source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | ChatGPT | Formas.ai | Gemini | Magnific AI | Midjourney | Nano Banana | Rhinoceros 3D | Runway ML
source_fields.introduction: Design tools are evolving faster than ever, and the role of the architect is shifting from form-giver to curator of intelligence . This workshop is a deep dive into Synthetic Architecture Methodology, 25 years of architectural theory and practice, enhanced with AI. We will explore why the faulty, the sloppy, and the imperfect often reveal more than “beautiful design,” and how to build Second Brains that manage complexity, structure ideas, and support critical decision-making. Participants will learn how to break down architectural problems into modular components and move from philosophical grounding to simulations, storytelling, and clear visual output.
source_fields.description: Synthetic Architecture: AI-Powered Adaptive Workflows is a course that teaches architects AI-powered, adaptive workflows for designing, visualizing, and refining architecture. Across two days, students build a Second Brain research system using Pinterest and Graphcommons, generate and combine concept visuals with Midjourney, Gemini, ChatGPT, Runway ML, and Magnific AI, refine outputs through a Photoshop-based surgery workflow, and validate designs against real constraints using environmental simulation in Autodesk Forma and Rayon. The course is Beginner level and expects genuine curiosity and critical engagement rather than passive image generation.
source_fields.objectives: Construct Second Brains: A digital ecosystem to organize references and ideas Read Context: Understand what is ugly, faulty, misplaced—and why that matters Master the Surgery Workflow: Combine all tools into controlled, meaningful illustrations Create Strong Visuals: Produce intentional architectural imagery with AI Validate with Data: Use environmental simulations and light BIM to prove feasibility Software Philosophy: Push tools to their limits, collaborate with technologies, and shape your design environment
source_fields.methodology: This course focuses on adaptive design systems, a way of thinking that outlives any single tool. Instead of “prompt engineering,” we practice Surgical Concept Formation: stitching, refining, and curating outputs into a coherent architectural narrative. We will cover: History of AI in Architecture: From pre-CAD to the AI era Data & Networks: Turning abstract ideas into relational diagrams Visual Production: Generating, mixing, upscaling, and repairing images through a modular workflow Simulation & Light BIM: Validating AI concepts with environmental and functional data The Scope: Modular Workflow Design is treated as a network of refinement stations rather than a linear or chaotic process. Second Brains: Using Pinterest, Graphcommons, and AI tools, we externalize thinking, classify information, and build intelligent visual repositories. The Surgery Table Rejecting the myth of the “perfect generation,” Photoshop becomes a surgical table—where we stitch, layer, and manipulate outputs into intentional architectural compositions. Reality Check: With Autodesk Forma and Rayon, we test AI hallucinations against real constraints: ergonomics, sunlight, climate, program, and feasibility. Program: Day 1 Module 1: The Mind — Introduction What is Synthetic Architecture History of tools Reading societies, context, and underlying forces Module 2: Secondary Brain Theory & Data Classification Building meaning with AI tools, spreadsheets, and Graphcommons Using Pinterest as an intelligent visual repository Module 3: Building the Concept Base Idea-generation tools and the value of “wrong” or “sloppy” outputs Deterministic prompting: telling AI exactly what you need Creating a sketch or simple 3D massing for downstream use Module 4: The Tool Arsenal Overview of Midjourney, Gemini, ChatGPT, Runway, Magnific, Photoshop, Forma, Rayon, Rhino, etc. Task: Prepare site, context, visual repository, sketches, and tools for Day 2. Day 2 Module 1: Forming the Base Reviewing site data Creating a network diagram for a function Reviewing Pinterest + sketches + base model Module 2: Storytelling, Illustration & Surgery Creating concept visuals using MJ, Gemini, and Mystic Selecting viable options Conducting the "surgery" for architectural integrity Module 3: Reality Check (Simulation & Light BIM) Environmental simulations in Forma Adapting plans in Rayon Creating elevations and render sets Module 4: Finalization Selecting final illustrations Storyboard-based video generation Final layout using ChatGPT + Canva
source_fields.requirements: Be Curious: This workshop requires reading, thinking, and engaging, not just generating images. The Ugly Truth: Understanding the faulty and the wrong is essential before arriving at good design.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated high-efficiency techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: Will this workshop teach me how to gain control and precision over my designs? :: Yes. This is a primary focus of the course. Instead of relying on "random" outcomes or basic prompting, the curriculum introduces "Surgical Concept Formation." This methodology treats the design process as a "surgery table," teaching participants how to stitch, refine, and curate specific AI outputs into intentional, controlled architectural compositions. || Will learning to build a 'Second Brain' help me manage the complexity of my design projects more efficiently? :: The "Second Brain" module teaches how to construct a digital ecosystem to organize references, research, and ideas. By mastering this system, participants learn to externalize their thinking and classify information effectively, making it much easier to manage complex architectural problems and support critical decision-making. || Is this workshop suitable for designers who prioritize storytelling and theory over purely technical skills? :: Yes, it is highly recommended for narrative-driven designers. The workshop emphasizes that the architect's role is shifting to that of a "curator of intelligence." The prerequisites prioritize curiosity, reading, and context-awareness, focusing heavily on how to weave abstract ideas into a coherent architectural story. || Will this workshop provide me with a comprehensive framework that I can use for future projects, regardless of how tools change? :: Participants will acquire a flexible methodology that can be applied to any future design challenge, ensuring their skills remain relevant in this field. || Can I apply this methodology to architectural projects? :: The workflow goes beyond simple image generation by integrating environmental data and simulation tools. This ensures that the designs produced are not just visually compelling but also grounded.

courses.name: Algorithmic Urban Design in Grasshopper: Data-Driven Site Analysis & Massing

source_fields.name: Algorithmic Urban Design in Grasshopper: Data-Driven Site Analysis & Massing
source_fields.introduction: Creating urban design from scratch on complex terrain can often feel like a big challenge. So, in order to gather a deeper understanding of the site and quickly explore different design possibilities, we can use digital tools, parametric modelling, and an algorithmic approach. The idea is to read the landscape first and let the environment guide the concept. Therefore, in this workshop, we will explore how to analyze the location and use the data to inspire design solutions, not just as technical requirements. You will learn how to create four different analysis methods: Sunlight exposure Terrain slope Vegetation density Visibility study Each of these methods will be demonstrated step-by-step, showing how raw site information can be turned into visual diagrams. Then, these diagrams will become inputs for a generative design workflow focused on finding optimal building positions and shapes. Rather than guessing where a building should go or relying purely on intuition, we can use algorithms, or in other words, a sequence of geometric operations, to analyze the site, gather data, and suggest initial massing for the urban design. This workflow is one of the strategies for early design exploration and can be used in any location. The complete workflow, including 4 analyses and generative design, will be developed entirely in Grasshopper for Rhino, since it is one of the best tools for architects and designers for parametric and generative design.
source_fields.description: Algorithmic Urban Design in Grasshopper: Data-Driven Site Analysis & Massing is a course that teaches architects to build custom, data-driven site analysis and generative massing workflows entirely in Grasshopper. Across two days, students build four analysis methods, sunlight exposure, terrain slope, vegetation density, and visibility, using Ladybug for daylight analysis, then integrate that data into a parametric model that generates urban massing scenarios and prioritizes building, park, and square locations. The course is Beginner level and requires Rhino 8 and Grasshopper pre-installed, with basic familiarity with both expected.
source_fields.objectives: Creative algorithmic thinking and problem-solving Analyzing complex terrain geometry (Sunlight + Slope + Vegetation + Visibility) How to create your own custom analysis method from scratch Data-driven design strategies Generative approach to urban design Tips & tricks for creating efficient and organized Grasshopper definitions
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will focus entirely on creating algorithms within Grasshopper. This includes creating different methods for site analysis and a parametric model for generating urban design. The input geometry will be available in Rhino, but we will not cover basic 3D modelling techniques there. Therefore, it is expected that the student is familiar with Rhino and basic Grasshopper concepts. This workshop will focus on creative algorithmic thinking and problem-solving in Grasshopper. The algorithms for site analysis and urban design will be created from scratch. You will learn how to set up your own custom analysis method, which will allow you to extend this workflow after the workshop based on your own preferences. Each student will work alone. We will start with the same terrain for input geometry, but the students will be encouraged to use the same algorithm for different site locations. By the end of the workshop, each student will have a complete parametric definition capable of generating multiple urban design scenarios based on environmental data and design priorities. Program Day 1 – Introduction and Terrain Analysis Presentation and Concept Overview Overview of the workshop and objectives. Explanation of key concepts for creating necessary algorithms and preparing for parametric analysis. Grasshopper Introduction and Setup Understanding the interface and workflow. Step-by-step setup for terrain analysis. Development of Terrain Analysis Methods Creation of four different analysis methods. Practical demonstrations and explanations for each method. Application and Experimentation Running analyses on sample terrains. Adjusting parameters and experimenting with settings. Visualization and Customization Applying color gradients and visual styles. Developing custom styles for improved readability and presentation. Outcome by End of Day 1 A fully functional Grasshopper definition capable of analyzing any terrain. Homework Continue experimenting with parameters, settings, and visualization styles. Explore ways to refine analysis speed and precision. Day 2 – Data Integration and Urban Design Working with Large Data Sets Using outputs from different analysis methods. Handling data for urban design purposes. Prioritization and Shape Extraction Setting priorities to identify relevant shapes for buildings, parks, and squares. Parametric Urban Design Development Completing the remainder of the parametric model. Integrating multiple datasets to generate complex urban layouts. Exploration of Design Solutions Comparing alternative outcomes based on input parameters. Observing how variations affect the overall design and spatial organization. Outcome by End of Day 2 A complete parametric urban design model ready for further development or presentation.
source_fields.requirements: The installation process is not part of the workshop. The student should have Rhino 8 and Grasshopper already installed. We will also use the Ladybug plugin for Grasshopper to perform daylight analysis. Basic familiarity with Rhino and Grasshopper concepts is expected
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of computational urban design and Grasshopper data management, enabling you to assess environmental impacts and package complex algorithms into reusable clusters. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated computational workflows is commendable.
source_fields.faq: I have used Rhino but only know the basics of Grasshopper. Is this workshop too advanced for me? :: Not at all. While basic familiarity with the interface is expected, the workshop is designed to guide participants step-by-step. The focus is on "logic" and "design thinking". All specific algorithms for the site analysis and massing are built from scratch during the sessions, ensuring everyone can follow along. || Do I need to be a programmer or an expert to understand the 'Algorithmic' part of this course? :: No coding background is required. The term "algorithmic" here simply refers to a sequence of geometric operations used to solve design problems. The workshop focuses on creative problem-solving and on translating design intuition into a digital workflow, making it accessible to architects and designers who want to work smarter. || What software do I need to have ready before the workshop begins? :: Participants need Rhino 8 installed on their computer. The Ladybug plugin is also required for the analysis. Software installation is not covered during the session, so having these tools ready beforehand is essential. || Can the analysis tools we build and workflows be used for other projects, or are they specific to the workshop's site? :: The tools are designed to be fully reusable. A key objective of the workshop is to teach how to create a flexible "definition" (script) that can accept different terrain geometries. By the end of the course, participants will possess a versatile tool capable of analyzing and generating concepts for future projects on different sites. || Is this workshop limited to data analysis, or does it also cover the design concepts? :: It bridges the gap between both. While the process begins with data analysis (sunlight, slope, visibility), the goal is design generation. The data serves as the foundation for the "Generative Design" phase, creating optimal building positions and urban layouts based on the environmental factors analyzed earlier.

courses.name: Rhino For Beginners 101

source_fields.name: Rhino For Beginners 101
source_fields.introduction: Rhinoceros 3D (Rhino) is an industry-standard modeling software widely used in architecture, design, and fabrication for its precision, flexibility, and ability to handle complex geometry. Its intuitive interface and powerful toolset make it an essential platform for designers looking to bridge conceptual design, detailed modeling, and technical documentation within a single workflow. Rhino for Beginners is a practical, hands-on introduction to Rhinoceros 3D, designed to help you understand the software from the ground up. Instead of overwhelming you with theory, the course focuses on the essential tools and workflows you need to start drafting, modelling, annotating, and documenting your projects with confidence. By the end of this course, you’ll be able to navigate Rhino’s interface fluently, create precise 2D drawings, convert them into 3D models, and prepare polished sheets for presentation or construction, all using industry-standard practices. This workshop also includes a live demonstration based on an ongoing residential project, ensuring you learn not just tools but real-world applications. You’ll also get a brief introduction to Grasshopper, Rhino’s powerful computational design plugin.
source_fields.description: Rhino for Beginners 101 is an 8-session beginner course on PAACADEMY that teaches Rhinoceros 3D from interface fundamentals through 2D drafting, 3D modeling, annotation, layout creation, and project documentation. The course follows a real residential project to demonstrate practical architectural workflows, and concludes with a bonus introduction to Grasshopper and parametric design. No prior Rhino experience is required.
source_fields.objectives: Learn navigation, viewports, and essential commands to establish an efficient Rhino workflow. Create precise 2D plans with clean, controlled geometry and linework. Add and manage text, dimensions, and annotations for clear documentation. Convert 2D drawings into accurate 3D forms using core modeling tools. Create layouts, place views, and export drawings for presentation or printing. Follow a real residential project to understand practical, real-world workflows. Get a brief introduction to Grasshopper and its parametric design potential.
source_fields.methodology: This course uses a clear, progressive workflow that moves from basic navigation to complete 2D drafting, 3D modeling, and documentation. Each session builds directly on the previous one through practical demonstrations, short assignments, and real project examples. By learning through applied exercises rather than theory, you quickly develop the confidence to use Rhino in a professional architectural workflow, ending with a brief introduction to parametric design using Grasshopper. Program: Session 1: Introduction to Rhino Overview of the Rhino environment Understanding the interface, viewports, and navigation tools Working with units, grids, snap settings, and display modes How Rhino’s command workflow operates and how to use it efficiently Session 2: 2D Drafting Fundamentals Creating lines, polylines, curves, circles, and arcs Editing tools, including trim, extend, fillet, offset, and join Session 3: Assignment Walkthrough and Plan Development Solving the guided assignment from the previous session Developing a simple architectural plan step by step Preparing curves and drawings for 3D use Session 4: Introduction to 3D Modelling Generating basic 3D geometries such as extrusions, surfaces, and solids Controlling geometry through gumball, control points, and transforms Understanding booleans, surface creation, and solid operations Building 3D forms from the plan created earlier Session 5: Annotations and Advanced Geometry Tools Adding text, leaders, dimensions, and managing annotation styles Setting up layers, colors, linetypes, and lineweight control Using loft, sweep, planar surface, and other advanced modeling commands Documenting models clearly for design communication Session 6: Layout Creation and Documentation Setting up layouts for printing and presentations Arranging drawings, title blocks, and sheet formatting Exporting drawings and preparing deliverables Session 7: Real Project Workflow Importing architectural plans from AutoCAD Cleaning and preparing the file Building a practical architectural model based on a real residential project Session 8: Bonus Introduction to Grasshopper Creating a simple parametric setup to demonstrate possibilities A glimpse of how computational design can enhance everyday modeling
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: How is Rhinoceros 3D different from AutoCAD for architectural drafting and modeling? :: Rhinoceros 3D and AutoCAD both support 2D drafting, but they serve different purposes in an architectural workflow. AutoCAD is optimized for 2D technical documentation and construction drawings, with a drafting-first logic. Rhino is built around precise 3D geometry and NURBS modeling, making it stronger for complex surfaces, custom fabrication geometry, and transitioning directly from a 2D plan to a 3D model without switching tools. Rhino also integrates directly with Grasshopper for parametric design, and is commonly used alongside rendering and fabrication workflows in contemporary architectural practice. || What does the Rhino for Beginners 101 course at PAACADEMY cover? :: The 8-session course covers the Rhino interface, viewports, navigation, and command workflow; 2D drafting using lines, polylines, curves, and editing tools; plan development and assignment walkthroughs; 3D modeling from 2D plans using extrusions, surfaces, solids, and booleans; annotations, dimensions, layers, and lineweight control; layout creation and drawing export for presentation; a live demonstration based on a real residential project imported from AutoCAD; and a bonus introduction to Grasshopper for parametric design. || Is this Rhino course suitable for complete beginners with no prior 3D experience? :: Yes. The course is designed for participants with no prior Rhinoceros 3D experience and starts from the interface, viewports, and snap settings before introducing any modeling tools. Each session builds on the previous one through practical exercises and short assignments, so no 3D software background is required. A general understanding of architectural drawing concepts such as plans and layouts will help, but is not a prerequisite. || What will I be able to do after completing the Rhino for Beginners 101 course? :: By the end of the 8 sessions, participants will be able to navigate Rhino fluently, create precise 2D architectural plans, convert them into 3D models using core modeling tools, add annotations and dimension styles, set up sheet layouts for presentation or printing, and prepare file deliverables based on real-world project workflows. The final session also introduces Grasshopper, giving participants a starting point for exploring computational and parametric design within Rhino.

source_fields.name: Cinematic Architecture: AI-Powered Design Workflows
source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | Luma AI | Magnific AI | Midjourney | Nano Banana | Weavy AI
source_fields.introduction: AI is transforming the way architects envision and communicate design, turning static ideas into dynamic, interactive experiences. This workshop explores how to harness AI as a creative collaborator, guiding your projects from initial concepts to immersive, cinematic presentations. This workshop focuses on enhancing your creative AI workflow, making your architectural or design projects stand out and feel recognized in 2026! In this workshop, you'll learn prompting principles inside of MidJourney, the best AI tools and techniques for editing your ideas, and how to combine them into compelling presentation videos with AI. The revealed workflow can be easily applied to your existing projects, making your presentations more impactful.
source_fields.description: Cinematic Architecture: AI-Powered Design Workflows is a course that teaches architects an AI-driven workflow for generating, editing, and animating interiors and exteriors into cinematic visual narratives. Students learn advanced prompting in Midjourney 7.0, edit and extend renders with Nano Banana Pro inside Weavy, and animate keyframes into a storytelling video with Luma AI, covering camera movement, atmosphere changes, and transitions. The course is Beginner level and requires software installed in advance, including a Midjourney Standard membership and a Weavy Starter subscription.
source_fields.objectives: How to generate, tweak, and take control over prompts in MidJourney 7.0. Key parameters, tokens, and camera angles for photorealistic results Alternative ways to transform an image into a prompt or get an image description Handy techniques for editing the parts or the entire image of your project (Nano Banana Pro and other editing tools inside Weavy) Effective prompting in Nano Banana Pro to generate multiple images based on your one image reference Tokens for image and video generation. Types of shots and camera movements. Key frames for smooth and cinematic video generation with Luma AI Principles of storytelling while generating and editing a video
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will focus on the workflow for generating the interior space and exterior facade for one building, based on the existing plan/image/reference. In conclusion, we will combine elements from both workflows into a comprehensive video that showcases your project from both inside and outside. Every participant is working on their own project, highlighting individual progress and contribution throughout the workshop. We will start by generating the base images for the interior and exterior. Alternatively, we will transform the white interior and exterior models into realistic renders using the AI editing toolset. Then we will proceed to the next stage by editing those images - creating different/extra views, changing the atmosphere/weather, and adding some people. To sum up, we will bring all the pictures to life by animating transitions between frames. This workshop is divided into three main parts: Idea generation (based on the existing early-stage project or without it) Participants will explore how to ideate and develop a precise, extended prompt to achieve a photorealistic and desirable outcome. We will explicitly cover the tokens in the prompts (including the camera position and adjustments), parameters, style, omni, and image references. Also, participants will receive a hands-on guide to working with the sketch/white model in MidJourney (and other AI editing tools) and to assigning a specific look/style to it. At this stage, we are working on both the interior and exterior images. Project edits with AI We are using the results from the previous stage (or an existing project image) and making adjustments with the AI editing tools (Nano Banana Pro and others). The goal is to showcase different edit scenarios that could be easily achieved with a prompt and reference combination. For instance, we will consider weather/time-of-day/atmospheric changes, object inpainting, extra-view/image generation, and people addition. The focus will be on the consistency of all generated images. Animation of the project with AI During the last phase of the workshop, we will explore video generation for all of the images, highlighting how these skills can elevate your projects. We will go through the key framing and storytelling for the final video. At this stage, we will cover the transition making, the morphing, and object manipulations. The aim is to develop a cinematic and convincing video to pitch your architectural/design idea at an early stage.
source_fields.requirements: Software Installation is NOT a part of the workshop! Students must have all the software installed before starting the workshop. If Luma AI is not an option, you can use any other video generation tool (e.g., Kling, Runway, Hailuo, and others) or use a video generation tool via Weavy. We will not cover the pre-project analysis or site analysis process in this workshop. The required subscriptions are a MidJourney Standard membership and a Weavy Starter tier. The instructor will demonstrate other AI tools used in the workshop, but subscriptions are not required to participate.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of AI-driven design, image editing, and cinematic animation, enabling you to generate, edit, and animate architectural concepts into immersive visual narratives. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated visual storytelling techniques is commendable.

A core part of the curriculum involves "Project Edits with AI," which focuses on generating consistent interior and exterior views of the same building. The course focuses on creating "Cinematic Visual Narratives," which go far beyond standard static renderings. By mastering AI-driven storytelling, motion, and atmosphere, you will be able to create immersive video pitches that capture attention and communicate your ideas.

source_fields.name: Advanced Grasshopper 3.0
source_fields.softwares: Dendro | Grasshopper 3D | Kangaroo | LunchBox | Mesh+ | MeshEdit | Pufferfish | Rhinoceros 3D | Weaverbird
source_fields.introduction: In nature, complex forms emerge not through direct design, but through simple rules repeated over time. Branches grow toward light, cells divide and differentiate, and networks optimize for efficiency. This workshop introduces you to a procedural workflow where computational rules generate intricate geometries that would be impossible to model manually. This workshop explores different computational design methods by examining three modeling paradigms—NURBS, mesh, and volumetric modeling—within the Grasshopper environment. The workshop presents a toolkit of strategies, allowing you to select the most appropriate method for each specific challenge. Some exercises will focus on a single paradigm, while others will demonstrate the power of hybrid workflows that transition between multiple geometric representations. As digital fabrication and generative design continue to reshape architecture and product design, the ability to choose and combine different geometric methods has become essential. Participants will move beyond basic parametric modeling to explore how specialized Grasshopper plugins unlock new possibilities for creating geometries that would be impractical through traditional modeling methods. The workshop emphasizes strategic thinking: understanding when to use NURBS for precision and continuity, meshes for subdivision and topology control, and volumetric methods for implicit surfaces and performance-driven forms. Through varied examples—from lattice structures to subdivision surfaces, from paneled facades to morphological transformations, you'll build a fundamental understanding of how each approach serves different design intentions. By the end of this workshop, participants will possess both the technical skills and conceptual framework to approach complex geometric problems strategically, selecting and combining the right tools for each unique design challenge.
source_fields.description: Advanced Grasshopper 3.0 is a workshop exploring three computational modeling paradigms NURBS, mesh, and volumetric within Grasshopper to build complex, fabrication-ready parametric geometry. The curriculum covers NURBS-based curvature and pattern systems using Pufferfish and LunchBox, mesh modeling with subdivision surfaces and physics-based form-finding using Weaverbird and Kangaroo, and volumetric workflows for voxel-based design, signed distance fields, lattice structures, and agent-based growth simulations using Dendro, Crystallon, Monolith, and Physarealm. Each session uses live-coded examples that combine native Grasshopper components with specialized plugins, teaching participants when and how to transition between geometric representations within a single parametric definition. Basic Grasshopper knowledge is recommended.
source_fields.objectives: Work with NURBS, mesh, and volumetric modeling paradigms Choose modeling methods strategically based on design intent Build hybrid Grasshopper workflows across geometry types Generate form through procedural and rule-based systems Use advanced plugins for implicit and voxel-based modeling Convert and optimize geometry for fabrication-ready output
source_fields.methodology: This workshop is structured around exploring three modeling principles through examples that reveal their unique capabilities and applications. Participants exploring tools like Pufferfish and Lunchbox for controlled curvature and pattern-driven forms, the mesh modeling introduces subdivision surfaces, physics-based form-finding, and topology optimization using Weaverbird, Mesh+, and Kangaroo for organic structures. The core focus emphasizes volumetric and implicit modeling through voxel-based design and signed distance field operations, where participants will create complex lattice structures, gradient density systems, bio-inspired cellular patterns, agent-based growth simulations, and performance-optimized forms using Dendro, Crystallon, Monolith, and Physarealm—generating geometries that would be extremely difficult with surface or mesh-based methods alone. Hybrid workflows demonstrate the advantage of Grasshopper to fluidly combine multiple paradigms to address geometric conversion challenges and data management when transitioning between NURBS control surfaces, volumetric operations, and output mesh. Each session includes theoretical foundations, live demonstrations, and hands-on exercises progressing from guided tutorials to open-ended design challenges, building both technical proficiency and strategic decision-making skills. Each session will cover complete design examples that demonstrate how multiple design and modeling strategies work together within unified scripts to achieve specific geometric outcomes. Rather than teaching tools in isolation, participants will build integrated definitions that combine native Grasshopper components with specialized plugins—learning how data flows between NURBS operations, mesh manipulations, and volumetric processes within a single workflow. This workshop will live-code each example from start to finish, explaining strategic decisions about when to introduce specific plugins, how to manage data structures across different geometric types, and troubleshooting common integration challenges. This method will help Participants develop intuition for how different tools complement each other. Through this process-oriented methodology, you'll understand not just individual plugin capabilities, but how to orchestrate them strategically—transitioning from NURBS surface generation to volumetric models, or from mesh subdivision to topology manipulation, all within parametric definitions. Each session builds toward increasingly complex integrations, with collaborative reviews allowing participants to compare approaches and discover alternative component combinations for wider design challenges.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced parametric design and hybrid modeling, enabling you to create complex, performance-driven geometries across NURBS, mesh, and volumetric systems. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated computational workflows is commendable.
source_fields.faq: Is this workshop too advanced for me? :: This workshop is the perfect bridge for users ready to move beyond the basics. While prior knowledge of the native Grasshopper interface is expected, the specialized plugins (such as Dendro for volumetric design and Pufferfish for transformations) are introduced from the ground up. The focus is on learning how to integrate these tools into a cohesive workflow. || Why does the curriculum emphasize 'Hybrid Workflows' instead of just mastering one modeling type? :: Complex design challenges often require more than one approach. By learning to transition fluidly between different paradigms, participants unlock the ability to generate intricate, performance-driven geometries. || What is the advantage of 'Volumetric' modeling compared to standard surface modeling in Rhino? :: Volumetric (or Voxel-based) modeling allows the creation of seamless, complex forms such as lattice structures and organic blends without the typical topological errors found in surface modeling. The workshop demonstrates how to use tools like Dendro to treat geometry as a density field. || Will this workshop help me understand how to organize large, complex Grasshopper definitions? :: Yes. A key learning objective is "Strategic Thinking." The sessions are structured around live-coding examples that demonstrate data management and logic. || Will I just be learning specific plugins, or does this workshop teach a broader design methodology? :: The focus is on methodology. While you will master specific tools like Dendro and Weaverbird, the core goal is to develop "Computational Thinking." You will learn the underlying logic of how natural systems grow and organize branches, cells, networks, and how to apply those procedural rules to solve complex problems.

source_fields.name: Robotic Fabrication for Irregular Geometry
source_fields.categories: 3D Modeling | Architectural Design | Artificial Intelligence | Fabrication
source_fields.introduction: Most robotic fabrication tutorials assume that you are starting with a perfect digital model. However, the future of construction and manufacturing involves interacting with irregular and 'messy' real-world objects, or digital captures of them. In this technical workshop, we will explore the latest frameworks for digitising complex objects and generating complex, surface-aware robotic toolpaths that adapt to their unique topology. This workshop provides an in-depth exploration of the generation of computational toolpaths. The technical workflows required to generate valid instructions for any robot will be covered. Input: We will use automated computer vision to digitise a physical object. Process: The geometry will be processed by Grasshopper to create suitable toolpaths. Output: We will validate these paths using a kinematic simulation (Robots plugin) to ensure they can be executed without issue.
source_fields.description: Robotic Fabrication for Irregular Geometry is a two-day workshop on PAACADEMY that teaches scan-to-robot workflows using Rhino, Grasshopper, and the Robots plugin. Participants learn to digitize physical objects into 3D meshes using computer vision tools, generate surface-aware parametric toolpaths in Grasshopper that adapt to irregular geometry, and validate those paths through kinematic simulation, checking reachability, singularities, and joint limits before exporting machine code for robotic execution. Google Colab is used for the scan-to-mesh computer vision workflow.
source_fields.objectives: Mastering computational concepts for managing complex toolpath arrays. Understanding robot kinematics and how to visualise and validate reachability. Mesh-to-Path Logic: Techniques for projecting vector paths onto 'noisy' scanned meshes. Simulation & Safety: Verifying toolpaths digitally to prevent physical crashes (singularity analysis). Machine Code Generation: Learn how to export your design as code that robots can read.
source_fields.methodology: Digitisation (the input): We will use a streamlined 'scan-to-mesh' workflow using computer vision tools to instantly create a 3D digital twin of a physical object from an image. Toolpath Logic (the core): We will develop parametric scripts to generate 'surface following' paths (e.g., for 3D printing or milling) that hug the geometry. Kinematics (The Validation): We will simulate the robot's motion to check reachability, collisions, and joint limits using the Robots plugin. Program: Day 1 - From Scan to Surface First step: Extract 3D models of objects from images using computer vision tools. Second step: Mesh clean-up and rationalisation in Rhino 8. Third step: Generating toolpaths on the geometry to guide the robot. Day 2 - The 'Robotic Hand' (Toolpathing & Simulation): Import the 'digital twin' into the robotic environment. Generate a toolpath for 3D printing, milling, or coating that adapts to the unique geometry of the object. Use the Robots plugin to simulate the execution of the robotic arm. If time allows, run it on a real robot.

source_fields.introduction: Step into the future of design innovation with Design-Tech Talk 9.0, a two-day online event exploring the evolving relationship between architecture, technology, and digital design. Across a series of curated sessions, the event will examine how emerging technologies are reshaping creative practice, from AI-driven design workflows and computational thinking to digital fabrication and sustainable innovation. Each session will combine focused presentations with open discussions, connecting conceptual ideas to real-world design challenges. Whether you are an architect, designer, researcher, or enthusiast, Design-Tech Talk offers a space to engage with current design intelligence, gain practical insights, and reflect on the tools and methodologies shaping the future of the built environment. Attending the live event is free. However, an active membership is required to watch the event's recordings. Program: Day 1, March 7th: Opening Session: 14:00-14:15 GMT 1st Speaker: Mathilde Marengo 14:15 – 15:15 GMT 2nd Speaker: James Merrill 15:30 – 16:30 GMT 3rd Speaker: Jason Kelly Johnson 16:45 – 17:45 GMT Closing Session: 17:45 – 18:00 GMT Day 2, March 8th: Opening Session: 14:00-14:15 GMT 1st Speaker: Masaaki Miki 14:15 – 15:15 GMT 2nd Speaker: Volkan Alkanoglu 15:30 – 16:30 GMT 3rd Speaker: Federico La Russa 16:45 – 17:45 GMT Closing Session: 17:45 – 18:00 GMT Speakers: Mathilde Marengo Mathilde Marengo is an Australian – French – Italian PhD Architect. Specialised in Research and Academia, her work focuses on enabling spatial justice in cities by leveraging advanced technologies to bridge data gaps and support practitioners to make more informed decisions. She has specifically focused on the development of computer-aided methodologies for the practical implementation of ecological justice and mobility justice in urban design. This includes integrating the needs of more than humans and environmental systems, as well as investigating drivers of urban vulnerability from an intersectional perspective through dynamic and evidence-based design processes. She is Head of Studio Operations at External Reference, an award-winning multidisciplinary design and architecture studio based in Barcelona, Spain. The firm creates immersive and experiential spaces by blending architecture, visual arts, and digital tools, using a combination of traditional craftsmanship and advanced digital technologies like 3D printing to achieve unique and custom designs. She was previously at the Institute for Advanced Architecture of Catalonia for over a decade, serving as Head of Studies and Director of the Urban Sciences Lab, and where she continues to teach today. Her investigation is conducted through her role in several National and EU-funded research projects, as well as being published and exhibited internationally. Masaaki Miki Masaaki Miki is an Assistant Professor at the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, the University of Tokyo. After receiving his Ph.D. from the University of Tokyo, he worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the Igarashi User Interface Group. During this period, he made short-term research visits to the University of Bath and ETH Zurich, where he initiated his work on Airy’s stress function–based form-finding of shells. This research led to his first SIGGRAPH publication in 2015. After gaining experience in architectural practice at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) in Chicago (2015–2020), he returned to academia in Japan. Since then, he has published three additional SIGGRAPH papers on grid shell form-finding, now implemented as Rhinoceros and Grasshopper plugins. Bridging architecture, engineering, and geometry, he currently teaches Visual Structural Design and Architectural Geometry at the University of Tokyo. James Merrill James Merrill is an algorithmic visual artist based in Vermont, USA. He creates computational artwork, combining generative system design, mathematics, randomness, and real-world data to create infinitely unique systems. A third-generation artist, James has been creating digital artworks for over 25 years. His work seeks to utilize technology to challenge assumptions about the nature of traditional art, and oftentimes starts as a program and ends as a physical artwork, drawn to extreme detail by robotic systems. Jason Kelly Johnson Jason Kelly Johnson is the lead artist and co-founding partner of FUTUREFORMS. Jason brings an expertise in computational design and advanced digital fabrication, produced through the lens of critical art production and public space advocacy. Jason was born and raised in Canada. He received a Bachelor of Science from the University of Virginia and a Master of Architecture from Princeton University. Johnson is currently a tenured full Professor at the California College of the Arts (CCA) in San Francisco, CA, where he is the Founding Director of the CCA Digital Craft Lab. He also serves on the board of the Museum of Craft & Design in San Francisco. He has previously taught at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University. Volkan Alkanoglu Volkan Alkanoglu works at the intersection of art and design. Born in Turkey and raised in Germany, Alkanoglu attended the Peter Behrens School of Arts in Düsseldorf and Hochschule der Künste in Berlin before receiving a Master of Architectural Design at the Bartlett School of Architecture in London. His creative focus lies in the exploration of futuristic designs through spatial, material, and technological innovations. Notable projects of his recent work have been installed in various metropolitan areas in the United States, including Seattle, Portland, Los Angeles, Boston, New York, Baltimore, Miami, Tampa, Atlanta, Denver, Dallas, and Washington D.C. Within his academic background, Volkan Alkanoglu has served as the Director for Graduate Studies at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta, GA, and has been part of the design faculty at the Southern California Institute of Architecture, SCI-Arc in Los Angeles, CA, and Harvard University, Graduate School of Design in Cambridge, MA. He holds the designation of LEED Accredited Professional in the USA. Volkan Alkanoglu is actively engaged in commissioned projects across diverse locations, spanning California, Oregon, Colorado, Maryland, Florida, and Taiwan. Federico La Russa Federico Mario La Russa, PhD, is a Computational Designer and Project Manager at Maffeis Engineering, where he leads BIM and parametric workflows using Grasshopper, Revit, and Tekla for complex and lightweight structural systems, including textile and ETFE architectures. With over seven years of experience in computational design, he focuses on algorithmic design, free-form shape optimization, digital fabrication, and AI-driven engineering solutions. Since 2018, his research and professional work have explored the intersection of computational design, digital surveying, and City Information Modeling, resulting in award-winning doctoral research and more than 25 international publications. His PhD investigated the integration of BIM, point clouds, machine learning, and urban-scale data environments. Alongside his professional practice, Federico contributes to academic training and knowledge transfer as Lead Mentor at NovaTr and Lecturer at Politecnico di Milano (DISKILLS), teaching Grasshopper and parametric design methodologies for architecture and engineering.

source_fields.name: AI-Powered Interior Design in Architecture
source_fields.softwares: ChatGPT | Flora AI | Midjourney | Nano Banana
source_fields.introduction: In today’s fast-paced design industry, interior designers are expected to move faster, communicate ideas more clearly, and deliver compelling visuals without compromising creativity or design integrity. AI-Powered Interior Design in Architecture is an immersive, hands-on workshop designed to bridge the gap between imagination and execution, demonstrating how artificial intelligence can become a powerful creative partner rather than a replacement for design thinking. This workshop is designed to provide custom & professional workflows for applying AI across different interior design stages. Participants will learn how to use AI tools to accelerate the process from early concept and mood development to actual design variations, material exploration, and high-quality visualizations. Through practical exercises, attendees will build AI-assisted design pipelines/workflows, creating consistent design directions, generating multiple render variations, refining outputs, and preparing client-ready presentation visuals while maintaining strong design logic, brand coherence, and creative control.
source_fields.description: AI-Powered Interior Design in Architecture is a course that teaches interior designers structured AI workflows for turning early concepts into consistent, client-ready visualizations. Using ChatGPT to shape design logic and prompt strategy, Midjourney to explore mood directions and style variations, Nano Banana Pro to refine outputs for consistency, and Flora AI to organize the process into a repeatable node-based pipeline, students move from mood boards and material exploration through 3D-style renders, isometric views, and upscaled presentation visuals to short AI-generated animations. The course is Beginner level and requires no prior AI experience.
source_fields.objectives: Turn scattered inspiration into clear, client-ready mood, furniture, and material boards. Convert 2D mood boards into consistent 3D-style renders using repeatable workflows. Generate fast, high-quality design variations without losing style consistency. Transform 2D plans into isometric views and 3D conceptual visuals for better storytelling. Create art-directed, realistic visuals driven by mood boards or specific furniture selections. Turn real photos of empty sites into client-ready proposed interior designs. Refine, enhance, and upscale renders to polished, presentation-ready quality. Create short AI-generated animations to elevate interior presentations and marketing.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop follows a practical, repeatable workflow that helps you move from early inspiration to client-ready interior visuals fast, consistently, and with creative control. The focus is not on using AI tools individually, but on building clear workflows you can reuse across different project types. You’ll work through a structured set of exercises using: ChatGPT to shape the design logic (concept narrative, style direction, material language, furniture intent, and a reliable prompt strategy). Midjourney to explore concepts quickly, test multiple styles, and generate strong mood directions. Nanobanana Pro to push outputs toward consistency and presentation quality through controlled refinements and variations. Flora AI to organize the workflow in a node-based pipeline, so each step (concept → style lock → variations → enhancement) is clear, modular, and easy to repeat. By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to produce a complete set of deliverables, mood boards, concept visuals, refined renders, and animated videos using custom AI workflows that balance speed with professional-level consistency.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools for AI-driven interior design and sequential image refinement, enabling you to systematically edit renders and iteratively modify specific interior elements, such as lighting and furniture. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated iterative AI workflows is commendable.
source_fields.faq: Will this workshop teach me how to maintain consistency in furniture and style across different views? :: Yes. One of the primary objectives is moving beyond random image generation. The curriculum focuses on building "structured pipelines" using tools like Nano Banana and Flora AI. These workflows allow for strict control over style, material language, and furniture selection. || Can I use these tools to visualize new designs directly onto photos of existing empty spaces? :: The workshop includes a specific module on "Turning real photos of empty sites into client-ready proposed interior designs." Participants will learn how to overlay new concepts onto existing site context, making this a powerful tool for renovation pitches and remodeling projects where clients need to visualize potential. || Does this workshop help with the concept development phase? :: This workshop will cover the entire design narrative, not just the visuals. You will learn to use ChatGPT to define your "Design Logic"—concepts, style, and materials—before generating images, ensuring the AI follows your creative intent rather than producing random results. || Does the curriculum cover how to translate 2D technical plans into 3D visualizations? :: The workshop bridges the gap between technical documentation and storytelling. Participants will learn workflows to transform 2D plans into isometric views and 3D conceptual visuals. || How will this workshop help me speed up my design process? :: This workshop will teach you to build modular, repeatable workflows. By organizing your process into clear steps (like Concept → Style → Variation), you can rapidly iterate on design options and generate high-quality visuals in a fraction of the time it takes using traditional methods.

courses.name: Reverse Engineering with AI

source_fields.name: Reverse Engineering with AI
source_fields.softwares: Formas.ai | Krea.AI | Luma AI | Midjourney | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: We see stunning designs created with AI every day, but how do we turn them into our own visual language and stand out from the masses? In this workshop, we focus on connected AI workflows that move seamlessly from one tool to the next, showing you how to build a personal, flexible pipeline instead of relying on isolated prompts. Using a single AI-generated image as a starting point, we rewind the process: breaking it down, analyzing it, and reconstructing it step by step through an intensive, hands-on AI case study. This “Reverse Thinking” approach takes the final image back to its possible origins, revealing new directions, alternative ideas, and creative decisions along the way. You’ll learn how to extract meaningful steps that go far beyond prompting, and how to chain different AIs together to develop a complete project and even an entire portfolio from one idea. Along the way, we introduce new features and unconventional workflows not only from the usual AI tools, but also from emerging platforms and hybrid techniques that can become highly relevant for your next project. The focus is not on a single platform but on creating a connected workflow and placing human vision at the center of the process.
source_fields.description: Reverse Engineering with AI is a course that teaches designers to use reverse thinking to turn a single AI-generated image into ideas, sketches, 3D models, and animations. Students deconstruct an AI image using Krea Nodes and Realtime Editor and ChatGPT or Copilot as analytical tools, rebuild it into refined visuals and context boards with Midjourney and Formas.ai, convert results into clean, editable 3D models in Rhino, and produce final animations and a showreel with Morphic and Luma AI. The course is Beginner level and results in a complete project pipeline from a single image to a polished portfolio piece.
source_fields.objectives: Build connected AI workflows using Krea Nodes & Realtime Editor Reverse-engineer images using ChatGPT / Copilot as analytical design tools Create context boards, styles, and timelapse visuals with Formas Generate, refine, and train visual assets using Midjourney Turn AI images into clean, editable 3D models in Rhino Expand designs through parametric thinking, simulations, and optimization Develop animations and visual narratives with Morphic & Lumalabs Enhance and adapt visuals using Adobe Photoshop with AI
source_fields.methodology: From the first idea to moods, sketches, renderings, 3D models, 3D printing, animations, and finally a polished showreel, this workshop guides you through the entire creative pipeline using a hands-on case study. We share the complete workflow we’ve developed to create a project from scratch to finish, making every step transparent and applicable to your own work. We combine a range of AI tools, including Krea (Nodes & Realtime Editor), Formas (rendering styles, Freeform Studio, and 3D modeling), Midjourney, Morphic, and Lumalabs for animation, alongside Rhino for 3D conversion and optimization, and Autodesk tools for simulation and performance testing. Together, these form a cross-media workflow that bridges concept, design, and production. For us, it’s not about mastering a single AI. It’s about understanding how tools connect, how workflows evolve, and how human vision and authorship remain at the center of the process, guiding the machine rather than being led by it. Program: Introduction to the workshop concept and the “Reverse Thinking” approach Analysis of a single AI-generated image as the starting point Reverse-engineering the image back to moods, sketches, and ideas Creating visual content using connected AI tools (image, video, and animation) Expansion into parametric design, simulations, and technical refinement Creation of animations and motion sequences with different camera movements Compilation of results into a final presentation, showreel, or project output
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of connected AI workflows and reverse engineering, enabling you to transform single AI-generated visuals back into foundational ideas, editable 3D models, and animations. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated cross-media techniques is commendable.

This workshop teaches you to analyze the "DNA" of a design to reveal new directions and alternative ideas, allowing you to extract meaningful creative decisions. || I am worried about AI tools feeling disconnected. Will I learn how to combine these different platforms into a smooth process? :: This workshop demonstrates how to chain multiple tools together into a flexible pipeline. You will learn to move seamlessly from text to image, to 3D, and finally to animation. || Does this workshop prioritize human design intent? :: The methodology places human vision at the center of the process. By learning to "reverse engineer" and refine outputs step-by-step, you learn to guide the machine rather than being led by it || Will this workshop help me create a cohesive project for my portfolio, rather than just isolated images? :: The workshop is structured around a complete case study. By the end of the program, participants will have developed skills to create a full project narrative from initial analysis to 3D modeling and final animation. || Will this workshop teach me how to develop my own unique visual style? :: By analyzing and deconstructing existing visuals, you will learn to build a personal, flexible pipeline that prioritizes your specific creative vision.

courses.name: The AI-Native Architect

source_fields.name: The AI-Native Architect
source_fields.softwares: Gemini | Krea.AI | Nano Banana | Narva AI
source_fields.introduction: Three and a half years ago, if you were asked how AI fit into your architectural workflow, the answer was likely “not much.” Today, that answer looks very different. AI has moved from a curiosity to an essential tool, embedded across concept development, visualization, iteration, and decision-making. And if this shift happened in just a few years, the real question is where your workflow will be five years from now. In this masterclass, you’ll learn the exact processes and workflows we’ve implemented for leading brands such as Dolce & Gabbana, ETRO, and others. More importantly, you’ll explore how AI is set to reshape the architecture and design industry in the years ahead. You’ll work hands-on with the most advanced AI models, integration systems, and platforms, tools that can dramatically free up your time, sharpen your creative edge, and strengthen your design thinking and problem-solving. This masterclass has already been delivered to over 50 of the world’s top architecture, interior design, and retail companies. For the first time, it is now available to the public. It’s everything you need to build a solid foundation for integrating AI into your architectural process for the years to come.
source_fields.description: The AI-Native Architect is a course that teaches architects to integrate multimodal AI into real design workflows, from concept to final presentation. Using Krea.AI, Gemini, Nano Banana, and Narva AI, students design an entire project from scratch under real-world constraints, moving through AI-augmented concept development, floor-plan-only visualization, high-end presentation documents, and animated video generation for client presentations. The course is Beginner level and draws on workflows the instructor has implemented for brands including Dolce & Gabbana and ETRO.
source_fields.objectives: AI augmented and Human-Centred Concept Creative Development Designing an entire project from scratch with real-world constraints Understand the foundation of Multimodal AI and how to engage with it Create animated videos for a client presentation Create high-end presentation documents using AI High-end visualisation without a 3D model, with only a floor plan
source_fields.methodology: This masterclass covers the full spectrum of how AI can be integrated into an architectural project from the earliest stages of interpreting a brief through to producing client-ready visual and presentation material. The focus is on showing participants how AI can meaningfully contribute to creative thinking, spatial planning, visual communication, and design development across multiple stages of practice. The workshop will address how architects can use AI for concept generation, programme development, floor plan creation, spatial atmosphere studies, site and context visualisation, high-quality interior and exterior imagery, animated storytelling, and professional presentation output, all without the need for complex modelling or advanced software skills. Participants will gain an understanding of how multimodal AI systems can be applied to real architectural constraints and design challenges, enabling them to rethink traditional workflows and expand the way they approach design, iteration, and communication in their own projects. This workshop follows a brief-led, project-based methodology where participants design a complete architectural project from concept to final presentation using AI as an integrated design partner rather than a standalone tool. The session begins with understanding the project brief, constraints, and design intent, after which students progressively move through concept development, spatial planning, visualisation, refinement, and presentation, mirroring a real architectural workflow. Each stage introduces a specific AI workflow that corresponds to a traditional design phase: concept ideation through multimodal prompting, AI-assisted floor plan development, plan-to-visual translation without 3D modelling, iterative visual refinement, site and context visualisation, and finally presentation and video creation for client communication. Participants will work individually on their own version of the project to ensure hands-on learning and personal exploration of the tools. However, key moments throughout the workshop include group discussions, reviews, and feedback sessions where students can observe alternative approaches, prompting strategies, and design outcomes from others. This balance allows for personal experimentation while benefiting from shared learning and collective critique during the process.
