source_fields.softwares: Graphic Statics 3D | Grasshopper 3D | Human | LunchBox | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: Architectural facades have become one of the defining features of contemporary buildings. Beyond shaping a project's visual identity, they must also satisfy structural, environmental, functional, and financial requirements. As buildings become more complex, designing façade systems requires architects to balance aesthetics, performance, and constructability while managing countless interconnected design decisions. A parametric workflow offers an efficient solution by replacing manual modeling with a reusable algorithm capable of generating a digital twin of the façade. Instead of creating a single design, you will build a flexible parametric system that can generate a wide range of façade variations with adjustable parameters. Through real architectural case studies, you will learn how to translate façade details into algorithms that automate geometry creation while enabling rapid design exploration and consistent project documentation. In this workshop, you will build a complete Parametric Facade Generator from scratch using Grasshopper. You will learn practical techniques for creating panel systems, controlling façade patterns, generating architectural details, and organizing clean, scalable Grasshopper definitions. Alongside detailed 3D façade geometry, you will also generate optimized mesh models for visualization and automatically export CSV data containing panel information, material quantities, and cost estimates. By the end of the workshop, you will have a production-ready parametric design tool that can be adapted to future projects. The computational design techniques covered throughout the workshop extend beyond façade design and can be applied to a wide range of architectural and engineering workflows.
source_fields.description: Grasshopper Masterclass: Parametric Facade Generator is a 2-day advanced computational design workshop where participants build a complete facade generator tool from scratch in Grasshopper and Rhino 8. The workshop covers panel grid creation, data tree management, geometric transformation, metadata attachment, mesh optimization, and automated CSV export of panel quantities and cost data. All techniques are demonstrated through real architectural facade case studies using LunchBox, Human, and Graphic Statics 3D plugins.
source_fields.objectives: Creative algorithmic thinking and problem solving Building robust Grasshopper definitions Debugging complex algorithms in Grasshopper Working with geometric transformations Optimizing algorithms for performance Attaching metadata to generated geometry Automating repetitive workflows such as baking thousands of facade elements
source_fields.methodology: In this workshop, we will focus on developing parametric models in Grasshopper and organizing a large number of highly detailed façade elements in Rhino. This includes explaining many useful tips, tricks, and techniques for both Grasshopper and Rhino workflows. For example, we will cover data tree management, geometric transformations, reusable algorithms, attaching metadata to geometry, optimizing mesh geometry, and many other useful computational design techniques in Grasshopper. In Rhino, you will learn how to automatically bake and organize thousands of façade blocks generated by your algorithm. All of these parametric techniques will be demonstrated through real-world façade projects, allowing you to understand not only how the algorithms work, but also how they can be applied in professional architectural practice. The workshop is intended for architects, designers, engineers, and students who already have a basic understanding of Rhino and Grasshopper and would like to improve their computational design skills. Scope: The workshop will combine theoretical explanations, step-by-step demonstrations, and practical exercises. Each part will begin with a short introduction to the main design problem and the Grasshopper techniques that will be used to solve it. After that, the complete workflow will be demonstrated through a real-world facade example. The workshop will follow a gradual learning process. We will begin by defining the main façade parameters and studying the input geometry and architectural drawings. The next steps will include creating panel systems, generating detailed façade elements, and attaching relevant metadata to the geometry. The complete facade generator will be divided into smaller, clearly organized parts. This will allow students to understand each part of the algorithm separately before combining everything into a complete parametric system. Particular attention will be given to building clean, scalable, and efficient Grasshopper definitions that can manage a large number of façade elements. Students will follow the demonstrations and complete practical exercises individually. During the workshop, they will be encouraged to test different parameters, explore design variations, and adapt the demonstrated workflow to their own ideas. Program: Day 1: Building the Parametric Facade System Study façade details and define key design parameters. Create adjustable panel grids and surface subdivision systems. Learn data tree management for organizing façade components. Generate parametric panels, frames, openings, and supporting elements. Build a clean, scalable Grasshopper definition from scratch. Day 2: Optimization, Automation & Documentation Develop detailed façade elements, including mullions, joints, and corner conditions. Optimize Grasshopper definitions and create lightweight mesh geometry for visualization. Attach metadata, generate panel IDs, and calculate quantities and cost data. Export structured façade information to CSV files. Automatically bake and organize façade elements in Rhino using layers, blocks, and object attributes.
source_fields.requirements: Please note that the software installation process is not part of the workshop. Participants are expected to have Rhino 8 and Grasshopper installed before the workshop begins. The required Grasshopper plugins are Human and Graphic Statics 3D (3DGS).

Software installation is not covered during the workshop, so participants must have Rhino 8 and all plugins installed and working before Day 1. || What does the Parametric Facade Generator masterclass cover over two days? :: Day 1 focuses on analyzing facade drawings, defining key design parameters, creating adjustable panel grid systems, managing data trees, and building a clean scalable Grasshopper definition from scratch. Day 2 covers detailed facade element generation including mullions, joints, and corner conditions, mesh optimization for visualization, attaching metadata and panel IDs, calculating quantities and cost data, exporting CSV files, and automatically baking and organizing thousands of facade elements in Rhino using layers, blocks, and object attributes. || Is this Grasshopper masterclass suitable for beginners? :: This workshop is designed for architects, designers, engineers, and students who already have a basic working knowledge of Rhino and Grasshopper. Participants new to parametric design are encouraged to complete a Grasshopper beginner course first. The workshop focuses on intermediate to advanced computational techniques including data tree management, algorithm optimization, and automated documentation workflows. || What will I produce by the end of this parametric facade workshop? :: You will complete a fully functional parametric facade generator — a production-ready Grasshopper definition capable of generating complex facade variations with adjustable parameters. The tool outputs detailed 3D facade geometry in Rhino, optimized mesh models for visualization, and a structured CSV file containing panel IDs, material quantities, and cost estimates. The workflow is reusable and adaptable to future architectural and engineering projects.

source_fields.instructor_usernames: vlad-tenu | kostas-grigoriadis | Hamid | sonakshi-pandey | ingrid-paoletti | eric-wong | sarahaladayleh
source_fields.introduction: Step into the future of architecture and design with Design-Tech Talk 12, a two-day online event exploring the ideas, technologies, and innovations shaping the next generation of creative practice. Bringing together leading architects, designers, and innovators from around the world, the event highlights a diverse range of perspectives at the intersection of design and technology. Through engaging presentations and discussions, attendees will discover emerging tools, evolving workflows, and forward-thinking approaches that are transforming architecture and the broader design industry. Whether you are an architect, designer, student, researcher, or technology enthusiast, Design-Tech Talk 12 offers an opportunity to gain fresh insights, expand your perspective, and connect with a global community passionate about the future of design. An active membership is required to watch the recordings after the live event. Guest Speakers: Vlad Tenu Vlad Tenu is a Romanian-British architect, designer and artist based in London. His practice explores the intersection of architecture, research and making, investigating how computational design, natural systems and digital fabrication can generate new spatial possibilities. Moving fluidly between buildings, installations, public art, sculpture, modular systems and wearable art, his work reveals connections between geometry, materiality and fabrication across multiple scales. With 20 years of architectural experience, Vlad is currently an Associate at Allford Hall Monaghan Morris (AHMM). A graduate of The Bartlett UCL, where he also taught Architectural Computation, he has developed an internationally recognized body of work, receiving awards including the TEX-FAB Repeat Competition and AIA Houston Design Award. His projects have been exhibited at leading design platforms and institutions, including London, Milan and Shenzhen Design Weeks, the Royal Academy Summer Exhibition, and Swarovski Crystal Worlds, with collaborations featuring Swarovski and Björk. Kostas Grigoriadis Professor Kostas Grigoriadis is an ARB-registered architect and academic. His work explores the spatial and theoretical implications of using multi-materials in architecture, as well as the new paradigm of spatial and material continuity they enable. His practice, Continuum, provides building design services and has completed the construction of a tourist center in Anhui, China, for Cozoo Ltd. Continuum previously won the Spiretec competition for the design and construction of the 62,000-square-meter World Trade Center Noida in Delhi, India. Kostas studied Architecture at UCL, followed by a Master's in Architecture and Urbanism at the Architectural Association’s Design Research Laboratory. He has worked for Foster + Partners and Populous in London and held a Visiting Lectureship at the Royal College of Art, where he also completed a PhD in Architecture by Project, focusing on multi-material design methodologies. He taught a design studio at the Architectural Association from 2010 to 2023. He is currently Professor of Multi-Material Architecture and Co-Director of Architecture MArch (ARB/RIBA Part 2) at the Bartlett School of Architecture, UCL, and Associate Editor of Architecture Intelligence (Springer). He is the co-author of 3D Printing and Material Extrusion in Architecture, and the editor of Mixed Matters: A Multi-Material Design Compendium, published by Jovis Verlag in June 2016. His awards include the Ivan Petrovic Prize (eCAADe 2014), the Arup Prize for Emerging Talent in Architecture—Special Mention (Royal Academy Summer Exhibition, 2016), the RIBA President’s Award for Design and Technical Research (2018), and the Google R+D in the Built Environment Fellowship (2019). Sonakshi Pandey Sonakshi Pandey is an architectural designer exploring the boundaries of computational design and digital fabrication. Her practice lives at the intersection of generative design and making, testing how complex geometric algorithms translate into physical form. Currently, she is experimenting with the material behavior of 3D printing on fabric, investigating how rigid computational patterns integrate with flexible textiles to create performative structures. Was recently a Resident in the Autodesk Research Residency Program, where she integrated robotic workflows into fabrication practices. Completed her Master of Advanced Architectural Design in Digital Crafts and Fabrication from the California College of the Arts (CCA). Sonakshi also holds a Master of Architecture from the University of Newcastle, Australia. Her ongoing research in additive manufacturing continues to develop new methods of fabrication. Ingrid Maria Paoletti Ingrid Paoletti is Full Professor of Architectural Technology at Politecnico di Milano, where she also earned her PhD in Construction Technology. She has conducted research as an associate researcher at MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) and is the founder of Material Balance , a research group focused on theoretical and design experimentation with innovative technologies and materials for a new and responsible material culture. She has served as Vice-Rector for Expo Dubai 2020 and Vice President of the Politecnico di Milano Foundation. She collaborates with several international universities and research centers, including KTH, KDAK, and the Gloknos Center. In 2022, she was a speaker at TEDxMilano. Since 2023, she has been the Rector's Delegate for Exhibitions and Events, and in 2025 she curated the Material Bank for the 19th edition of the Venice Biennale. Her publications include L'innovazione consapevole (Maggioli, 2012), Advanced Customization in Architectural Design and Construction (with R. Naboni, Springer, 2015), Material Balance: A Design Equation (Springer, 2020), and Siate Materialisti! (Einaudi, 2021). Eric Wong Eric studied Art and Architecture at the Byam Shaw School of Art, Central Saint Martins. He completed his undergraduate degree at Cardiff University and later earned a master's degree from the Bartlett School of Architecture, UCL. Eric was nominated for the RIBA President's Silver Medal and is a recipient of the Bartlett School of Architecture Medal for outstanding academic achievements in professional performance, the Sir Banister Fletcher Medal for highest marks in Part 2 graduate studies, and the Fitzroy Robinson Drawing Prize for best drawings in Part 2 graduate studies. He later completed his Part III professional studies at the University of Cambridge, where he qualified as an Architect. Eric is a practicing Architect who has worked at CJ Lim Studio 8 Architects and Allford Hall Monaghan Morris Architects on a range of projects of varying scales and complexities. He is also a senior lecturer and architecture design tutor who has taught at UCL: Bartlett School of Architecture and the University of Greenwich at undergraduate and postgraduate level, respectively. Eric has also been a visiting critic to the Architectural Association, University of Westminster, Aarhus School of Architecture, The Cooper Union, Carnegie Mellon University of Architecture, University of Johannesburg Graduate School of Architecture, and the National University of Singapore Department of Architecture. Eric’s work has been widely published and exhibited in the RIBA Journal, Architects Journal, Blueprint Magazine, and VICE, through to the Design Museum, World Architecture Festival, and Sir John Soane Museum. He has also worked with Oscar-nominated Director Mamoru Hosoda as the concept artist and production designer for the award-winning animated feature film ‘Belle ’, where he designed the virtual world known in the film as U. His architectural journey has been influenced by critical thinking, speculative world-building, and intricate line drawings. Sarah Aladayleh Sarah Aladayleh is an architect and urbanist based in London. As a Design Lead at Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG), she leads large-scale urban design and masterplanning projects across the Middle East and the UK. Her design methodology explores the intersection of spatial frameworks and visual storytelling. Alongside her architectural career, Sarah is a published illustrator. Her work has been commissioned and exhibited internationally by the Institut du Monde Arabe in France, the Cultural Foundation in Abu Dhabi, and the Sharjah Art Foundation.

courses.name: Richard Hassell - Rethinking Architecture

source_fields.name: Richard Hassell - Rethinking Architecture
source_fields.introduction: In an era defined by rapid urbanization, climate challenges, and growing populations, architecture must do more than provide shelter. It has the responsibility to reconnect cities with nature, improve environmental performance, and create healthier places for people to live and work. Through thoughtful design, buildings can become living systems that contribute to the resilience of entire urban environments. As contemporary cities continue to evolve, the integration of landscape, climate-responsive strategies, and sustainable technologies is reshaping how architecture is conceived. Rather than treating nature as an addition, the most innovative projects embed it into the very fabric of buildings, creating spaces that enhance biodiversity, improve wellbeing, and strengthen the relationship between people and their environment. Today, architecture is measured not only by its aesthetic qualities but also by its ecological impact and social value. By combining environmental intelligence with design excellence, architects have the opportunity to create cities that are greener, more resilient, and better prepared for the future.
source_fields.description: Richard Hassell - Rethinking Architecture is a free lecture in which Richard Hassell, co-founder of WOHA Architects, explores climate-responsive architecture and the future of sustainable urban living. The one-hour session includes a 45-minute talk followed by a 15-minute live Q&A, covering biophilic design principles, passive strategies for dense urban settings, and lessons from WOHA's landmark sustainable projects. The lecture is free to attend and open to all levels.
source_fields.objectives: Core design principles behind climate-responsive and biophilic architecture. Methods for embedding nature and passive design strategies into dense urban settings. Key insights and lessons learned from landmark sustainable design projects. Future-focused frameworks for building resilient, human-centered communities.
source_fields.methodology: Richard Hassell, co-founder of WOHA Architects, has established one of the world's leading architectural practices dedicated to sustainable, climate-responsive, and biophilic design. His work explores how architecture can integrate nature, technology, and urban density to create buildings that improve environmental performance while enriching the everyday lives of their occupants. From award-winning residential towers and mixed-use developments to cultural and civic projects, WOHA's portfolio demonstrates a pioneering approach to designing vertical communities where greenery, natural ventilation, and public space become essential architectural elements. Through decades of innovation, Richard Hassell has helped redefine the future of tropical urbanism and sustainable city-making. Join us on Friday, September 25th at 10:00 GMT as PAACADEMY hosts Richard Hassell for an exclusive 45-minute open talk , followed by a 15-minute live Q&A . During the session, he will present key projects and share insights into WOHA's design philosophy, innovative approach to biophilic architecture, and the strategies shaping the future of resilient, sustainable cities.

source_fields.name: AI-Powered Interior Design in Architecture 3.0
source_fields.softwares: Claude AI | Flora AI | Formas.ai | Magnific AI | Midjourney | Nano Banana
source_fields.introduction: This workshop teaches a complete AI workflow for architectural design, from the first concept to a fully presented project. Rather than creating isolated AI images, you will learn how to develop a consistent architectural proposal that includes exterior views, interior spaces, walkthrough videos, and professional project documentation. Through a structured process, you will combine leading AI tools to generate concepts, maintain visual consistency, enhance image quality, produce animations, and automate project documentation. By the end of the workshop, you will have a repeatable workflow you can apply to future architectural and interior design projects.
source_fields.description: AI-Powered Interior Design in Architecture 3.0 is a 2-day online workshop that teaches a structured AI workflow for architectural design projects. Using Claude AI, Midjourney, Flora AI, Nanobanana, Magnific, and Formas, participants develop a single concept into a complete architectural proposal including exterior views, interior spaces, walkthrough videos, and professional presentation boards. The workflow is designed to be reusable on future projects.
source_fields.objectives: Build a complete architectural project from a single design concept. Generate consistent exterior and interior visualizations using multiple AI tools. Create AI-powered walkthrough videos and architectural presentations. Develop reusable AI workflows with Claude AI and Flora. Enhance renders and maintain visual consistency with Nanobanana and Magnific. Produce professional documentation, material schedules, and presentation assets using AI.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop follows a structured end-to-end AI workflow where every tool has a specific role within a single design process. You will begin by defining the project's concept, visual language, materials, and design narrative using Claude AI. Early concepts for both exterior and interior spaces will then be explored in Midjourney, while Flora AI organizes the entire workflow into a clear node-based process that is easy to understand and reuse. Once the design direction is established, Nanobanana is used to maintain visual consistency across all project images, while Magnific enhances and refines renders to presentation quality. Finally, Formas brings the project together by generating diagrams, sketch-to-image workflows, multiple viewpoints, 3D visualizations, and cinematic walkthrough videos. Claude AI then completes the workflow by generating presentation boards, material schedules, and project documentation. This methodology enables participants to transform a single concept into a complete architectural presentation using an efficient and repeatable AI-driven workflow. Program: Day 1 - Building the Design Workflow Define the project concept, architectural language, materials, and prompts using Claude AI. Generate and refine exterior and interior design concepts with Midjourney. Organize the complete workflow inside Flora AI using a node-based visual process. Build reusable Claude AI assistants to maintain style consistency across the project. Produce cohesive architectural images with Nanobanana and establish a unified visual language. Day 2 - Visualization, Video & Project Delivery Refine, edit, and upscale presentation-quality renders using Magnific and Nanobanana. Generate diagrams, multiple viewpoints, sketch-to-image workflows, and 3D visualizations with Formas. Create cinematic walkthrough videos from plans, layouts, and AI-generated imagery. Automate project books, presentation slides, material schedules, and supporting documentation using Claude AI. Assemble a complete architectural presentation including exterior views, interior spaces, videos, and final deliverables ready for clients or portfolios.

courses.name: Living Geometry: Deployable Systems with Grasshopper

source_fields.name: Living Geometry: Deployable Systems with Grasshopper
source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: Adaptive and deployable systems are opening new possibilities in architecture by enabling spaces and structures to transform in response to different needs and conditions. Behind these dynamic behaviors lies geometry - not simply as a way to create form, but as a system that can generate movement. In this workshop, participants will explore how scissor-based geometry can be used to design transformable architectural systems through computational design. Starting from the fundamental principles of scissor mechanisms, we will gradually build parametric models in Grasshopper and investigate how geometric patterns can evolve into deployable and adaptive structures. Grasshopper was chosen for this workshop because it allows designers to work directly with geometric relationships, test different design variations, and simulate movement in an intuitive visual environment. Instead of repeatedly rebuilding models, participants will learn how to develop flexible systems that can be modified, explored, and refined throughout the design process. By the end of the workshop, participants will have created their own deployable geometric system and gained a practical workflow applicable to responsive architecture, kinetic structures, and other computational design projects.
source_fields.description: This workshop introduces parametric scissor-based geometry in Grasshopper for designing, modeling, and transforming adaptive, deployable architectural systems.
source_fields.objectives: Understand the basic logic and geometric principles of scissor-based deployable systems Model and control scissor mechanisms through parametric workflows in Grasshopper Create flexible geometric systems by defining relationships between form, movement, and parameters Explore how repetitive patterns can be transformed into deployable architectural structures Develop computational approaches for designing kinetic and adaptive systems Use Grasshopper as a tool for exploring and testing different geometric possibilities
source_fields.methodology: This workshop focuses on the design of adaptive and deployable architectural systems using scissor-based geometry and parametric modeling. Rather than developing a single predefined project, participants will learn a computational workflow applicable to a wide range of design applications, from kinetic pavilions and transformable canopies to responsive façades and experimental spatial installations. Participants will build parametric scissor units, study their geometric behavior, and combine them into deployable systems capable of controlled transformation. Through a series of guided exercises, they will learn how to organize geometric relationships, define movement through parametric constraints, and generate different design variations from a single computational model. By the end of the workshop, each participant will have developed a fully parametric, deployable system, along with a design concept demonstrating how the workflow can be adapted to different architectural scales and applications. Scope: The workshop follows a step-by-step, hands-on computational design workflow that combines geometric exploration, parametric modeling, and design development. 1. Introduction to Scissor-Based Geometry Introduction to deployable and kinetic architectural systems Understanding the geometric principles behind scissor mechanisms Exploring the relationship between geometry, movement, and transformation 2. Parametric Modeling in Grasshopper Building basic scissor units through parametric definitions Establishing geometric relationships and controlling design parameters Exploring different configurations through computational modeling 3. Developing Deployable Geometric Systems Combining scissor units into larger geometric configurations Studying transformation behavior and movement logic Exploring how repetitive patterns can generate adaptive structures 4. Design Exploration and Computational Workflow Testing variations of deployable systems through parametric control Understanding how the developed workflow can be applied to different architectural applications Discussing potential applications in kinetic structures, adaptive installations, and transformable systems Program: Day 1 - Understanding and Modeling Scissor-Based Systems Introduction Workshop goals and overall computational design workflow Introduction to Scissor Mechanisms Definitions, applications, and geometric principles Exploring kinetic logic through selected examples Translational Scissor Mechanism Understanding linear transformation logic Developing geometric relationships Modeling a parametric scissor unit in Grasshopper 3D Scissor Mechanism Exploring spatial configurations Analyzing geometric behavior Expanding the basic unit into a 3D system Polar Scissor Mechanism Studying radial transformation logic Developing polar configurations through parametric modeling Angular Scissor Mechanism Exploring angular configurations Modeling scissor-based geometric variations in Grasshopper Wrap-up & Q&A Reviewing the developed systems and key concepts Day 2 - From Geometric Patterns to Adaptive Transformations Introduction to Repetitive Geometries Exploring the logic of repetitive geometric patterns Investigating their potential for dynamic configurations Geometric Pattern Transformation Transforming static patterns into movable and adaptive systems Pattern-Based Motion Studies Developing animated geometric patterns Exploring different transformation behaviors Creating Dynamic Pattern Systems Applying transformation strategies Generating opening and closing behaviors within geometric patterns Adaptive Geometric Applications Exploring applications in architectural elements Investigating kinetic and transformable systems Wrap-up & Q&A Reviewing the workshop process and discussing further design possibilities

source_fields.faq: Which software is used in this Grasshopper computational design course? :: The workshop uses Rhinoceros 3D and Grasshopper 3D as the primary tools. Participants also work with two Grasshopper plugins: Anemone for looping and animation of movement sequences, and Weaverbird for mesh topology operations. All software must be installed and tested before Day 1. Workshop materials and resource files are provided to all participants. || What does the Living Geometry deployable systems workshop cover across two days? :: Day 1 introduces the geometric principles of scissor mechanisms and progresses through four types of parametric scissor units: translational, 3D, polar, and angular. Each is modeled and controlled in Grasshopper. Day 2 shifts to repetitive geometric patterns and how they can be transformed into adaptive, deployable systems with opening and closing behaviors. The workshop concludes with architectural application discussions and design variations. || Do I need prior Grasshopper experience to join this workshop? :: Basic familiarity with Rhinoceros 3D and Grasshopper is expected, as the workshop moves directly into parametric modeling from Day 1. courses.name: Tensegrity and Tensile Membranes in Kangaroo

source_fields.name: Tensegrity and Tensile Membranes in Kangaroo
source_fields.introduction: This workshop will introduce participants to computational modeling approaches using Rhino and Grasshopper to design and simulate deployable structures. The workflow will move through a series of design studies ranging from simple to more complex designs. Beginning with simple scissor mechanisms for deployment, to more complex systems of hyperbolic and tensegrity structures. The participants will also investigate how membrane surfaces can be integrated as active elements contributing to the movement and equilibrium of the structures. Grasshopper and Kangaroo will be used to study how these types of structures move and simulate the tensioned membrane materials. The participants will learn how to control the various parameters to build complexity and generate animations of their designs to study the materials and structures. The workshop will also introduce methods for translating the models into simple physical prototypes to assess simulation accuracy. By the end of the workshop, participants will have developed a set of parametric definitions and designs for deployable systems. The goal is to provide learners with a conceptual understanding of the possibilities for scissor mechanisms and tension membranes to be used in the design of adaptive and lightweight structures and architectural designs. Setting up a practical workflow from computational design and simulation to physical prototypes.
source_fields.description: Tensegrity and Tensile Membranes in Kangaroo is a workshop that teaches designers to design, simulate, and prototype deployable tensegrity and membrane structures using Rhino, Grasshopper, and Kangaroo. Across two days, students build parametric scissor mechanisms, simulate tensioned membrane surfaces with Kangaroo physics, develop hyperbolic and tensegrity systems, produce deployment animations, and translate their digital simulations into physical prototypes. The workshop is Beginner level and includes recommendations for prototyping materials such as wood dowels and stretchy fabric.
source_fields.objectives: Understanding the principles of deployable structures in architecture (particularly scissor mechanisms) Develop parametric workflows in Rhino and Grasshopper to create scissor mechanisms that deploy and collapse Use Kangaroo physics to simulate membrane surfaces attached to deployable structures Control various design variables to develop new designs and influence deployable behaviors Simulation of Tensegrity in Grasshopper and Kangaroo with membrane surfaces Producing animations of deployment and movement Ability to translate design simulations into physical prototypes
source_fields.methodology: The workshop will be broken into parts, first looking at references for deployable systems and particularly focusing on scissor mechanisms. The first simulations will be 2 dimensional and will go over the basic types of scissor mechanisms and movements. The next step will be adding membrane materials to this by using Kangaroo to simulate mesh relaxation. The membrane material will follow and connect to the expanding and contracting scissor forms. The Second part will be exploring in 3 dimensions with hyperbolic deployable systems; these will add more complexity and include Grasshopper and Kangaroo to again transform the base geometry and gain an understanding of the variety of variables and controls to transform these geometries. The next portion will be to combine these with membranes as well as adding aggregation and repetition of modules. The final part will be a study of tensegrity systems where the membranes act in tension and linear struts are in compression. These forms are deployed through the activation of the membranes and structures to deploy and reach a structural equilibrium state. This will allow learners to understand structural arrangements as well as deployable forms for tensegrity modules in Grasshopper. Finally, suggestions and workflow to translate these designs into physical prototypes will be addressed and discussed. To provide opportunities to study and understand the physical principles further. Throughout the workshop, step-by-step instruction on making Grasshopper code will be provided. As well as discussion of the structural systems behind the designs and bringing in precedents and built examples, including deployable roofs and satellite forms from space travel. The studies ultimately will combine theory with the instruction of tools and methods. Scope: The workshop will introduce topics with lectures and precedents describing the goals for geometry to be created. As well as step-by-step instructions for developing the desired Grasshopper code for each of the pre-determined base forms. The results will allow students to deviate by adjusting a variety of parameters and scales, allowing them to individually develop their own designs. Ultimately, the workshop will emphasize iterative design and working back and forth between the digital design simulations and testing results with physical study models and prototypes, allowing participants to work with a variety of materials that they may have available at hand to re-create their desired designs. Group discussions of the results at each phase will offer an opportunity for participants to share and demonstrate their work. Opportunities will also be available to receive feedback and support for their individual developments. Program: Day 1: Foundations of 2D & 3D Deployable Scissor Systems Introduction to deployable systems: Understanding scissor mechanisms Basic Grasshopper workflow 2D scissor mechanisms in Grasshopper Introduction to precedents and examples Adding membrane simulation in Kangaroo 3D scissor aggregation in Grasshopper Discussion on physical prototypes Final questions and conclusions Day 2: Hyperbolic Geometry, Tensegrity & Motion Simulation Introduction to deployable hyperbolic forms Grasshopper coding of hyperbolic forms Adding membranes to simulation Animating simulations Introduction to tensegrity and structural configurations Grasshopper coding for tensegrity modules with tensile membranes Discussion on physical prototypes Final questions and conclusions
source_fields.notes: Physical materials for prototypes, such as wood dowels, stretchy fabric, paper, and other tools, are recommended.
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced architectural design software, enabling you to create captivating materials and efficiently render projects. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: What prerequisite skills or software knowledge do I need to attend? :: A basic familiarity with Rhino and Grasshopper is recommended to get the most out of the workshop. While coding sessions will be guided step by step, prior exposure to parametric concepts will help you follow along more smoothly as we transition to physics simulation with Kangaroo. || What physical materials do I need to prepare for the prototyping sessions? :: You can use readily available physical materials at home or in your studio. Recommended items include wooden dowels or skewers (for compression struts and scissor arms), stretchy fabrics like lycra/spandex (for active membranes), rubber bands or string, paper, fasteners/pins, and basic cutting tools. || Do I need to purchase any additional software or plugins? :: No extra software purchases are necessary. You will only need Rhinoceros 3D (version 6, 7, or 8) installed on your computer. Grasshopper and Kangaroo Physics are built natively into recent versions of Rhino. || Will I learn how to create motion graphics or export animations of my designs? :: Yes. On Day 2, the workshop explicitly covers how to capture and animate your digital physics simulations in Grasshopper, allowing you to showcase the expanding, contracting, and equilibrium behaviors of your deployable structures in motion. || Will I leave the workshop with reusable computational files? :: Yes. By the end of the two-day session, you will have built a complete library of custom, working Grasshopper and Kangaroo definitions covering 2D/3D scissor mechanisms, hyperbolic deployable modules, and tensegrity systems with integrated tensile membranes.

courses.name: Multi-Scalar Urbanism: Concept Buildups with AI

source_fields.name: Multi-Scalar Urbanism: Concept Buildups with AI
source_fields.softwares: Adobe Illustrator | Adobe InDesign | Gemini | Krea.AI | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: Masterplans are built up in layers: a framework in plan, a gesture in volume, and a story tying the two together. These layers, whether extracted from context, narrative, environment, or formal gestures, can be sequentially represented in a concept buildup. On an urban scale, framework layers identify the core ingredients of a concept's expression. From mobility and superplots down to plots and buildings, these elements dictate zoning and spatial languages. This workshop teaches the critical skill of extracting and filtering these layers with clarity, using the sequential thinking needed to express a masterplan in a multi-scalar lense. Urban diagramming is treated as a storytelling skill here: a masterplan's logic legible through its story, shown step by step. Participants will work from a provided demo masterplan project, or their own personal urban project, to extract/create layers. These layers will then be expressed into an axonometric sequence at the urban scale, sequenced as an annotated pitch deck, and finally animated into a dynamic concept buildup using AI.
source_fields.description: Multi-Scalar Urbanism: Concept Buildups with AI is a 2-day workshop on PAACADEMY led by Sarah Aladayleh, Architect and Design Lead at Bjarke Ingels Group. Participants use Rhino, Adobe Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere Pro, and AI tools like Krea and Gemini to deconstruct masterplans into multi-scalar frameworks, create annotated axonometric sequences, and generate animated concept buildups. Basic Rhino knowledge is sufficient, and no prior video editing experience is required.
source_fields.objectives: How to read and deconstruct a masterplan into its layered plan framework, including blocks, grids, superplots, and individual plots. How to translate a framework into a volumetric gesture buildup in an axonometric view. How to diagram design reasoning as a clear sequence so a concept reads as a persuasive buildup. How to produce clear, annotated diagrams and format them into a sequential pitch deck. How to use AI to animate a concept buildup.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop is structured as a live studio where participants can choose to work from one shared demo masterplan or use their personal urban projects to mirror the buildup approach. Participants can work individually or be assigned a different workstream from the same base project. (Dependant on number of students) Step 1: Principles, Frameworks & Multi-scalar Urbanism An introductory presentation covering urban design principles, frameworks, and multi-scalar case studies (BIG). An intro to the demo masterplan project and its underlying story is introduced as a reading framework. Step 2: Axonometric Build-up Extracting or creating additional layers of a masterplan into a volumetric axonometric buildup. Each student develops a sequence of axonometric steps that show how the masterplan gesture forms. Step 3: The Deck Diagrams are annotated, then laid out as an axo sequence. This creates a short, sharp pitch sequence telling the story of the masterplan. Step 4: The Animation Krea or Gemini will be used to input the buildup stills, allowing AI to fill in the increments between steps. Adobe premiere is then used if needed to stitch the video outputs and tweak as needed. Program: Day 1: Introductory presentation on urban design principles, frameworks, multi-scalar case studies, and storytelling in urbanism. Framing the workshop and the importance of a concept buildup. Introduction to the demo masterplan project. Live demonstration of extracting the plan-layer buildup (grid/blocks to superplots to plots to buildings) step by step. Storyboarding the concept sequence logic based on design and narrative. Setting up Rhino cameras for the sequence. Day 2: Recap of Day 1 plan sequences. Rhino model and axonometric export workflow to turn moves into a volumetric buildup base. Sequencing the axonometric gesture buildup step by step. InDesign or Illustrator workflows for editing and annotating the axonometric linework. Animating in AI (Krea or Gemini) to generate the incremental buildup steps.
source_fields.requirements: Only basic knowledge is needed in Rhinoceros 3D.
source_fields.notes: Students can work from a demo masterplan project or use their own personal urban project to extract a concept build-up Final deliverable: step-by-step concept build-up + sequenced animation.
source_fields.certificate_text: Congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online course. This course provided foundational knowledge of Rhinoceros 3D, Adobe Creative Suite, and AI animation tools , empowering you to build multi-scalar urban masterplans and volumetric axonometric sequences and integrate them into persuasive visual storytelling and architectural pitch presentations . Your commitment to mastering AI-driven concept animation and developing adaptable workflows within this innovative design space is truly commendable.
source_fields.faq: Can I use my own project instead of the demo masterplan? :: Yes. You can work with the provided demo project or apply the methodology to your own urban masterplan. || How much Rhino experience is required? :: You need to navigate the 3D space, extract clean linework, and export white-model camera views. || What if I have never used Krea or Premiere Pro before? :: Prior video experience isn't necessary. The instructors demonstrate how to feed static diagram frames into the AI tools to generate the transitions, then stitch them together. || What is the final deliverable at the end of the two days? :: You will produce a sequenced, annotated axonometric pitch deck and a short animated video showing your masterplan’s step-by-step concept buildup. || Do I need paid AI subscriptions or high-end hardware? :: No special hardware is needed beyond a computer that runs Rhinoceros3D and Adobe software. Free or basic web accounts for Krea and Gemini are sufficient for the workshop.

courses.name: Neural Vernacular: Bio-Responsive Design

source_fields.name: Neural Vernacular: Bio-Responsive Design
source_fields.introduction: As emerging technologies blur the boundaries between biology, computation, and spatial design, designers must move beyond static forms toward responsive, living systems. This workshop investigates the novel concept of ‘Neural Vernacular’, a speculative design approach where biological signals (instead of raw earth) directly inform material, wearable, and architectural logic. To bridge rapid conceptualization with computational design, we pair generative AI with parametric modeling. Midjourney serves as an ideation tool, allowing students to quickly imagine and iterate complex, speculative visuals without the technical limitations. We then transition into Rhino 3D and Grasshopper to ground those visions into precise, algorithmic geometries. By integrating Arduino and simulated bio-signal workflows, students learn how physiological data translates into dynamic parametric parameters, giving them a practical foundation in responsive, bio-integrated design without requiring physical lab hardware.
source_fields.description: Neural Vernacular: Bio-Responsive Design is a workshop that teaches designers to explore AI-driven, bio-integrated design through parametric modeling and simulated biological signals. Students use Midjourney for speculative visualization, then translate concepts into algorithmic geometry in Rhino and Grasshopper, using Arduino and simulated bio-signal workflows to drive dynamic parametric parameters without requiring physical lab hardware. The workshop is Beginner level and results in a set of speculative, bio-responsive parametric designs.
source_fields.objectives: Utilise AI image generators to visualise complex design concepts. Translate speculative biological concepts into parametric geometries. Mathematically simulate neural signals within the Grasshopper environment. Explore responsive design workflows driven by simulated biological data.
source_fields.methodology: This workshop will encompass an exciting focus on speculative design. Attendees will explore the theoretical foundations of the concept of neural vernacular, examine sensor technology and biological signal translation, and apply parametric design logic to generate complex geometries. It also integrates visual speculation and provides critical takeaways on future technological outlooks. Following a brief theoretical introduction, we will jump into speculative visualization leveraging AI image generation tools such as Midjourney to establish a conceptual vision and aesthetic direction. The parametric form-finding workflow will then allow us to translate these ideas into speculative geometries using Rhino and Grasshopper. Finally, the simulation and computational integration portion of the workshop will take mathematically simulated internal biological signals to drive responsive, parametric parameters within the digital models. After that, we will look at the next steps of how students could potentially prototype and fabricate their designs with methods like 3D printing technology. Program: Introduction and theoretical framework on Neural Vernacular. Speculative visualization using Midjourney to develop conceptual vision. Parametric modeling tutorial in Rhino and Grasshopper. Workflow mapping for simulated biological signals. Review, Q&A, and future outlook.
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced architectural design software, enabling you to create captivating materials and efficiently render projects. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: Which software and tools are used in this workshop? :: The workshop uses Midjourney for AI-driven concept visualization, Rhinoceros 3D and Grasshopper for parametric modeling, and Arduino IDE to structure simulated bio-signal workflows. || What exactly is covered in the curriculum? :: The program moves from a theoretical introduction to Neural Vernacular through speculative visualization in Midjourney, a parametric modeling tutorial in Rhino and Grasshopper, and workflow mapping for simulated biological signals, ending with a review and future outlook session. || Do I need physical lab hardware or sensors to attend? :: No. The workshop uses mathematically simulated bio-signal workflows within Grasshopper, so you build a practical foundation in responsive, bio-integrated design without needing any physical lab equipment. || What will I produce by the end of the workshop? :: A set of speculative, parametric design concepts that translate simulated biological signals into material, wearable, or architectural geometry, developed across the full workflow from AI-driven ideation to algorithmic form-finding.

source_fields.name: Architecture in Motion: AI Cinematic Workflows
source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | ChatGPT | Claude AI | Gemini
source_fields.membership_plans: Full Access | Pro Monthly | Pro Yearly | Pro Quarterly
source_fields.introduction: This workshop introduces practical workflows for using AI as a personal architectural visualization assistant to develop architectural hero images from scratch and explore how these images can be extended into short cinematic sequences using AI. Students will learn to build and train their own customized GPT based on their design goals, visual language, and workflow. They will then learn how to use AI image-generation workflows to transform sketches, models, and screenshots into cinematic architectural hero images based on the project's story and concept. After the workshop, students won't just have ready-to-use workflows. They will learn how to build and train their own workflows from scratch. Students will learn the principles and skills behind these workflows, allowing them to use their own creativity to adapt, experiment, and develop new workflows that fit their own needs, language, and creative style. The goal is not simply to use a workflow, but to learn how to create and evolve workflows independently.
source_fields.description: Architecture in Motion: AI Cinematic Workflows is a course that teaches architects to build personalized AI workflows and direct architectural visuals from sketches and 3D models into cinematic hero images. Students train their own custom GPT using Claude AI, ChatGPT, and Gemini, then apply a repeatable Define, Build, Direct, Generate, Iterate, Refine workflow with Adobe Photoshop and 3ds Max to control camera angle, materials, lighting, and composition, finishing with a brief exploration of turning a hero image into a short cinematic sequence. The course is Beginner level and results in a personalized, reusable AI visualization workflow.
source_fields.objectives: Build a personalized AI workflow for architectural visualization. Create effective prompts for architectural image generation. Transform 3D models and sketches into cinematic hero images. Refine and direct AI-generated visuals while preserving design intent.
source_fields.methodology: The workshop focuses on contemporary architectural visualization, with an emphasis on residential, hospitality, conceptual architecture, and urban projects. Students will work with a range of inputs, including 3D screenshots, sketches, massing studies, and existing architectural images, and learn how to turn them into cinematic hero shots while maintaining the original architectural intent. The workshop is based on a simple, repeatable workflow: Define → Build → Direct → Generate → Iterate → Refine Students will: Build a personalized trainable GPT for their own architectural workflow. Learn how to describe architecture, atmosphere, materials, lighting, and composition effectively. Develop essential prompting frameworks for architectural image generation. Transform 3D model screenshots and sketches into cinematic hero images. Control camera angle, composition, materials, lighting, landscape, and atmosphere. Learn image-to-image, text-to-image, and reference-based workflows for greater visual consistency. Refine and present final images using AI and post-production tools. Explore a simple workflow for transforming a final hero image into a short cinematic sequence. Program: AI Visualization System: Build a personalized GPT and establish your visual workflow. Prompting & Direction: Learn how to communicate architecture, composition, materials, lighting, and atmosphere. Hero Image Generation: Transform sketches and 3D screenshots into cinematic architectural visuals. Iteration & Refinement: Develop variations, improve realism, and maintain architectural consistency. Final Hero Shot & AI Film: Complete a final architectural hero image and briefly explore AI-generated cinematic video.

courses.name: Eco-Parametric Architecture

source_fields.name: Eco-Parametric Architecture
source_fields.instructors: Arthur Mamou-Mani | Fun Yuen | Clinton Mendonca
source_fields.introduction: This workshop demonstrates integrated methods for leveraging parametric tools and circular materials to translate initial design concepts into production-ready physical structures and examine how these systems can be disassembled for future reuse. Participants will discover how to construct modular Grasshopper algorithms shaped by material volume, curvature, and joint logic. They will subsequently learn how to convert complex geometry into robotic toolpaths and G-code tailored for large-scale 3D printing with recycled compounds. Upon completing the course, attendees will gain far more than pre-packaged scripts. They will master the ability to engineer and refine complete digital-to-physical pipelines on their own. Attendees will grasp the core algorithmic logic and physical constraints driving these processes, empowering them to innovate, test, and design custom fabrication strategies tailored to their unique architectural vision and material requirements. The objective is not merely to execute a pre-designed script, but to develop the skills needed to formulate and advance circular design frameworks autonomously.
source_fields.description: Eco-Parametric Architecture is an intermediate workshop that teaches designers to build parametric systems and convert initial concepts into fabrication-ready circular structures. Participants use Rhino 8, Grasshopper, and RunChat to apply a modularize, path, print, and reuse workflow controlling geometry, connections, and material limits, finishing with disassembly testing to leave with a personalized, reusable circular design workflow.
source_fields.objectives: Translate briefs into parametric systems. Shape geometry using material behavior. Control modules and fabrication limits in Grasshopper. Prepare components for robotic 3D printing. Account for layer heights, overhangs, and print orientation. Convert digital geometry into toolpaths and G-code. Design for assembly, disassembly, and circular reuse. Use AI exploration without sacrificing geometric precision.
source_fields.methodology: Participants will develop a new modular architectural system created specifically for the workshop. It will draw on principles from Mamou-Mani’s architectural projects and Fab.Pub’s circular-material research without reproducing client work or disclosing proprietary files. The project will progress through concept development, parametric modelling, material constraints, modularisation, robotic toolpathing, assembly and future reuse. The material focus will be large-scale 3D printing with reclaimed or recycled compounds. Available material volume, print bed size, layer height, minimum curvature, overhang analysis, connections, print direction, and disassembly requirements will inform the design and fabrication strategy. A 45-minute live revision session will take place two weeks after the workshop to check your progress and answer any remaining questions. Students will: Interpret an architectural brief and define its regenerative-material objectives. Use AI-assisted exploration to test design directions and visualise the system in context. Develop an adaptable architectural system in Rhino and Grasshopper. Translate material and fabrication constraints into geometry, modules and connections. Prepare a selected component for robotic fabrication and large-scale 3D printing. Reassemble the components and evaluate disassembly, reprocessing and future reuse. Demonstrate RunChat as a bridge between precise parametric geometry and rapid visual iteration. Program Day 1: Brief to Parametric System Block 1 - From Brief to System: Introduction to the single canopy or pavilion brief Review of relevant built precedents Definition of regenerative-material objectives Role of AI in transitioning from narrative intent to a controlled design system Block 2 - Building the Parametric System - Led by Fun Yuen: Live build of the workshop project in Grasshopper Parametric control over module dimensions, density, and curvature Integration of connections, material limits, and fabrication constraints Day 2: Robotic Toolpathing & Circular Workflow Block 3 - From Geometry to Robotic Toolpath - Led by Clinton Mendonca: Transitioning Grasshopper geometry into robotic fabrication Setting tolerances, print orientation, and componentisation Defining bead and layer logic, robotic toolpaths, and G-code Conducting production checks for reclaimed printing compounds Block 4 - Completing the Circular Workflow: Reassembling components into the complete canopy or pavilion system Testing assembly and disassembly logic Evaluating reprocessing and reprinting strategies Using AI-assisted visualization to present the design in context
source_fields.certificate_text: as congratulations on successfully completing our comprehensive online workshop. This course offered insights into essential tools of advanced architectural design software, enabling you to create captivating materials and efficiently render projects. Your dedication to mastering these sophisticated techniques is commendable.
source_fields.faq: Can I actually adapt these Grasshopper scripts for my own projects? :: Yes. You build the logic step-by-step from scratch so you walk away with a flexible workflow you can tweak for your own designs, not just locked files. || How does AI fit in without messing up the precise 3D geometry? :: AI is used strictly for quick visual concepting and setting final images in context. Your Grasshopper script maintains absolute control over exact measurements and print toolpaths. || Is learning robotic toolpathing useful if I don't own a robot? :: Definitely. Understanding layer heights, overhangs, and G-code logic changes how you design for any digital fabrication lab, even if you send files out to print. || Do we design for real-world material limits or theoretical geometry? :: Real limits. You’ll design around actual recycled compound constraints, factoring in print bed size, layer height, joint connections, and disassembly. || I only have basic Grasshopper experience. Will I be able to keep up? :: No. Basic navigation and a general understanding of how components connect is plenty. The modeling block builds the script sequentially so it is easy to follow.

courses.name: Monolithic Furniture: Large-Scale Additive Manufacturing

source_fields.name: Monolithic Furniture: Large-Scale Additive Manufacturing
source_fields.introduction: This workshop demonstrates integrated methods for leveraging computational design and large-scale additive manufacturing to translate digital furniture concepts into fabrication-ready physical structures. Participants will explore how manufacturing constraints can directly inform geometry, structure, material deposition, and ergonomic performance. Using a sculptural, monolithic chair as the primary case study, participants will reverse-engineer and recreate its continuous geometric system. They will subsequently learn how to develop seamless, single-shell forms and evaluate them according to overhang angles, layer heights, print orientation, wall thickness, and material behavior. Upon completing the course, attendees will gain far more than a recreation of a single furniture piece. They will develop the ability to construct and refine computational workflows for continuous furniture forms while preparing their designs for large-format additive manufacturing and robotic fabrication. Attendees will grasp the core geometric, structural, ergonomic, and fabrication constraints driving these processes, empowering them to innovate, test, and develop custom furniture strategies tailored to their own design intentions and specific manufacturing conditions. The objective is not merely to reproduce a pre-designed chair, but to develop the skills needed to formulate and advance manufacturing-driven computational design workflows autonomously, creating self-supporting furniture geometries that can progress toward slicing, toolpathing, and physical production.
source_fields.description: Furniture Design for Large-Scale Additive Manufacturing is an intermediate workshop that teaches designers to develop computational furniture systems and translate digital concepts into fabrication-ready 3D-printed structures. Participants use Rhino, Grasshopper, and large-scale additive manufacturing workflows to apply a model, refine, print, and fabricate approach controlling continuous geometry, structural integrity, ergonomics, and material limits, finishing with a personalized furniture proposal ready for slicing and robotic toolpathing.
source_fields.objectives: Reverse-engineer continuous geometry from a sculptural chair case study. Build computational workflows for continuous, single-shell furniture forms. Shape geometry around structural and ergonomic requirements. Design self-supporting ribs, folds, and curvatures. Account for overhangs, wall thickness, layer heights, and print orientation. Adapt furniture geometry to large-format additive manufacturing. Evaluate geometry for continuous robotic printing and toolpath logic. Develop a fabrication-ready digital furniture proposal for slicing and production.
source_fields.methodology: Participants will recreate and adapt a continuous, monolithic chair developed for large-scale additive manufacturing. The project will examine how computational geometry, structural logic, ergonomics, and fabrication constraints can be integrated into a single furniture design workflow. The project will progress through case study analysis, computational modelling, geometric refinement, fabrication assessment, and development of an individual furniture proposal. The fabrication focus will be large-scale 3D printing. Overhang angles, wall thickness, layer height, print orientation, material behaviour, self-supporting geometry, and continuous toolpath logic will inform the design and fabrication strategy. Students will: Analyse and recreate the reference chair using computational design. Develop continuous geometry with ergonomic and structural considerations. Integrate overhang, wall thickness, layer height, and print orientation constraints. Prepare self-supporting geometry for large-scale additive manufacturing and robotic toolpathing. Develop and present an individual fabrication-ready furniture proposal. Program Day 1: Case Study & Computational Furniture Design Introduction to large-scale additive manufacturing and the reference chair. Analysis of its continuous geometry, structural logic, ergonomics, and fabrication principles. Live recreation of the chair using computational design workflows. Development of individual geometry variations with ergonomic and structural considerations. Day 2: Fabrication Optimization & Final Proposal Refinement of furniture geometry based on overhang, wall thickness, layer height, and print orientation. Development of self-supporting geometry and continuous printing strategies. Preparation of geometry for slicing and robotic toolpathing. Final development, presentation, and review of individual furniture proposals.

courses.name: AI-Powered Design Exploration: From Ideation to Visualization

source_fields.name: AI-Powered Design Exploration: From Ideation to Visualization
source_fields.softwares: Adobe Photoshop | Kling AI | Midjourney | Nano Banana | Rhinoceros 3D
source_fields.introduction: The early stages of architectural design are often driven by exploration: studying references, testing ideas, generating alternatives, and deciding which possibilities are worth developing. While computational tools are highly effective once a design direction has been established, they are less suited to the loose and intuitive process of searching for that direction. Generative AI introduces a new approach by allowing architects to analyze references, combine architectural elements, and rapidly explore unexpected design variations. In this workshop, you will develop an AI-assisted workflow for both architectural ideation and visualization using Midjourney, Nano Banana Pro, and Kling. You will learn how to read buildings and objects as collections of physical elements rather than simply as stylistic references, extracting characteristics such as massing, openings, terraces, recesses, and structural conditions. These elements will then be translated into Midjourney prompts to generate and combine multiple design possibilities before critically selecting the strongest direction based on a defined design brief. Once a design direction has been established, the workflow shifts from exploration to visualization. Starting from a 3D model view , you will use Nano Banana Pro to create accurate architectural images while preserving the original massing, openings, and proportions. You will refine materials, lighting, camera conditions, people, and context, before using Kling to transform the approved visualization into a short architectural animation. By the end of the workshop, you will have developed a practical workflow for using AI at two distinct stages of the architectural process: generating and evaluating design possibilities, and communicating an established design through accurate still images and animation. The focus throughout remains on architectural judgment, selection, and authorship rather than simply generating more images.
source_fields.description: AI-Powered Design Exploration: From Ideation to Visualization is a 2-day AI-driven architectural design workshop where participants explore the complete workflow from early-stage ideation to accurate architectural visualization. The workshop covers precedent analysis, architectural element extraction, AI-generated mutation and variation, critical selection, Rhino-based visualization, material and lighting studies, contextual editing, and AI-assisted animation using Midjourney, Nano Banana Pro, and Kling.
source_fields.objectives: Ideation through inspiration, variation, selection, and refinement Architectural anatomy, precedent analysis, and multi-reference exploration Critical evaluation and selection of AI-generated design options AI workflows for ideation and visualization using Midjourney and Nano Banana Pro Controlled visualization studies for material, lighting, season, people, context, and camera Image-to-video workflows with Kling and the importance of selection over quantity
source_fields.methodology: In this workshop, we will focus on using AI as a practical tool across two distinct stages of the architectural design process: early-stage ideation and architectural visualization. The first part explores how Midjourney can be used to study references, extract architectural elements, generate unexpected mutations, and critically select design possibilities. The second part focuses on using Nano Banana Pro and Kling to develop accurate visualizations and short animations from an established 3D view. Throughout the workshop, you will learn to analyze buildings and objects through their physical characteristics rather than simply their style. These observations will be translated into prompts and combined across multiple references to generate a wide range of massing, façade, and spatial options. You will then evaluate the generated results against a design brief, identify the elements worth carrying forward, and select a clear design direction. Once a direction has been established, the workflow shifts from exploration to visualization. Starting from a 3D model view, you will use Nano Banana Pro to develop accurate architectural images while maintaining the original massing, openings, and proportions. You will explore controlled changes to material, lighting, camera, people, and context, before using Kling to turn the approved still into a short architectural animation. The workshop is intended for architects, designers, and students interested in incorporating generative AI into architectural design and visualization workflows. Participants should have a basic understanding of architectural design and visual communication. Scope: The workshop will combine theoretical explanations, demonstrations, and practical exercises across two complementary workflows. Each part will begin by introducing a specific design problem and the role of AI in addressing it. The first chapter will establish a methodology for AI-assisted ideation. Participants will study selected buildings and objects, identify their architectural anatomy, and translate physical elements into prompts. These will be used to generate variations through single-source and multi-reference workflows in Midjourney. The generated options will then be critically evaluated against the project brief. Rather than focusing on image quantity, the process emphasizes identifying what makes a particular option successful and clearly articulating which elements should be carried forward. The second chapter will focus on visualization rather than design generation. Participants will begin with a 3D model view and use Nano Banana Pro to produce an accurate architectural image. The original massing, openings, and proportions will remain fixed while material, lighting, camera, people, and context are refined. The approved image will then be developed into a short animation using Kling. Program: Day 1: Midjourney - Ideation, Mutation & Selection Analyze architectural references and objects through physical elements and architectural anatomy. Extract massing, openings, materiality, recesses, terraces, and other key characteristics. Translate observations into Midjourney prompts. Generate design variations using single-source and multi-reference workflows. Explore unexpected massing, façade, and spatial possibilities. Evaluate generated options against a design brief. Select one design direction and identify the elements carried forward. Day 2: Nano Banana Pro & Kling - Visualization & Animation Start from a 3D model view as the visualization base. Generate accurate architectural images while preserving massing, openings, and proportions. Explore material, lighting, season, camera, people, and contextual changes. Develop controlled image-editing instructions without altering the underlying structure. Refine and approve a final architectural visualization. Transform the approved still into a short animation using Kling. Explore approach, orbit, interior movement, or light-change sequences while maintaining the same design.
